REDACTED
REDACTED
The respective contracts for electric service are provided as trade secret STF-JKA-1-2 Attachments A through C. 


===== DKT 56002 & 56003 STF-JKA-1 PD/STF-JKA-1-20.docx =====
STF-JKA-1-20
Question: 
Regarding the Company’s retirement analysis:
Please compare and contrast the coal retirement methodology used in the 2025 IRP versus the 2022 IRP.
Did the Company evaluate the most optimal year to retire coal units in the coal retirement study? Provide all workpapers, notes, documentation regarding the assumptions required to evaluate optimal timing.
Response: 
The methodology used in the 2022 IRP and the 2025 IRP both compare the incremental costs and benefits of the unit being evaluated to the costs and benefits of replacement unit(s). The costs for the replacement unit in the 2022 IRP were assumed to be results from the 2,356 MW of low-cost replacement capacity identified in the 2022-2028 Capacity RFP, which was intended for the replacement of coal unit retirements. The replacement capacity cost assumption used in the 2025 IRP was assumed to be a generic natural gas combined cycle “NGCC.” The methodology used in the 2022 IRP assigned a capacity value to the unit being evaluated and to the replacement unit in order to make a direct comparison. Due to various environmental compliance pathways, the 2025 IRP methodology shifted to a total cost view so that more than one compliance pathway could be evaluated for each resource. When evaluating total costs, a capacity benefit is not assigned. Instead, capacity costs are assigned when the unit is assumed to retire.  
No, the Company did not evaluate the most optimal retirement year. The Company evaluated costs and benefits of continuing to operate coal units beyond 2028, including assessing the potential impact of various environmental compliance pathways, and is not requesting a retirement date in this IRP.

Overview:

Fixed capital may be defined as the total cost of processing installations, buildings, auxiliary services, and engineering involved in the creation of a new plant. Capital
must be allocated for direct plant expenses, such as those for raw materials, labor, and equipment.

The capital needed to supply the necessary manufacturing and plant facilities is called the fixed capital investment, while that necessary for the initial operation of the
plant is termed the working capital (funds required before creating a final end product available for sale). The sum of the fixed-capital investment and the working capital
is known as the total capital investment.

This Cost Estimate will include the Fixed Capital Investment based on the equipment proposed. Working Capital estimate not applicable.
Internal factors such as cost of capital, AFUDC, escalation, contingency, corporate overhead, and allocated funds are excluded and should be applied using the
corporate factors in place at the time of the estimate.

(B) Adjustment for Equipment Sizing by Ratio and Proportion Estimating:

A ratio indicates the relationship between two (or more) items in quantity, amount, or size.
Proportion implies that the two (or more) items are similar, differing only in magnitude.
When preparing these preliminary estimates, equipment costs can be scaled by the Rule of Six-Tenths.
Approximate costs can be obtained if the cost of a similar item of different size or capacity is known.

(C) Adjustment of Estimate Based on Historical Cost Indices

Cost Indices are useful when basing the estimated costs of a project on other than current prices.

Choice of the Cost Index to apply is at the discretion of the estimating engineer.
Several indices may include:

  - Engineering News Record (ENR),

  - Marshall and Swift Equipment Cost Index (M&S)

Calculation Summary (ZLD Portion)
Reference Plant Description
     Process Estimate is for equipment and treatment as required by the Supplemental Effluent Limitations Guidelines and Standards for the Steam
     Electric Power Generating Point Source Category (40CFR Part 423). One portion of this treatment system requires Zero Liquid Discharge for
     Combustion Residual Leachate while a second portion requires treatment for Arsenic and Mercury removal for a waste stream classified as
     uncontrolled leachate.

     For the Zero Liquid Discharge Stream, the Reference Plant is a Thermal Evaporator/Crystallizer Unit (Mechanical Vapor Recompression) proposed for
     treatment of Softened Reverse Osmosis Brine produced from the FGD Process at Plant Scherer. Thermal Energy is supplied by Electric Heaters and
     Mechanical Components since no waste heat or natural gas is available at the site. The Process includes both liquid evaporation and solids handling
     steps which lend to the use of the mid-range Lang Factor for Total Installed Costs. Select vendors offer modularized and prepackaged units that may
     afford some cost reductions (i.e. smaller Lang Factor 1.7 Reported) (to be addressed by more detailed project estimates).

Calculation Summary (Uncontrolled CRL Portion)
Reference Plant Description
     Process Estimate is for equipment and treatment as required by the Supplemental Effluent Limitations Guidelines and Standards for the Steam Electric
     Power Generating Point Source Category (40CFR Part 423). One portion of this treatment system requires Zero Liquid Discharge for Combustion
     Residual Leachate while a second portion requires treatment for Arsenic and Mercury removal for a waste stream classified as uncontrolled leachate.

     For the Uncontrolled Leachate portion, physical/chemical processes and adsorptive treatment processes are available to meet Arsenic and Mercury
     removal rates specified in the ELG Rule. During Ash Pond Closure, this CRL is returned to the Ash Pond to be treated by the temporary Wastewater
     Treatment System currently installed. This portion of the estimate would apply to installation of a new treatment system, if desired, that allows a smaller
     flowrate - once the ash pond dewatering system is no longer required.

     The Reference Plant is based on Adsorption Treatment Vessels (Qty = 4) operated in series. First set captures mercury and the second set captures
     arsenic. The permeate from this system will be sent to discharge or reuse. The media, once saturated with the arsenic and mercury captured, will be
     discarded to landfill and replaced with fresh media. The adsorptive technology was selected due to high modularity and standardization of the design
     (which allows significant future reduction of the Lang Factor for Total Installed Cost estimation.

Response:

The technology screening process is detailed in the 2025 IRP filing in Technical Appendix Volume 2, Technology Screening & Application Standards TRADE SECRET. Note that RICE is retained in the technology screening process but is not included in the Resource Mix Study. While RICE units have similar performance characteristics to CT w SCR, these units have substantially higher capital cost and are not expected to be selected over CT w SCR. Supercritical CO2, which is also retained in the screening process for generic resources, is assumed to be represented by CC w CCS in the Aurora analyses as indicated in the Technical Appendix Volume 2 Resource Mix Study. 
All capital expenditures and revenue requirements can be found in the SAM Files for Generics TRADE SECRET workpapers folder that was provided to Commission Staff on January 31, 2025, for Technical Appendix Volume 2 Resource Mix Study. Declining revenue requirements from the SAM files are inputs to STF-JKA-1-22 Attachment A TRADE SECRET and STF-JKA-1-22 Attachment B TRADE SECRET.  Outputs from STF-JKA-1-22 Attachments A & B are input to the Resource Mix Study workpaper titled “TAS to Aurora - FinalB25 TRADE SECRET.xlsx” to prepare the data for input to Aurora.

Capital costs include land costs and the cost for 2 miles of Transmission Line to a substation. AFUDC and associated financing costs are included in the financial analysis that supports the Resource Mix Study as provided in the SAM Files referenced in part b. 
The revenue requirements for the generic resources were developed using the Standard Analysis Model (SAM), a tool the Company has developed to analyze financial impacts of potential and existing assets.  Transmission upgrades are not studied for generic resources, as the cost of resulting transmission interconnection and upgrade costs is only available after a lengthy interconnection study process which is sensitive to timelines and siting. SAM models are provided as stated in part b above, and natural gas firm transportation (“FT”) and fuel assumptions are provided in STK-JKA-1-22 Attachment H TRADE SECRET. 
Useful lives of all generic resources were provided in the initial filing in Technical Appendix Vol 2 Technology Screening & Application Standards.

Heat rates and outputs were developed using the Thermoflow suite of modeling software incorporating OEM performance data. The output shown in STF-JKA-1-22 Attachment I TRADE SECRET is derived from that software suite. 
STF-JKA-1-22 Attachment J TRADE SECRET presents a sample round-trip efficiency (“RTE”) calculation for the 4-hour battery energy storage system represented in Aurora.  Efficiency for medium duration energy storage was based on OEM specifications.

Generic solar PV resources are modeled as described in Technical Appendix Vol. 2 Resource Mix Study, sections 3.6.1 and 3.6.2.  Table 5 provides the associated costs used in the model.  Generic Solar PV is modeled in Aurora as 300 MW blocks, all having identical operating characteristics.

See STF-JKA-1-11 TRADE SECRET for discussion of differences between the 2023 IRP Update and the 2025 IRP.  
 

===== DKT 56002 & 56003 STF-JKA-1 PD/STF-JKA-1-23.docx =====
STF-JKA-1-23
Question: 
Regarding generic Small Modular Reactor Technology resource options.
a. Has Georgia Power assumed generic resource options related to nuclear and/or small modular reactor (SMR) technologies? What studies have been conducted to support the development of this resource?
b. Provide all supporting documentation and industry information regarding costs, risks, and availability of nuclear/SMR resources in Georgia.
c. Did Georgia Power consider any federal incentives for investment in screening this technology in or out of consideration? Explain why or why not.
Response: 
a.Yes, the Company included SMR as a generic nuclear candidate unit in the 2023 IRP Update.  In preparation for this 2025 IRP, the projected costs for SMR increased significantly from the 2023 IRP Update resulting in the AP1000 nuclear technology projected to be the most cost-effective nuclear option.  Therefore, in this 2025 IRP, the generic nuclear candidate unit is based on cost and performance information for the AP1000 nuclear technology.  Cost and performance metrics for the AP1000 are informed from previous nuclear resource development in which the Company has been involved. SMR costs are informed by recent updated pricing available from OEMs, with operations and maintenance characteristics informed by experience with nuclear operation.
b. Please see Attachments B and C in 2025 IRP Technology Screening TRADE SECRET located in 2025 IRP Technical Appendix Volume 2.
c.Yes, Investment Tax Credits at 30% were applied, in line with guidance from the clean energy credit made available through the IRA. See the Technical Appendix Volume 2, Resource Mix Study for additional discussion of generic resource technologies.

                         SCHEDULE OF DEFINED TERMS AND RULES OF CONSTRUCTION

         This All-Source RFP uses the defined terms identified in this Schedule, or in the body of this All-Source
         RFP, and the rules of construction identified in this Schedule.
         2022 IRP: GPC’s 2022 Integrated Resource Plan as approved by the Commission in Docket No. 44160.
         2022 IRP Final Order: The Order from the 2022 IRP as approved by the Commission in Docket No. 44160.
         AC: Alternating current.
         Access Route: The suitable all-weather access route from the nearest public roadway to the Point of
         Interconnection that is acceptable to GPC and that must be always available to GPC (24/7/365(366))
         throughout the IA term to facilitate GPC’s construction, operation, or maintenance of the Interconnection
         Facilities or other related GPC activity.
         Affected System: An Electric System utility other than the Southern Company Transmission System or an
         electric facility owner whose facilities require additions, modifications, or upgrades that are necessary for safe
         and reliable operation of the Electric System during parallel operation of the Facility, other than those required
         due to GPC’s designation of the Facility output to serve GPC’s customers (i.e., to deliver the energy from the
         Point of Delivery to GPC’s customers).
         Affected System Upgrade(s): Any addition, modification, or upgrade to an Affected System’s Electric System
         that would be necessary for safe and reliable operation of the Electric System during parallel operation of the
         Facility. Each addition, modification, or upgrade will be constructed and owned by that Affected System.
         Affiliate: For any specific Person, any other Person directly or indirectly controlling, controlled by, or under
         common control with that Person. For purposes of this definition, “control” when used regarding any entity
         means the power to direct the management and policies of the entity, directly or indirectly, whether through
         the ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise. A Person directly or indirectly owning 50% or
         more of the outstanding stock or other equity interest of another Person has “control” of that Person. The terms
         “controlling” and “controlled” have meanings correlative to “control.”
         Affiliate Bid Team: As defined in Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(d), any GPC Affiliate that intends to submit
         a Bid into this All-Source RFP, as well as any other Persons acting for that Affiliate or on its behalf in support
         of the development and submission of any Bid.
         AGC: See Automatic Generation Control.
         AIER: See Associated Interchange Energy Rate.
         All-Source RFP: This All-Source Capacity Request for Proposals for 2029–2031.
         Alternative Bid: Defined in Section 7.4.1 (Alternative Bid).
         Alternate Resource: A generating resource, other than the Facility, that: (i) is connected to the Southern
         Company Transmission System, either directly or through other transmission systems; (ii) can be called on a
         first-call basis by Seller; and (iii) is reasonably reliable to meet GPC’s schedule, as determined in GPC’s sole
         judgment and as further defined in the PPA.
         Ancillary Services: All commercial products other than electrical output that are produced by or related to the
         Facility, including Electrical Products, Environmental Attributes, any other environmental or regulatory credits,
         or allowances resulting from operation of the Facility, and any other benefit GPC otherwise would have realized
         from or related to the Facility if GPC rather than Seller had constructed, owned, or operated the Facility, it
         being the Parties’ intent that all the benefits and entitlements in addition to electrical output that flow to the
         owner or operator of the Facility, whether existing as of the Effective Date or at any time during the PPA Term
         or Facility Design Life, belong to GPC at no additional cost to GPC. However, if a commercial product is not
         produced by the Facility, Seller will not be required to acquire the commercial product in the market to comply
         with the Awarded Contract. Ancillary Services do not include: (i) any federal, state, or local tax attributes arising
         from the ownership of the Facility, including investment tax credits (ITC), production tax credits (PTC), or
         depreciation deductions; (ii) grants instead of ITC or any similar financial payment or grant regarding the
         Facility or the metered electric energy output from the Facility; or (iii) the metered electric energy produced by
         the Facility.

         Rules of Construction:

         In this All-Source RFP: (i) whenever the term “include,” “including,” “e.g.,” or “i.e.” is used, in connection with

         (e.g., “include” means “include, but is not limited to”; “including” means “including, without limitation”); and
         (ii) “or” means either or both (i.e., “A or B” means “A or B or both A and B”).

         Unless otherwise specified, reference to: (a) a Party or Person includes any allowed successor or assign; (b) a
         Governmental Authority includes any authority succeeding to the same function; (c) an agreement or document
         includes any exhibit, attachment, appendix, or schedule; and (d) an applicable law, agreement, document,
         policy, procedure, standard, or provision is to the law, agreement, document, policy, procedure, standard, or
         provision as modified, amended, supplemented, or restated, and then-effective or current.

         A defined term may be singular or plural, as the context requires. Captions are for convenience only and do
         not affect interpretation.

                                  All-Source Capacity Request for Proposals
                                                for 2029-2031

         Georgia Power Company’s 2022 IRP identified a need for additional Capacity Resources. On July 21, 2022,
         the Commission issued the 2022 IRP Final Order concerning the 2022 IRP. The 2022 IRP Final Order
         amended and approved the Stipulation that requires GPC to conduct an all-source solicitation to address
         capacity needs identified by GPC.

         GPC estimates that up to 8,500 MW of Capacity Resources are necessary to satisfy GPC’s capacity needs,
         as reflected in the table below. This estimate is based on expiration of capacity power purchase agreements,
         potential retirement of certain GPC generation units, and projected load growth. Final capacity needs, including
         the period when capacity is needed, are contingent upon GPC’s decisions regarding retirement and load
         growth and will be subject to Commission review and approval.

         GPC issues this All-Source RFP to procure Capacity Resources that meet GPC’s identified capacity needs,
         including: (i) Standalone ESS with grid charging capability; (ii) ESS with Renewable Resource and grid
         charging capability; and (iii) thermal generation (e.g., natural gas or oil-fired).

         GPC may revise its capacity need forecast to reduce, eliminate, or increase the amount of capacity and energy
         sought, or, in consultation with the Staff and IE, change the Solicitation Schedule at any point during the RFP
         process. Further, the RFP Documents are subject to modification or withdrawal at any time in the sole discretion
         of GPC.

                                                                   2023 IRP Update (MW)
                                    2028/2029                              2,280
                                    2029/2030                              3,247
                                    2030/2031                              5,960

              1.2.   Independent Evaluator.
                     1.2.1. Purpose and Role of IE. GPC is utilizing the IE to oversee this All-Source RFP and to
                     serve as the point of contact for all Participants. As provided in the RFP Rule, the IE serves to
                     maintain fairness, transparency, and consistency in the RFP Process, which helps to prevent
                     claims of favoritism in the evaluation and advancement of Submissions. Commission Rules
                     require GPC to retain an IE, who is selected by and reports to the Commission in carrying out its
                     duties and assisting with development of this All-Source RFP and evaluation of Submissions.

                     1.2.2. The IE Website. The IE Website serves as the required forum for all RFP communication
                     among the Evaluation Team, Participants, and all interested Persons. Any Participant or
                     interested Person may only communicate with GPC, the IE, or Staff regarding this All-Source RFP
                     through the IE Website. If any Participant or interested Person directs questions regarding any
                     RFP information to Staff or GPC, as applicable, will direct the Participant or interested Person to
                     the IE Website to ensure all communications are documented and treated consistently, fairly, and
                     transparently. If a Participant attempts to make contact outside the process described in this All-
                     Source RFP, Participant will be directed to the IE Website for all information and communication
                     and will be reported to the IE for a violation of this All-Source RFP requirement. Repeated violation
                     of this requirement may result in the Bidder being prohibited from participating and all Bids from
                     the Bidder being disqualified.

              1.3.   Standards of Conduct.

                     response to this All-Source RFP. Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(d) incorporates measures to
                     segregate the Evaluation Team and any Affiliate Bid Team. The lists identifying the Evaluation

                          conduct or communication regarding the development of any Company-Owned Proposal by
                          the COP Team that would unfairly influence the design or evaluation processes for this All-
                          Source RFP.
                          C.       Company-Owned Proposal Team and Specialized Technical Support
                          Personnel. The COP Team will develop any Company-Owned Proposal in a manner that
                          preserves the integrity and fairness of the RFP Process for all Participants. Due to their
                          functional expertise and breadth of job responsibilities, two Specialized Technical Support
                          Personnel in the SCS Treasury Department will be involved both with development of a
                          Company-Owned Proposal and with certain aspects of this All-Source RFP. The RFP
                          information provided to Specialized Technical Support Personnel is limited to the scope of
                          their job responsibilities. Specialized Technical Support Personnel serving as members of
                          both the Evaluation Team and the COP Team will not be allowed to determine the total
                          economic benefit of Submissions. GPC voluntarily posted a list of the COP Team members
                          on the IE Website, and the Evaluation Team and the COP Team lists will separately identify
                          any Specialized Technical Support Personnel who serve on both teams. GPC will not
                          substitute any Specialized Technical Support without first consulting Staff and the IE.

                     can commence delivery in the Winter 2029 – Winter 2031 timeframe (December 2028 –
                     December 2030). Participant may propose a Capacity Resource that is available earlier than
                     Winter 2029, but no earlier than January 1, 2026, and GPC will determine if the proposed option
                     is an economical option that meets customer needs. A Submission may offer any reliable energy

                     including but not limited to: (i) Standalone ESS with grid charge capability and a minimum duration

                     2.1.1. Other Technology. If Bidder desires to submit a Bid comprised of equipment utilizing
                     other technology that is not described in Section 2.1 (Products Sought), including any demand-

                     Schedule. Upon request, Bidder must provide information to the IE regarding the Other

                     discussions, the IE will advise Bidder whether a Bid utilizing Bidder’s proposed Other Technology
                     will be accepted as a Bid that meets the requirements of this All-Source RFP. GPC will not
                     consider for this All-Source RFP non-dispatchable technologies, including: (i) third-party
                     aggregators; or (ii) other demand response options that do not: (a) meet the minimum Facility
                     Size parameters described in Section 3.2.1 (Facility Size Parameters) at each Site; or (b) allow
                     firm control of the demand response technology and associated infrastructure solely by GPC via
                     AGC.

              2.2.   Facility Ownership Structures. Under this All-Source RFP, Bidders may submit Bids proposing
                     one of two ownership structures for Facilities:
                     2.2.1. Seller-Owned Facilities. GPC will accept Bids for Facilities where Seller will retain
                     Facility ownership. The Awarded Contract that a Winning Bidder would execute would be a PPA,
                     where GPC would have exclusive rights to the Facility’s capacity.

                     2.2.2. GPC-Owned Facilities. GPC will accept Bids for Facilities comprising Capacity
                     Resources where Bidder proposes to transfer to GPC Facility ownership. The Awarded Contract
                     that a Winning Bidder would execute with GPC would be an APA or a BTA.

                          A.       Consideration of APA/BTA Bids. GPC will consider APA and BTA Bids for
                          Capacity Resources that can interconnect to the STT. A BTA Bid must offer a Capacity
                          Resource to be located in the state of Georgia and 100% ownership of that Capacity
                          Resource. GPC will consider offers for partial ownership of or partial unit(s) of an Existing
                          Resource that is a CC or CT. GPC will not consider offers for partial ownership of or partial
                          unit(s) of a New Resource.
                          B.      APA/BTA Bid Requirements. A Bidder offering an APA/BTA Bid must submit the
                          same forms as a PPA Bidder, but an APA/BTA Bidder must also complete additional
                          questions, including the questions on the questionnaire found in Exhibit C (Additional Bid
                          Information and Questionnaire), which indicates the information GPC must receive to
                          perform necessary due diligence.
                          C.      APA/BTA Bid Evaluation. APA/BTA Bids will be evaluated alongside PPA Bids and
                          Company-Owned Proposal(s). If an APA/BTA Bid advances to the Conforming List, the
                          evaluation of the APA/BTA Bid requires additional due diligence.
                          D.      Generating Resource and Business Entity Purchase. If an APA Bid makes the
                          Short List of competitive Submissions, and even though GPC is likely only interested in the
                          purchase of the Facility itself, GPC may also consider purchasing the business entity that
                          owns the Existing Resource, subject to reaching acceptable terms and conditions. GPC may
                          ask the APA Bidder to submit an offer allowing GPC to purchase the business entity that
                          holds the Existing Resource. If the APA Bidder chooses to offer the business entity for
                          purchase, GPC will have the right to proceed with the purchase of either the Existing
                          Resource or the Existing Resource together with the business entity. GPC will not consider
                          APA Bids for business entities unless the APA Bid for the Existing Resource advances to
                          the Short List.

              2.3.   Bids for Existing Resources or New Resources. Under this All-Source RFP, Bidders may

                             (i). An Existing Resource would be in the form of either an APA or pro forma PPA,
                             depending on whether GPC or Seller would be the ultimate owner of the Existing

                             (ii). A New Resource that has not been constructed, but that would ultimately be owned
                             by GPC, would be in the form of a BTA; or
                             (iii). A New Resource that has not yet been constructed, but that would ultimately be
                             owned by Seller, would be a PPA in the form of one of the pro forma PPAs.
              2.4.   ESS Submissions. GPC will consider an ESS resource structured as: (i) Standalone ESS with
                     grid charging capability; or (ii) ESS with Renewable Resource, with grid charging capability. In
                     addition to the subsections that immediately follow, the pro forma ESS with Renewable Resource
                     PPA, pro forma ESS PPA, and the additional guidance for ESS Submissions in Exhibit L
                     (Additional Guidance for ESS Submissions) provide the parameters for the acceptable and
                     applicable use of an ESS in this All-Source RFP. GPC’s evaluation of an ESS Submission in this
                     RFP will be appropriately focused upon the capacity use of the ESS, which is to ensure system
                     reliability.

                     2.4.1. Degradation. GPC is not responsible for any degradation of any Facility over the Term,
                     whether because of GPC scheduling, charging, or discharging of energy. As set forth in pro forma
                     Standalone ESS PPA and pro forma ESS with Renewable Resource PPA, and as applicable to
                     all generating types, the ESS is subject to monthly and annual performance metrics and must
                     maintain the guaranteed Storage Device Design Capacity and guaranteed Storage Device
                     Discharge Duration for the PPA Term.

                     2.4.2. Operating Policy. Any Participant offering an ESS Submission must be familiar with, and
                     will be expected to comply with, Southern Company Transmission’s Operating Policy for Inverter-
                     Based Electric Storage Resources Interconnecting to the Southern Companies’ Transmission
                     System, as appropriate, which may be found at: https://www.oasis.oati.com/woa/docs/SOCO/SOCOdocs/Inverter-
                     Based_Electric_Storage_Operating_Policy.pdf.

                     2.4.3. Standalone ESS. A Participant offering a Standalone ESS must provide: (i) a description
                     of the ESS; (ii) if offering a PPA, the plan to maintain the ESS to ensure the ESS performs as
                     evaluated for the PPA Term; (iii) the guaranteed Storage Device Design Capacity (AC); (iv) an
                     annual schedule of the guaranteed Round-Trip Efficiency for the PPA Term or Facility Design Life,
                     as applicable; and (v) any other information required by the Bid form. GPC must have the
                     exclusive right, without penalty, to discharge and charge the ESS by dispatching it in accordance
                     with Section 3.5.1 (AGC). To ensure GPC can toll the energy, a Standalone ESS must be
                     interconnected to, and solely charged from, the STT. GPC will provide (toll) all energy required to
                     charge a Standalone ESS, but Seller will be solely responsible for Station Service.
                     2.4.4. ESS with Renewable Resource. In addition to the information required by Section 2.4.3
                     (Standalone ESS), an ESS with Renewable Resource Submission must also include: (i) a
                     description of the Renewable Resource (including the generation type of the Renewable
                     Resource (e.g., solar panels, wind turbines)); (ii) the total expected capacity (AC) from the
                     Renewable Resource; and (iii) a Profile reflecting the Renewable Resource, to demonstrate the
                     charging contribution of the Renewable Resource for the ESS.

                     2.4.5. Additional ESS Guidance. Critical guidance concerning the required parameters for an
                     ESS Facility charging from the Renewable Resource (as applicable), grid charging, and
                     deliverability parameters, are outlined in Exhibit L (Additional Guidance for ESS Submissions).

                     KEY PROJECT REQUIREMENTS

              3.1.   PPA Term, Facility Design Life, RCOD, and RCD.
                     3.1.1. PPA Term and Facility Design Life. GPC will consider Bids for: (i) PPAs with a PPA
                     Term of 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, or 30 Annual Periods, at Bidder’s option; (ii) APAs for Facilities with a
                     Facility Design Life of at least 10 years; and (iii) BTAs with a Facility Design Life appropriate with
                     the technology type and consistent with Prudent Industry Practices. GPC will evaluate Bids under
                     the methodology outlined in Exhibit H (Overview of Evaluation Methodology).

                     3.1.2. RCOD and RCD. Under the 2022 IRP Final Order, GPC seeks Capacity Resources with
                     in-service dates in or before 2030. Each Bidder must indicate the RCOD or RCD, as applicable,
                     in its Bid, and the date must be in accordance with the Solicitation Schedule. GPC may decline
                     to enter into a PPA, APA, or BTA with any Bidder if, in the opinion of GPC, in consultation with the
                     IE and Staff, the transmission facilities cannot be constructed in time to achieve Commercial
                     Operation or Closing by the date set forth in the Solicitation Schedule. ESS Bidders must provide
                     a Profile(s) for each Bid that begins on the RCOD or the RCD, as applicable. Bidders may consult
                     the Southern Companies’ Seller Interconnection Business Practices document posted on OASIS
                     for information related to interconnection activity timeframes and limitations. If Seller fails to
                     achieve Commercial Operation or Closing by the RCOD or RCD, as applicable, Seller must pay
                     Delay Damages to GPC under the Awarded Contract. Delay Damages will be calculated in
                     accordance with the applicable Delay Damages table in Exhibit E (Summary of Fees, Costs,
                     Security, and Deadlines), Attachment 2 (Delay Liquidated Damages Summary).

              3.2.   Facility Size and Output.
                     3.2.1. Facility Size Parameters. Except for any QF participating in this All-Source RFP under
                     Part 9 (Qualifying Facilities) or an ESS as described in Section 3.2.1.A (ESS Submissions), a
                     proposed Facility must be at least 80 MW and not larger than 1,200 MW in size. If a Submission
                     offers multiple units located on the same Site, each unit may be sized less than 80 MW so long
                     as, when combined, the minimum Facility size is at least 80 MW and all units deliver to the same
                     Point of Delivery. A Participant cannot offer multiple units to be located on different Sites. If
                     Participant offers multiple units in a single Submission, the Submission must indicate the size of
                     each unit and whether each unit may advance separately at the pricing stated in the Submission,
                     including the dollar per kilowatt ($/kW) annual capacity price stated in the Submission. The
                     Submission must clearly state if units can or cannot advance separately or in combinations. If
                     Participant desires to offer different pricing for different unit combinations, the Submission must
                     specifically identify this pricing.

                          A.       ESS Submissions. A proposed ESS must have a Storage Device Design Capacity
                          of at least 80 MW at the POI and a minimum Storage Device Discharge Duration of at least
                          four hours. The Storage Device Design Capacity must be no more than 500 MW at the POI.
                          An evaluated capacity contribution will be assigned to each configuration. An ESS must have
                          grid charging capability.
                     3.2.2.    Partial Output Bids.

                          A.       Existing Resources.
                               (i). CC/CT: For an Existing Resource that is a CC or CT, GPC will consider Bids that
                               offer less than 100% entitlement to the full output capability of the Capacity Resource
                               (PPA) or partial ownership of the Capacity Resource (APA Bids).
                               (ii). ESS: Each ESS PPA and APA Bid must offer 100% entitlement to the full output
                               capability of the Capacity Resource.
                          B.       New Resources. For a New Resource, each Bid must offer full ownership (BTA
                          Bids) or 100% entitlement to the full output capability (PPA Bids) of the Capacity Resource.

                     3.2.3. GPC Consent Required for Facility Changes. A Winning Bidder must obtain GPC’s
                     written consent before making any material change to Facility design, performance, or output (as
                     specified in the Bid and considered by GPC in Bid evaluation).

              3.3.   Location of Facilities.
                     3.3.1. Facility Location. GPC will accept Submissions for a Facility located within the STT, so
                     long as the Facility (i) can deliver energy to GPC in accordance with one of the interconnection
                     options set forth in Exhibit B (Interconnection and Delivery Requirements); and (ii) if offered as a
                     BTA Bid, is located in the State of Georgia. Except for ESS PPA Bids, GPC will also accept PPA
                     Bids to deliver energy and capacity from a Facility located outside of the STT, so long as the
                     Facility can deliver energy to a Southern Transmission Interface and otherwise meets RFP
                     requirements, including AGC. A Bidder may not submit a Bid that locates the Facility on GPC
                     property. Only a Company-Owned Proposal may propose a Facility on GPC property.

                          A.       ESS with Renewable Resource Location. Any Renewable Resource included as
                          part of an ESS Submission must interconnect to the same POI as the ESS.
              3.4.   Transmission Interconnection. Each Bidder is responsible for determining all transmission
                     interconnection and delivery-related rules, practices, and policies with which it must comply, as
                     further detailed in Exhibit B (Interconnection and Delivery Requirements). Each Bid must comply
                     with one of the interconnection options identified in Exhibit B (Interconnection and Delivery
                     Requirements).
                     3.4.1. New Resources. Each Participant proposing a New Resource must propose a discrete
                     POI for its Facility. The proposed POI must be consistent with the expected point of electrical
                     interconnection that would be established if Participant were currently applying for
                     interconnection. GPC (through the IE) may suggest a different POI (regarding location or voltage)
                     if it would result in more favorable economic consideration of the Submission. Participant will be
                     responsible for all equipment necessary to interconnect the Facility to the Interconnection
                     Facilities at the POI. All transmission facilities beyond the proposed POI (into the network
                     transmission grid) will be owned by the Transmission Service Provider.
              3.5.   Dispatchability. Capacity Resources offered in this All-Source RFP must be fully dispatchable
                     and available to meet GPC’s scheduling instructions for the PPA Term or Facility Design Life, as
                     applicable, which means the Facility can flexibly adjust its output in response to GPC’s scheduling
                     instructions, subject to any technical limit or other requirement stated in the Awarded Contract.
                     Preference may be given to Submissions that offer shorter unit commitment notification and
                     greater scheduling flexibility.

                     3.5.1. AGC. Because of their expected use and cost-effectiveness, each Capacity Resource
                     offered through a Bid for full output of the Capacity Resource must be capable of operating on
                     Automatic Generation Control, including any Renewable Resource offered as part of an ESS
                     Submission. Seller will be responsible for conforming to GPC’s requirements to integrate AGC
                     functionality and for all costs to make the Facility respond to GPC’s AGC signals. GPC will have
                     the right, but not the obligation, to dispatch the Facility in the AGC mode. Each Bid must include
                     the cost of the operation in its pricing. For PPA Bids involving Facilities that are not connected to
                     the STT, Bidders should verify dynamic transfer capability and protocols with the Southern
                     Company Transmission System to ensure proper telemetry communications in accordance with
                     the Southern OATT.

              3.6.   Availability. GPC will rely, in part, on the contracted capacity and energy supplied under a PPA
                     to provide dependable and reliable electric service to meet the needs of its customers.
                     Accordingly, GPC will require stringent protection for GPC and its customers against failures by
                     the Seller to deliver Contracted Capacity and energy in accordance with the PPA.
                     3.6.1. Guaranteed Availability. Any PPA will contain provisions that require Seller to forfeit a
                     portion of the capacity payment for Facility availability below 96% (calculated on a seasonal or
                     monthly basis, as the case may be). After taking scheduled maintenance outages and Alternate
                     Resource delivery into account, availability during any monthly period that is below 75% will result
         ALL-SOURCE RFP                                                                                     Page 24 of 115

                     in a 100% forfeiture of the monthly capacity payment. Bidder may review the applicable pro forma
                     PPA for more information regarding the availability calculation and adjustments to the capacity
                     payment (which may be determined by replacement costs). In addition, a PPA Event of Default
                     will occur if the availability remains below 60% for a certain extended period as specified in the
                     PPA.

              3.7.   Multiple Modes of Operation. For a PPA Bid offering a Facility with multiple modes of operation,
                     Bidder must specify the guaranteed nominal capacity of each mode and quote a single capacity
                     Bid price for the entire output of the Facility. If during any Annual Period the capacities designated
                     by mode are different from their respective guaranteed nominal capabilities by mode, an
                     adjustment to the capacity payment will be made in a manner that reflects the value of each mode
                     to GPC. The adjustment is described, for example, in Exhibit B (Capacity; Capacity Payments
                     and Payment Reductions; Buydown) of the pro forma CC PPA. If during any Annual Period the
                     capacities designated by mode match their respective guaranteed nominal capabilities by mode,
                     the capacity payment will match the single capacity Bid price.

                     3.7.1. APA/BTA Bids. For an APA or BTA Bid with multiple modes of operation, a Bidder must
                     provide the expected nominal capacity output for each mode.

              3.8.   Firmness of Proposed Resources. To be considered responsive, a Submission must
                     demonstrate an appropriate level of firmness, which means the Facility must deliver capacity for
                     the duration of any period of guaranteed commitment in accordance with GPC’s scheduling
                     instructions, even under adverse conditions. GPC’s evaluation will assess the reliability and
                     economic value of limits indicated in the Submission. Each Submission must propose to provide
                     the proposed capacity and energy to GPC from specific, dedicated resource(s) on an
                     unencumbered, first-call basis and priority.

              3.9.   Demineralization. The use of demineralized water supply for a resource should not limit the
                     operations or delivery of capacity. CCs operating on natural gas should be able to support at least
                     14 hours of full load generation plus 10 hours of full pressure generation (24 hours of total
                     operation). Demineralized water intended for use in conjunction with fuel oil operation should match
                     the specified storage capacity for fuel oil in Section 3.10 (Fuel/Energy Plan). Bidder must also have
                     adequate demineralized water replenishment capabilities at the Facility.
              3.10. Fuel/Energy Plan. For evaluation purposes, GPC will develop an individual fuel plan for each CC
                    and CT Submission and a grid charging plan for any ESS Submission to reliably and economically
                    meet the fuel/energy supply requirements for those Submissions. The projected fuel/energy plans
                    will be developed in a consistent and fair manner for all Submissions.
                     3.10.1. Fuel Evaluation. Natural gas prices will be linked to a single monthly forecast of gas
                     prices at a common point (Henry Hub). Delivered gas prices will include applicable gas
                     transportation charges, fuel retention rates, historical basis differentials, and taxes. GPC will
                     evaluate fuel-related requirements, including the purchase of firm gas transportation and storage,
                     as follows.

                          A.        CT. GPC prefers that CTs have dual-fuel capability to burn natural gas and oil. Gas
                          storage will be evaluated consistent with other GPC CT units, and fuel oil inventory costs will
                          be applied as appropriate. The Submission must indicate the permitted hours of operation
                          and the maximum hours per year the Facility is permitted to run on fuel oil. The supporting
                          facilities (including infrastructure and property interests) and operation for onsite fuel oil
                          storage, if applicable, must comply with the following standards:
                             (i). CT Facilities with sufficient fuel oil backup will not require firm gas transportation
                             provided the oil can be burned year-round. If a CT Facility has sufficient fuel oil backup
                             but cannot burn oil in the summer months, then, for months with seasonal limitations on
                             oil, the Submission must include five to twelve hours firm transportation per Day on gas
                             depending on site limitations and unit heat rate.

                             (ii). For an existing CT Facility with dual-fuel capability, the Facility should include: (1)
                             sufficient fuel oil storage to operate the Facility for 24 continuous hours, without
                             replenishment, at full load; and (2) adequate replenishment capabilities.
                             (iii). For a new-build or transfer CT Facility with dual-fuel capability, the Facility must
                             include: (1) sufficient fuel oil storage capacity to operate the Facility for 72 continuous
                             hours, without replenishment, at full load; and (2) adequate replenishment capabilities.
                             (iv). Unless otherwise mutually agreed by GPC and Seller under a PPA, Seller will
                             acquire, permit, construct, own, operate, and maintain all facilities, infrastructure, auxiliary

                          B.      CC. Each CC Facility will be evaluated with sufficient firm gas transportation to allow
                          14 hours of operation at full load plus 10 hours operation at peaking or secondary modes of

                          permitted hours of operation.
                    3.10.2. Fuel Tolling for CC and CT PPA Bids. Each PPA Bidder offering a CT or CC Facility
                    must submit a firm fuel transportation proposal to confirm that the resource can meet the firmness
                    requirements of this RFP for the PPA Term, but Bidders are not required to have a firm fuel
                    transportation arrangement in effect at the time of Bid submission.
                          A.      Tolling. GPC requires a fuel tolling arrangement (i.e., an arrangement in which GPC
                          is responsible for fuel supply and transportation) for CC and CT Facilities for which the Bidder
                          does not have a pre-existing fuel transportation arrangement.
                          B.      Preexisting Fuel Arrangements. Regarding resources for which the Bidder has a
                          pre-existing fuel transportation arrangement, GPC prefers a fuel tolling arrangement with
                          assignment/release of the pre-existing fuel transportation arrangement. If a fuel tolling
                          arrangement with assignment/release of the pre-existing fuel transportation arrangement is
                          proposed, this will be factored into the evaluation. Bidder must provide specific data
                          regarding the costs and rates that will be assigned/released in accordance with the fuel
                          transportation arrangement as a Bid term.
                          C.       GPC Delivery of Gas. GPC will be responsible for delivering to the agreed-upon
                          gas delivery point sufficient quantities of natural gas to generate energy in accordance with
                          GPC’s energy schedules. GPC will bear the risk of loss of natural gas until it is delivered to
                          the delivery point. The party responsible for causing any imbalance will be responsible for
                          payment of any imbalance charges assessed by the pipeline operator.
                    3.10.3. Charging Plan for ESS Bids. GPC requires each ESS to connect to the Southern
                    Company Transmission System and for each ESS PPA to contain an energy tolling provision for
                    grid charging. In addition to grid charging, an ESS with Renewable Resource is expected to be
                    appropriately sized to allow the Renewable Resource to be the primary source of charging for the
                    ESS. Additional charging details are listed in Exhibit L (Additional Guidance for ESS
                    Submissions).

                    commensurate reduction in the calculated availability of the Facility, an Awarded Contract will
                    contain provisions that give Seller the option to elect a physical alternate delivery option for the

              3.15. CC Operating Flexibility. A Participant offering a 2-on-1 CC Facility must offer operation in the
                    1-on-1 mode if technically feasible by design. Operating in 1-on-1 mode entails the ability to
                    operate a single CT, one HRSG, and the steam turbine while second CT is shutoff. A Participant
                    offering this type of Facility must offer cycling from 2-on-1 operation down to 1-on-1 mode and
                    back up to 2-on-1 mode if technically feasible by design. A Participant may also propose a 1-on-
                    1 CC Facility.

                     3.15.2. Operation Mode Pricing. A Participant offering a 2-on-1 CC Facility should offer 1-on-1
                     operation pricing based on the cost of operating in this mode. This should entail a start charge
                     that accurately represents the cost of starting the Facility in the 1-on-1 mode and the cost of
                     moving from 1-on-1 mode to 2-on-1 mode. The Participant should also provide heat rate curves
                     consistent with the actual cost of 1-on-1 operation. If a Participant proposes a resource with other
                     operational capabilities, (e.g., 3-on-1 or power augmentation), Participant’s Submission must offer
                     the operational flexibility consistent with the Facility capabilities and pricing based on the cost of
                     providing such operational flexibility.

              3.16. Compliance with Laws Generally. It is Bidder’s sole responsibility to take all necessary actions
                    to satisfy any regulatory requirements, licenses, and permits that may be imposed on Bidder by
                    any federal, state, or local Governmental Authority concerning the permitting, development,
                    construction, operation, maintenance, addition, renewal, retirement, or disposal of the Facility, or
                    concerning the generation, sale, and delivery of energy. GPC will cooperate with Winning
                    Bidder(s) to provide information or other assistance as may reasonably be requested by the
                    Bidder to satisfy regulatory requirements. Bidder must likewise provide necessary information
                    and assistance to GPC concerning GPC’s regulatory approvals.


                     PRICING, FEES, AND SECURITY

              4.1.   PPA Pricing. PPA Bid prices must include all costs GPC will pay for the capacity and energy to
                     be delivered under the PPA in accordance with GPC’s scheduling instructions. GPC will not be
                     responsible for any other cost associated with the Facility, including Station Service, fuel for
                     testing, transmission system interconnection, and all costs (including fuel) incurred to accomplish
                     synchronization.

                     4.1.1. Escalating Pricing. A PPA Bidder may submit a Bid with the capacity payment escalated
                     at a fixed percentage not to exceed 2.5% in any Annual Period. The minimum escalation during
                     any Annual Period for the capacity payment will be limited to 0%.

                     4.1.2. Variable Pricing (Not Applicable to ESS Bids). All energy pricing, Variable O&M, and
                     heat rates must be quoted as indicated in the Bid Form. Variable O&M must escalate at actual
                     GDPIPD or actual GDPIPD plus or minus 1% per annum. Bidders are encouraged to propose
                     variable costs consistent with their actual realized variable costs. The Bid heat rate should closely
                     approximate the anticipated heat rate. If the Bid’s variable components are not consistent with
                     Facility design specifications, GPC may request, through the IE, that Bidder modify its Bid(s). This
                     cost-based pricing approach must reflect the following components, as applicable: (i) Variable
                     O&M; (ii) start cost; (iii) heat rate; and (iv) fuel commodity cost.

              4.2.   APA/BTA Pricing. Each APA/BTA Bid must provide an “all-in” price that includes all customary
                     and reasonable facilities necessary for reliable operation of the Facility, including transmission
                     interconnection, gas lateral, any other facilities, and the Site. An APA/BTA Facility must include

                     the Facility’s major equipment and all auxiliary equipment and facilities necessary or used for the
                     production, control, delivery, or monitoring of electricity produced on the property. All equipment
                     and other facilities installed on the Facility’s side of the POI and the primary gas delivery point, if
                     applicable, must be considered part of the Facility. All data provided in Exhibit C (Additional Bid
                     Information and Questionnaire), including capacity, heat rate, Variable O&M, startup fuel, and
                     Facility availability must be based on: (i) testing, past performance, and good faith estimates for
                     an APA Facility; or (ii) design criteria for a BTA Facility.

                     4.2.1. Option to Purchase Land. If an APA/BTA Bidder owns property adjacent to the Site, the
                     Bidder may include within its Bid an offer to sell to GPC the adjacent property for an optional price
                     stated in the Bid.

                     4.2.2. Due Diligence. Concurrent with GPC’s initial economic screening of all conforming
                     Submissions, GPC will begin APA/BTA due diligence assessments as generally described in
                     Exhibit A (Due Diligence Phases and Fees Overview (APA and BTA Bids Only)) to determine
                     GPC’s best estimate of the cost to own and operate the Facility.

              4.3.   Change of Law. If a Change of Law occurs, Participant may request to adjust its Submission
                     pricing to account for Change of Law Capital Expenditures more than: (i) for PPA Bids, 10% of
                     Bidder’s offered Annual Capacity Price multiplied by the Facility Nominal Capability (kW) for the
                     first Annual Period; or (ii) for BTA/APA Bids and COPs, more than 20% of the purchase price
                     divided by the Facility Design Life (“Excess Change of Law Capital Expenditures”).
                     4.3.1. Notice. If Participant determines that any Change of Law will cause Change of Law
                     Capital Expenditures not accounted for in Submission pricing, Participant must notify GPC
                     through the IE Website no later than 15 Business Days after Participant knew or should have
                     known of the Change of Law. Participant’s notice to GPC must identify in reasonable detail the
                     claimed Change of Law and its likely effects on the Facility.

                     4.3.2. Submission Pricing Adjustment Before Refresh. For any Change of Law that occurs
                     before the Submission refresh deadline stated in the Solicitation Schedule and for which
                     Participant provided notice in accordance with Section 4.3.1 (Notice), Participant may include
                     Change of Law Capital Expenditures in its refreshed Submission Pricing.

                     4.3.3. Submissions Pricing Adjustment After Refresh. For any Change of Law that occurs
                     after the after the Submission refresh deadline stated in the Solicitation Schedule and for which
                     Participant provided timely notice in accordance with Section 4.3.1 (Notice), Participant may
                     request approval to adjust its Submission pricing to account for Excess Change of Law Capital
                     Expenditures. Participant must submit its request through the IE Website. Participant’s request
                     must state Participant’s proposed Submission pricing adjustment and be supported by
                     documentation sufficient for GPC to validate the need for and amount of Excess Change of Law
                     Capital Expenditures. GPC will evaluate Participant’s request and reasonably determine if it is
                     appropriate to allow Seller to adjust its PPA Bid Price by taking into account the requested
                     adjustment amount, composition of the Competitive Tier, the Submission’s potential benefit to
                     GPC customers, and any other quantitative or qualitative factor GPC deems appropriate. GPC
                     will notify Participant of GPC’s determination through the IE Website. If GPC determines a pricing
                     adjustment is not appropriate, GPC will notify Participant and allow Participant to withdraw its
                     Submission without penalty (including Bid Security forfeiture), at Participant’s election.

                     4.3.4. PPA Pricing Adjustments. If GPC agrees an adjustment is appropriate, GPC and Bidder
                     will, each acting in a good faith and commercially reasonable manner and under the oversight of
                     the IE, establish an appropriate annual fixed charge rate to apply to the original capital cost of the
                     additions, modifications, or other capital expenditures that comprise Excess Change of Law
                     Capital Expenditures for purposes of calculating an adjustment to the Annual Capacity Price(s)
                     associated with capitalized additions or modifications to the Facility (determined in accordance
                     with GAAP).

                     with a Submission that advanced to the Conforming List to inform the Participant that it may better
                     (increase or decrease) its Submission price as a final and best offer, as described in the applicable
                     subsections below. The IE will post a ranking list on the IE Website showing each Participant’s
                     relative rank. Each Participant on the Conforming List will be identified blindly, so each Participant
                     may only see its rank compared to those of all other anonymous Submissions. GPC will further
                     evaluate refreshed Submissions and advance a Competitive Tier in accordance with the RFP
                     Rule and as described in Section 8.6 (Bid Lists).

                     4.4.1. Refreshed Submissions Process. Each Participant invited to refresh Submission
                     pricing must submit refreshed pricing (as limited by the subsections that follow) by the deadline
                     stated in the Solicitation Schedule. Except as described in the subsections that follow, no changes
                     to the Submission are allowed, including changes to Facility size, technology, or commercial
                     operation date. Any refreshed Submission pricing will supersede the Submission’s initial price. At
                     submission, Participant must also include a written narrative explaining why it is necessary for
                     Participant to change its pricing. GPC will use Participant’s explanatory information for
                     informational purposes and, to the extent the Submission is a Winning Submission, in support of
                     its Certification request.

                     4.4.2. PPA Bid Refresh. Each PPA Bidder with a Bid that advances to the Conforming List will
                     be given one opportunity to refresh the fixed-price portion of its Bid (i.e., capacity price and fuel

                     4.4.3. APA/BTA Bid Refresh. Each APA/BTA Bidder with a Bid that advances to the Conforming
                     List will be given one opportunity to refresh its acquisition price and fuel transportation price.

                     4.4.4. COP Refresh. If a COP advances to Conforming List, the COP Team will be given one
                     opportunity to refresh the total fixed-cost portion of the Company-Owned Proposal.

                     portion of each Bid Fee in the amount of $10,000 will be earmarked to offset IE costs. Bidder

                     Design Life basis for BTAs and Company-Owned Proposals. Winning Bidder must pay the

                     Bid Period commences and Participant initiates the Submission process. A Participant may ask
                     Site-specific and Facility-specific questions using the “Messages” feature on the IE Website.
                     Communications submitted through a Bid Book are not seen by other Participants and are only

                     SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

              7.1.   Notice of Intent to Submit. GPC requests that each Participant submit a notice of intent (NOI) to
                     submit using the form available on the IE Website by the date and time recommended in the
                     Solicitation Schedule. Each BTA Bidder must submit an NOI to receive GPC’s nondisclosure
                     agreement as required under Section 3.12.1 (BTA Bids and COPs). Participant must list only one
                     point of contact in the NOI. If Participant intends to submit multiple Submissions, Participant may
                     list all potential Submissions on a single NOI. Participant must indicate its proposed technology type
                     and contract form (PPA, BTA, or APA), if applicable, for each Submission.
              7.2.   Bid Process. Each Submission must be submitted via the Bid Form on the IE Website by no later
                     than the date and time specified in the Solicitation Schedule. If a Bidder discovers an error or
                     omission in the Bid after submitting its Bids but before the Bid Due Date, Bidder must note any
                     change in the electronic filing and the changes must be posted to the Bid Form by no later than
                     12:00 p.m. ET on the Bid Due Date.
              7.3.   Effect of Bid Submission. Bidder’s Bid submission will constitute Bidder’s acknowledgment and
                     acceptance of all terms, conditions, and requirements of this All-Source RFP, including pro forma
                     PPA terms and conditions. Failure to provide all requested Submission information may invalidate
                     a Submission. GPC is not required to contact any Participant to obtain any omitted information.
              7.4.   Alternative Bids; Multiple Submissions; Bid Fees.

                     7.4.1. Alternative Bid. Bidder may submit a separate, mutually exclusive Bid that offers a
                     Facility located on the same Site and using the same Point of Delivery as another Bid, but the
                     Alternative Bid: (i) offers the same technology under a different form of contract; (ii) offers the
                     same technology with varying PPA Term lengths; or (iii) offers a different technology (e.g., CT vs
                     CC) (“Alternative Bid”). The placement of a Bid on the Release List will not affect GPC’s
                     evaluation of the Alternative Bid.

                     7.4.2. Multiple Submissions. Participants may submit multiple Submissions into this All-
                     Source RFP. Except for an Alternative Bid, GPC will not accept contingent Submissions (i.e., a
                     Submission that is dependent upon another Submission’s outcome). For example, GPC will not
                     accept Submissions where Participant submitted multiple Submissions for several Sites but is
                     only willing to develop a limited number of those Facilities or requires a combination of the
                     Submissions to be advanced together. Additionally, Bidder may not aggregate multiple Facilities
                     from one or more Sites to meet the minimum MW required to be submitted in this All-Source RFP.

                     7.4.3. Bid Fees. If Bidder submits separate Bids that vary regarding certain critical parameters,
                     including contract type, the Site, output, electrical characteristics, or technology (e.g., gas-fired
                     CC and simple cycle CT facilities, cogeneration, primary fuel, ESS duration), Bidder will be
                     required to pay the Bid Fee ($20,000.00) for each Bid. However, PPA Bids submitted by one
                     Bidder for the same Site, same generation technology, and same size that offer options in the fuel
                     plan or fixed cost components will be considered a single Bid. In addition, Bids for the same Site
                     containing options in the number of generating units offered will be considered a single Bid if the
                     generation technology is the same and the operational parameters and variable pricing are the
                     same in all Bids. PPA Bids for 5-, 10-, 15-, 20-, 25-, or 30-year Terms with all performance and
                     variable pricing characteristics remaining the same will be considered one Bid. A maximum of
                     three (3) options will be accepted as a single Bid covered under one Bid Fee.

                     as and when deemed necessary by GPC.

                     7.5.3. Bidder Variable Interest Entity Certification. Depending on the PPA Term and the
                     business structure, a PPA Bidder may choose to adopt accounting and tax rules that may require:
                     (i) that a PPA, or components of the PPA, be accounted for by GPC as a lease; or (ii) Seller under
                     the PPA be consolidated as a VIE onto GPC’s books. Because GPC is unwilling to be subject to
                     accounting or tax treatment that results from VIE treatment, each Bidder is required to certify,
                     using the form found in Exhibit J (VIE Certification), its independent belief that the Bidder’s Bid
                     will most likely not require the Seller at any time over the proposed PPA term to deconsolidate on
                     its books and records any assets, liabilities, cash flow, profits, or losses where GPC is determined
                     to be the Primary Beneficiary. At PPA execution, annually through the Term, and at any time the
                     PPA is amended by the Parties, the Seller’s chief financial officer or an officer having responsibility
                     for financial accounting matters associated with the PPA, must again provide this certification.
                     Further, any PPA that GPC executes will require that: (a) Seller covenant that GPC will not be
                     subject to VIE treatment at any point during the Term; and (b) if the PPA causes GPC to be subject
                     to VIE treatment at any point during the Term, unless cured, such treatment will constitute a PPA
                     Event of Default. As provided for in the pro forma PPAs, GPC would have the right to terminate
                     the PPA, and unless Seller can clearly demonstrate that the consolidation event was not due to
                     the direct or indirect actions of Seller, Seller will be liable for termination damages as outlined in
                     the PPA.

                     for each Bid based on Bidder’s personal consideration of the factual matters and Bidder’s
                     understanding of accounting standards regarding a Finance and Operating Lease, using the form
                     provided in Exhibit K (Finance Lease Certification Checklist). If Bidder responds in the affirmative
                     on one or more of the factual statements, Bidder must also provide the amounts that GPC would
                     be required to capitalize and the residual value of the Facility as defined in Exhibit K. In any case
                     for which Bidder responds in the negative to all the factual statements set forth in Exhibit K, Bidder
                     is required to certify such declaration, with supporting information sufficient to enable GPC to
                     independently verify that Finance Lease treatment will not occur. At the time of Bid submission,
                     at PPA execution, and at any time the PPA is amended by the Parties, Seller’s chief financial
                     officer or an officer having responsibility for financial accounting matters associated with the PPA
                     must again provide this certification. For Bids declared as Finance or Operating Lease, the Bid
                     evaluation will include the cost to GPC resulting from capitalization of PPA costs on GPC’s
                     balance sheet.

              8.1.   Staff and IE Oversight/Evaluation. In accordance with the RFP Rule, Staff and the IE actively

                     contact any Participant for additional information or to cure a deficiency identified in a Submission.

                     will be evaluated to establish an initial ranking before the Refreshed Submissions Process.
              8.4.   Competitive Tier Identified. Under the oversight of the IE and Staff, GPC will determine a
                     Competitive Tier that consists of the most competitive Submissions. An appropriate selection of
                     Submissions meeting GPC’s requirements will advance as the Competitive Tier for additional

                     quantified. GPC may evaluate Submissions against more than one CO2 and fuel scenarios. All
                     Submissions (including Company-Owned Proposals, APA/BTA Bids, and Affiliate Bids) will be
                     considered and evaluated together. As part of its Competitive Tier evaluation, GPC will review
                     generation and transmission costs and Ancillary Service requirements, as appropriate, to
                     determine the Submission’s total cost impact. After the detailed transmission and portfolio
                     analysis concludes, the most competitive Submissions will advance to the Short List, which may

                    CERTIFICATION

              10.1. Awarded Contract Certification. Following completion of the All-Source RFP evaluation and
                    award process, GPC will seek Commission Certification, under O.C.G.A. § 46-3A-4, of each
                    Awarded Contract executed with this All-Source RFP. The Certification process will take place
                    under a separate Commission Docket and may take up to six months to complete, unless
                    otherwise expedited by the Commission Order. GPC’s performance of an Awarded Contract is
                    conditioned on the Commission issuing a certificate approving the Awarded Contract in a timely
                    manner without material qualification or condition adversely affecting GPC; otherwise, the
                    Awarded Contract will provide that GPC may terminate the PPA without any further obligation. In
                    addition to GPC’s Awarded Contract obligations being contingent on Commission approval,
                    GPC’s obligations are also contingent upon GPC continuing to have a need for capacity and
                    energy for the identified need years.

                    10.1.1. FERC Acceptance. Performance of an Awarded Contract is also conditioned upon, if
                    required by applicable law, FERC issuing an order accepting the Awarded Contract in a timely
                    manner and without material qualification or condition adversely affecting either party to the
                    Awarded Contract; otherwise, the Awarded Contract will provide that either party may terminate
                    the Awarded Contract without any further legal obligation.

              10.2. Company-Owned Proposal Certification. In accordance with O.C.G.A. § 46-3A-5, and under
                    Commission Rule 515-3-4-.07(2), if a Company-Owned Proposal advances, it will be submitted for
                    Certification together with other winning Bids, and the IE will testify regarding its evaluation of the
                    Company-Owned Proposal. The Commission’s certificate approving any Company-Owned Proposal
                    will set forth the not-to-exceed cost, which, like the certified cost of any PPA or asset purchase
                    agreement under which GPC acquires a Facility, may not otherwise change, except as allowed by law
                    under O.C.G.A. § 46-3A-7, and only with the Commission’s express approval.
