          EXHIBIT A – DUE DILIGENCE PHASES AND FEES OVERVIEW (APA AND BTA BIDS ONLY)

         PART 1      BID INFORMATION.
         1.1     Identification of Critical Due Diligence Topics for First Due Diligence Phase. At the time of Bid submission,
         an APA/BTA Bidder must: (i) provide the APA/BTA Due Diligence Checklist available on the IE Website and required
         accompanying documents; and (ii) recommend additional critical due diligence topics that the Evaluation Team should
         include in the first due diligence phase (“Phase One Due Diligence”) described in this Exhibit A. If Bidder is proposing
         an APA, Bidder must identify known plant equipment and operational concerns (e.g., vibrations, recurring problems or
         failures, needed maintenance, cracked turbine blades) and known legal or environmental issues concerning the
         Facility so key issues that could affect life-cycle cost or Facility reliability can be addressed early in the due diligence
         process.

         PART 2      INITIAL ECONOMIC SCREEN ($20,000 FEE).
         2.1    Bid Fee. Each Bidder must submit a non-refundable Bid Fee ($20,000) with each Bid in accordance with RFP
         Section 7.4.3 (Bid Fees) before the Evaluation Team will begin evaluating the Bid.
         2.2    Screening Overview. If a Bid advances past the initial economic screening, the Bid will proceed through the
         additional due diligence steps outlined in the following sections of this Exhibit A.

         PART 3      PHASE ONE DUE DILIGENCE ($50,000 FEE).
         3.1    Fee Requirement. Bidder must submit a Phase One Due Diligence Fee of $50,000 in addition to the required
         Bid Fee ($20,000) by no later than the Bid Due Date shown in the Solicitation Schedule. The total initial payment
         required for APA/BTA Bids is $70,000, which is the sum of: (i) the $20,000 Bid Fee; plus (ii) the $50,000 Phase One
         Due Diligence Fee.
         3.2   Phase One Due Diligence Overview. Phase One Due Diligence will consist of “fatal flaw assessment” to
         determine if there are significant issues with the APA/BTA Bid that would call into question the value of the asset. The
         Phase One Due Diligence review will be preliminary and will include the following:
            A. APA Phase One Due Diligence
              (i) Technical and engineering review of APA Due Diligence Checklist and accompanying documents, including
              review of major equipment and balance of plant components.
                    (a) For items requested in the APA Due Diligence Checklist and required accompanying documents that
                    Bidder does not provide with the Bid Submission, Bidder must explain in writing why Bidder did not submit
                    the information. Bidder must provide to the Evaluation Team for review, any applicable information or
                    supporting documentation that Bidder obtains during due diligence.
              (ii) Review of independent engineering report.
              (iii) Site design and engineering review.
              (iv) Review of Bidder-identified due diligence topics.
            B. BTA Phase One Due Diligence
              (i) Technical and engineering review of BTA Due Diligence Checklist and accompanying documents, including
              review of major equipment and balance of plant components.
                    (a) For items requested in the BTA Due Diligence Checklist and required accompanying documents that
                    Bidder does not provide with the Bid submission, Bidder must explain in writing why Bidder did not submit
                    the information. Bidder must provide to the Evaluation Team for review, any applicable information or
                    supporting documentation that Bidder obtains during due diligence.
              (ii) Proposed Site design and initial engineering review.
              (iii) Review of Bidder-identified due diligence topics.
         3.3   Refund or Credit of Unused Fee. If GPC does not expend the entire $50,000 Phase One Due Diligence Fee,
         GPC will refund the unused portion to Bidder or credit the balance as payment toward the Phase Two Due Diligence
         Fee, as applicable.

                         EXHIBIT B – INTERCONNECTION AND DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS
         Each Bidder is responsible for determining all transmission interconnection and delivery-related rules,
         practices, and policies with which Bidder must comply. Each Bid must comply with the general requirements
         outlined in Part 1 (Interconnection and Delivery Requirements – General) of this Exhibit B and with one of the
         interconnection options described in Parts 2 (Interconnection with the Southern Company Transmission
         System (>40 kV)), 3 (Interconnection to the Electric System of an ITS Participant (>40 kV)), or
         4 (Interconnection of a Non-ESS Facility Outside the STT (PPA Bidders Only)) of this Exhibit B.

         PART 1 INTERCONNECTION AND DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS – GENERAL
         The following interconnection requirements apply to all Bids, regardless of Facility location.
         1.1     Transmission Projected Commercial Operation Date. GPC may decline to advance a Bid to the Short
         List or to execute an Awarded Contract with any Bidder if, in GPC’s opinion, the transmission facilities cannot
         be constructed in time to achieve Commercial Operation or Closing, as applicable, by the date set forth in the
         Solicitation Schedule. Except for the provision in Section 2.7 (Facility Interconnecting Directly to GPC) of this
         Exhibit B for a Facility interconnecting to the Southern Company Transmission System via GPC, Bidder
         assumes all interconnection and delivery lead-time risk (if applicable) to meet the RCOD or RCD, as applicable.
            A. Bid Price Assumptions. If the Facility’s POI is not on the Southern Company Transmission System, each Bid
            must state the assumptions regarding interconnection and delivery costs that are included in the Bid price.
            Specifically, each Bid must include details of these costs and refer to any completed or active Interconnection Study
            results related to the Facility.
            B. Bid Lead-Time Assumptions. Each Bid must describe the Facility’s current status within the applicable
            interconnection process and Bidder’s ability to meet the RCOD, or RCD in the case of an APA or a BTA, based
            upon the applicable interconnection process timeline.
            C. Interconnection Agreement Required. Each Winning Bidder must enter into an IA with the appropriate
            Interconnection Provider, depending on the geographic location and interconnection configuration of the Facility.
            Each Bidder must contact the appropriate Interconnection Provider to obtain all relevant information and
            interconnection requirements. The submission of a Bid in response to this All-Source RFP does not
            constitute an interconnection request or an IA. Bidder is solely responsible for all fees, deposits, and other
            charges regarding Bidder’s interconnection request and the IA. At any point in time, the Facility is prohibited from
            delivering output to the Point of Delivery that exceeds the lesser of the Generating Capacity or the Interconnection
            Limit.
            D. Timing and Notification of Initiating Interconnection Process (New Facility). At the time of Bid submission,
            Bidder must indicate if there is an existing interconnection request for the Facility (either in active study stage or if
            there is an IA that is in suspension), and if so, Bidder also must identify the Interconnection Provider, request
            number/identifier, and status. If Bidder has an IA in suspension, Bidder must initiate the process with the appropriate
            Interconnection Provider to move out of suspension and back to active status by no later than seven Days after
            notification that the Bid advanced to the Short List. If Bidder has not submitted an interconnection request as of the
            date of the Bid’s advancement to the Competitive Tier, Bidder must initiate the interconnection process with the
            appropriate Interconnection Provider no later than seven Days prior to Short List determination as set forth in the
            Solicitation Schedule. Further, Bidder is responsible for understanding applicable timing requirements associated
            with submitting an interconnection request and obtaining an Interconnection Agreement from the applicable
            Interconnection Provider and any related risk to meeting the RCOD, or RCD in the case of an APA or a BTA, of this
            RFP.

         equipment, tie-line (which carries electrical power and communications), and any additional equipment (such as a
         utility-owned interrupting device and metering needed to connect to the transmission facilities), as well as any additional
         real property for the interconnection substation and access, and any operation and maintenance expenses and
         administrative costs. In addition, if applicable, Bidder is responsible for the cost, risk, and coordination of all Affected
         System Upgrades. It is Bidder’s responsibility to determine and consider all information regarding interconnection costs
         in preparing its Bid.

            beyond the POI. For a Facility interconnecting to the Southern Company Transmission System, any interconnection
            costs for new or modified equipment on the Southern Company Transmission System beyond the POI (refundable
            “Network Upgrades” under the LGIP/LGIA) will be imputed to the Bid during the Bid evaluation and should not be
            included in the Bid price. However, as stated above in Section 2.3 (Bidder Cost Responsibility) of this Exhibit B any
            costs associated with Affected System Upgrades are solely Bidder’s responsibility and will not be reimbursed by
            GPC.
            B. SCS LGIA Costs. A Winning Bidder (i.e., Seller) may be required under the terms of its SCS LGIA to fund or
            provide security for new or modified equipment beyond the POI (interconnection costs beyond the POI that are
            refundable “Network Upgrades” per the LGIP/LGIA). However, if Seller incurs such interconnection-related costs
            for new or modified equipment on the Southern Company Transmission System beyond the POI, after the Facility

                                    EXHIBIT F – BID ASSIGNMENT GUIDELINES

            PART 1    BID ASSIGNMENT
            1.1   Overview.
              A. A Bid may only be assigned, including any assignment of a previously assigned Bid to the original
              Bidder, with the prior written notice to and consent of GPC in accordance with the requirements of this
              Exhibit F (Bid Assignment Guidelines).
              B. For each proposed Bid Assignment, Bidder and the proposed Bid assignee named in and
              executing the Consent Request (“Bid Assignee”) must review the requirements of this Exhibit F (Bid
              Assignment Guidelines) and agree to the GPC Bid Assignment Consent Form included as Attachment
              1 to this Exhibit F (Bid Assignment Guidelines) (“Consent Request”).
              C. These guidelines are limited to Bid assignments during the All-Source RFP Bid solicitation phase
              (each attempted or completed assignment, a “Bid Assignment”). For assignments, transfers, or other
              changes after Awarded Contract execution, the contracting party must comply with requirements in
              those agreements. For purposes of this Exhibit F (Bid Assignment Guidelines) a Change of Control of
              a Bidder will be deemed an assignment, subject to the provisions of this Exhibit F (Bid Assignment
              Guidelines). For purposes of this Exhibit F (Bid Assignment Guidelines), a “Change of Control” is any
              transaction or series of related transactions which, if consummated, would result in Bidder being an
              Affiliate of another ultimate parent entity immediately after the transaction or series of transactions. For
              purposes of this definition, the ultimate parent entity is the Person who directly or indirectly controls
              50% or more of Bidder’s outstanding capital stock or other equity interests having ordinary voting power
              and who does not itself have an ultimate parent entity.
            1.2   Notice and Consent Requirements.
              A. Notice Requirements.
                (i) Assignment Before Awarded Contract Execution. If Bidder intends to assign its Bid, Bidder
                must provide GPC with prior written notice through the IE Website in the form of the Consent
                Request of: (i) Bidder’s intent to assign the Bid; (ii) the name of the proposed Bid Assignee; (iii) the
                information required under Section 1.3 (Required Information) of this Exhibit F regarding the Bid
                Assignee; and (iv) Bidder’s request for GPC to consent to the Bid Assignment. The Consent
                Request and all required information must be submitted to GPC through the IE Website at least 15
                Days before the proposed effective date of the Bid Assignment, but in no event less than 15 Days
                before the Awarded Contract Effective Date.
                (ii) Failure to Comply with Notice Requirements. If a Bidder does not comply with the notice
                and consent requirements of this Exhibit F (Bid Assignment Guidelines), GPC may include the Bid
                in the Release List for that reason alone. A consent granted by GPC for a Bid Assignment does not
                mean that the Bid will be advanced as a winning Bid or advanced to the Competitive Tier or Short
                List.
              B. Consent by GPC. Bidder must not assign any Bid without GPC’s prior written consent. Any
              attempted Bid assignment without GPC’s prior written consent will be void and the original Bidder will
              remain responsible for all its obligations relating to the Bid. GPC's consent to a proposed Bid
              Assignment will not create any obligation for GPC to the original Bidder or Bid Assignee beyond GPC's
              evaluation of the Bid according to the All-Source RFP. GPC reserves the right to reject a Bid Assignment
              in its sole but reasonable discretion, including if notice is late, incomplete, or GPC determines the Bid
              Assignment would be contrary to the All-Source RFP or the Commission’s orders relating to the All-
              Source RFP. If GPC rejects a Bidder’s proposed Bid Assignment, GPC will provide Bidder with notice

                          EXHIBIT H – OVERVIEW OF EVALUATION METHODOLOGY
            The following is a general overview of GPC’s methodology for Submission evaluation. PPA Bids,
            APA Bids, BTA Bids, and any Company-Owned Proposal(s) will receive comparable evaluation
            that ensures a net total cost is calculated while accounting for the net present value of generation
            and transmission aspects over the life of the asset. As part of the evaluation, GPC may also
            consider the non-price factors described in Exhibit I (Non-Price Considerations).

            All graphics and tables included in this Exhibit H are for illustrative purposes only.

            I. Net Total Cost Evaluation. Each Submission advanced to the Conforming List will be
               evaluated and ranked using a net generation cost analysis approach. Each Submission
               advanced to the Competitive Tier will be evaluated and ranked using a net total cost analysis
               approach. The net total cost is the net present value of the generation and transmission aspects
               of the Submission in dollars per kilowatt ($/kW) of capacity contribution. The generation cost is
               comprised of both the fixed cost associated with the Submission and the variable cost
               associated with the operational parameters of the Submission, which will be used in production
               cost modeling simulations. The capacity contribution of each Submission will be based on the
               effective load carrying capability (“ELCC”), which will be determined by the process approved
               by the Commission in the 2022 IRP filed in Docket No. 44160. ELCC may vary based on
               technology type and operational characteristics within the same technology. For example,
               Energy Storage Systems that differ in discharge duration may have different ELCC.

                A. Generation Costs – Determining Fixed Costs.

                Fixed generation cost will include the following (as applicable to the Submission):

                1. The Bidder-specified capacity cost payment (typically quoted in dollars per kilowatt ($/kW)
                   for each year) for PPA Bids;
                2. The costs associated with PPA treatment as either an Operating Lease or a Finance Lease,
                   as applicable, if it is determined that the PPA constitutes a lease in accordance with RFP
                   Section 7.5.4 (Finance Lease Certification);
                3. GPC’s revenue requirements for the purchase price for APA/BTA Bids and in-service costs
                   for Company-Owned Proposals. These revenue requirements account for depreciation,
                   cost of capital, and taxes; and
                4. The fuel pipeline costs, which include the estimated costs for adequate firm natural gas
                   transportation and natural gas storage, as applicable. This requirement is not applicable to
                   an ESS Bid.

                The evaluation will consider differences in the seasonal capability of each Submission.

                B. Equity Cost of PPA – Determining the Balance Sheet Consequence for Operating
                   Lease or Finance Lease Treatment.

                If a Bid is determined to be a lease, there is an equity cost to GPC when the PPA is placed on
                GPC’s balance sheet caused by the rating agency treatment of a lease in accordance with
                FASB ASC Topic 842.

                For a Finance Lease, GPC must capitalize the PPA as an asset on its balance sheet and must
                offset it by a debt obligation on the liability side of the balance sheet. The addition of the debt
                obligation on the balance sheet requires GPC to recapitalize to maintain the appropriate debt
                and equity ratio. As a result, there are direct equity costs incurred by GPC when a PPA is
                capitalized and reflected on the balance sheet as a Finance Lease. The equity cost of a Bid


            ALL-SOURCE RFP                                                                            Page 86 of 115

                                                    www.gonitro.com

STF-JKA-1-24 Attachment A.pdf

                                                                     All-Source Capacity RFP for 2029–2031
                                                                                            RFP Document
                                                                                Final Approved – Revision 1


               determined to result in a Finance Lease, if selected, will be evaluated by determining the net
               cost (lease cost less depreciation and tax implication) of capitalizing the PPA.

               For an Operating Lease, the PPA is also added to the balance sheet but without directly
               affecting the debt and equity ratio on GPC’s books. However, rating agencies impute debt onto
               GPC’s balance sheet in their evaluation of the credit rating for GPC. Therefore, GPC must still
               recapitalize to maintain the target debt and equity ratio needed to ensure its credit rating is not
               impacted by the PPA. There is a direct equity cost premium associated with this treatment.

               The additional annual revenue requirement cost to GPC is calculated for the Operating Lease
               or Finance Lease. The result is the equity cost applied to the Bid.

               C. Generation Costs – Determining the Production Cost Savings.

               The variable generation cost includes:
               1.   Fuel cost for any CT or CC Submission
               2.   Charging costs for any ESS Submission
               3.   Variable O&M
               4.   Facility dispatch characteristics
               5.   RECs and integration costs for ESS with Renewable Resource Submissions.
               Production cost computer simulations are required to estimate the operational savings
               associated with operating each proposed Facility with the system dispatch. Each Submission’s
               contribution to reducing the aggregate annual system generation fleet fuel and variable cost
               can be calculated by comparing a cost simulation that includes the Submission against a
               reference simulation (without the Submission). The variable cost components of each
               Submission are modeled within the production cost simulation. In addition to fuel and O&M
               Costs, Facility operating characteristics, including efficiency (e.g., heat rate, Round-Trip
               Efficiency), scheduled maintenance requirements, any applicable Ancillary Services, and
               projected availability will contribute to the total production cost. For ESS Submissions,
               additional operating characteristics such as charge and discharge duration, cycle limits, and
               charging source (grid or paired resource) will contribute to calculation of the total production
               cost.

               Evaluation of ESS with Renewable Resource Submissions requires the renewable generation
               profile to be submitted for inclusion in the production cost simulation. There will be a $/MWh
               REC component attributed to any Renewable Energy to account for the forecasted value of
               RECs. Depending on the renewable generation technology and configuration of a paired ESS,
               a $/MWh integration cost will be applied to any Renewable Energy to account for costs arising
               from actions taken by system operators to respond to the additional volatility on the system
               from the intermittent nature of Renewable Resources. RECs and integration costs will be
               evaluated in accordance with the RCB Framework, as approved by the Commission in Docket
               44160.

               In general, GPC conducts the production cost simulation to calculate the projected annual
               production cost savings on a per kilowatt capacity basis for the Submission.

               An illustrative example of the net generation cost calculation (total fixed generation costs net
               production cost savings) is provided below.

               D. Net Generation Cost: Calculating the Net Generation Cost of a Proposal.

               The production cost simulation is conducted to achieve the annual production cost savings.
               The calculation of the net generation cost for each proposal is a three-step process: (i) the
               Submission’s fixed costs are calculated annually on a dollar per kilowatt basis; (ii) on an annual
               basis, the per kilowatt production cost savings are subtracted from the fixed costs resulting in
               the annual net generation per kilowatt costs; and (iii) the final net generation cost is the
               accumulated net present value of the annual net generation costs.

               An illustrative example of the net present value of the net generation cost calculation is provided
               in the following table.

                                                Evaluation Task:
                             Determine the Present Value of the Net Generation Costs


               E. Transmission Costs: Evaluation of Transmission Impacts of Bids.

               After determination of the Competitive Tier, an assessment of the transmission impact of each
               Submission will be an integral part of the net total cost analysis. Each Submission on the
               Competitive Tier is evaluated from a transmission network perspective to assess:


            ALL-SOURCE RFP                                                                          Page 88 of 115

                                                   www.gonitro.com

STF-JKA-1-24 Attachment A.pdf

                                                                     All-Source Capacity RFP for 2029–2031
                                                                                            RFP Document
                                                                                Final Approved – Revision 1


                 1. The additional network transmission investment required to deliver Facility output to native
                    load on a firm basis;
                 2. The additional network transmission investment required to provide grid charging service
                    from the network, if applicable; and
                 3. The increase (or decrease) in transmission system energy losses due to the operation of
                    the proposed Facility.

                 Each Submission is analyzed using transmission system computer simulation models to
                 determine if additional transmission network improvements are required to accommodate the
                 proposed Facility. For evaluation purposes, the Submission is assessed the yearly amortized
                 cost of the transmission improvements.
                 The transmission simulation models include future projections of transmission facilities and
                 planned GPC-owned generation to maintain grid reliability in areas of major load (net of
                 generation).
                 In addition, each Submission is analyzed to determine whether operation of the proposed
                 Facility increases or decreases the transmission system energy losses. Each Submission is
                 assessed an annual cost (or credit) associated with its projected impact on the transmission
                 system energy losses.
                 As part of the evaluation of transmission impacts of each Submission, GPC will further
                 assess any project scheduling risk posed by the transmission system evaluation, including
                 the ability of the proposed project to meet the RCOD or RCD, as applicable.
                 Illustrative examples of how the net transmission cost and net total cost are determined are
                 provided below.

           II.   Due Diligence Portfolio Analysis

             The Competitive Tier will be evaluated and ranked using a consistent methodology that identifies
             the best Submissions based on the net present value of net total cost per kW. To satisfy the

            capacity need targeted in this All-Source RFP, more than one Submission may be selected. A
            portfolio analysis will be required to determine the best portfolio (combination of two or more) of
            Submissions that satisfy the identified capacity need. For Submissions offering multiple units in a
            single Submission, each unit or group of units may be selected separately by GPC.

            In the due diligence portfolio analysis, the best Submissions will be packaged together into several
            combinations or “portfolios.” Each of the resulting portfolios will be evaluated using a net total cost
            approach that is consistent with the methodology used to evaluate each individual Submission. In
            the portfolio phase, a production cost simulation and a transmission cost analysis are required to
            evaluate the cost impacts resulting from any interaction that may result from packaging several
            Submissions into a portfolio.

                          EXHIBIT L – ADDITIONAL GUIDANCE FOR ESS SUBMISSIONS
            This Exhibit L provides additional guidance, including operational requirements, for Participants
            developing ESS Submissions. This Exhibit L also summarizes PPA pricing structure and
            performance metrics, but PPA Bidders must also reference the pro forma Standalone ESS PPA or
            the pro forma ESS with Renewable Resource PPA to gain full understanding of ESS-related
            requirements. ESS BTA Bidders must also reference the pro forma BTA and conform to GPC’s
            Minimum Technical Requirements.
            PART 1       DEFINITIONS
            For purposes of this Exhibit L, each of the following terms has the corresponding assigned
            meaning:
            Cycle: The equivalent charge of Storage Device Operating Energy (in MWhs) from 0% to 100%
            and subsequent discharge from 100% to 0%, regardless of whether the complete charge or
            complete discharge occurs during one or more charges or discharges. For daily Cycle
            determinations, the Day in which the relevant discharging occurs will include the discharging in the
            Cycle determination for that day, regardless of when the charging occurred.
            Round-Trip Efficiency (RTE): The amount of energy received from the ESS at the POI divided by
            the original amount of energy that was used to charge the ESS at the POI.
            Storage Device Design Capacity: The guaranteed amount of ESS storage capacity allocated to
            GPC under the PPA, as will be designated in the PPA.
            Storage Device Discharge Duration: The guaranteed number of hours that the ESS must be
            capable of continuously discharging to the POI at the Storage Device Design Capacity.
            Storage Device Operating Energy (SDOE): The guaranteed number of MWh that the ESS must
            be capable of discharging to the POI and is equal to the product of the Storage Device Design
            Capacity multiplied by the Storage Device Discharge Duration.
            Storage Performance Reduction (SPR): As defined in the pro forma Standalone ESS PPA or pro
            forma ESS with Renewable Resource PPA.
            PART 2       OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR ESS FACILITIES
            2.1     In addition to the requirements of RFP Section 2.4 (ESS Submissions), an ESS Facility must meet
            the following requirements:
               A. Facility control system must be capable of communicating bidirectionally with GPC’s AGC system,
               including:
                  (i)    Charging and discharging in response to GPC’s 6-second AGC signals;
                  (ii)   Operating continuously on AGC for both charging and discharging of the ESS;
                  (iii) Operating manually in response to scheduling communications if AGC signals are interrupted
                  for any reason; and
                  (iv) Sending and receiving all AGC-related signal data (see RFP Section 3.5.1 (AGC) for details)
                  and responding as required by GPC.
               B. The Facility must include control system updates, logic upgrades, connections, and other
               alterations, as requested by GPC, and must be capable of monitoring and controlling the energy flows
               from and to each Facility component.
               C. The ESS must: (i) be capable of Grid charging from the Southern Company Transmission System;
               and (ii) meet all specifications listed for inverter-based generator interconnections on OASIS
               (http://www.oasis.oati.com/SOCO/).

            PART 3     ADDITIONAL OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR AN ESS WITH RENEWABLE
                       RESOURCE FACILITY
            3.1    In addition to meeting the requirements of Part 2 (Operational Requirements for ESS Facilities) of
            this Exhibit L, an ESS with Renewable Resource Facility must be capable of:
               A. Charging and discharging using Renewable Energy in response to GPC’s 6-second AGC signals;
               and
               B. Charging from the Southern Company Transmission System or the Renewable Resource in
               response to GPC’s AGC signals.
            3.2     The Renewable Resource must be: (i) sized to fully-charge the ESS; and (ii) capable of operating
            continuously in response to GPC’s AGC signals for GPC to direct the Renewable Energy. For a Facility
            that includes a Renewable Resource, GPC prefers that the Renewable Resource be AC coupled to the
            ESS. GPC reserves the right to modify the performance metrics for the proposed Facility if Bidder
            proposes a Facility that is DC coupled. GPC will have exclusive rights to the energy output of the
            Renewable Resource and the ESS at no additional cost to GPC (i.e., Seller will not receive any variable
            payment for the Renewable Energy). Seller’s Annual Capacity Payment represents all compensation
            owed to Seller for all Facility capacity and energy delivered during the Annual Period.

            PART 4     CAPACITY AND DISPATCH REQUIREMENTS FOR PPA BIDS
            4.1    Over the PPA Term, the ESS must:
               A. Discharge at the guaranteed Storage Device Design Capacity (SDDC) at the guaranteed Storage
               Device Discharge Duration, which must be at least four hours;
               B. Be on AGC and available for charging or dispatch on a 24-hour daily basis except during pre-
               approved scheduled maintenance outages; and
               C. Be capable of at least 365 Cycles per Annual Period, and Cycles will be limited to a maximum of
               two Cycles in any Day.
            4.2    GPC will evaluate the guaranteed Storage Device Design Capacity (SDDC) based on the ESS’s
            charging ability and ability to continuously discharge to the POI for the Storage Device Discharge Duration
            each Day over the PPA Term. GPC is not responsible for any degradation of the ESS over the PPA Term,
            and either Party may request a performance test to demonstrate the performance capability of the ESS.
            4.3   The maximum delivered energy from the ESS or the Renewable Resource, separately or
            combined, to the POI, at one time, may not exceed the Interconnection Limit.
            4.4    There will be a tolling arrangement for grid charging. GPC will provide all grid energy, excluding
            Station Service, required for grid charging a Standalone ESS or an ESS with Renewable Resource in
            accordance with the applicable pro forma PPA. There will be no cost to GPC for tolled grid energy. Seller
            must separately procure any energy needed for Station Service, including, if required, a metered retail
            service connection to GPC or another provider.

            PART 5     STORAGE PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS
            5.1    GPC will evaluate ESS performance monthly based on two components:
               A. Energy Storage Performance Metric. This metric will compare the actual daily availability of the
               ESS to store energy, including both grid energy and Renewable Energy, in an amount equivalent to the
               guaranteed Storage Device Operating Energy. See the pro forma PPAs for details.
               B. Charge/Discharge Rate Performance Metric. This metric will compare the daily composite
               charge or discharge rate of the ESS to the guaranteed ESS charge rate or the guaranteed Storage


            ALL-SOURCE RFP                                                                               Page 98 of 115

                                                      www.gonitro.com

STF-JKA-1-24 Attachment A.pdf

                                                                        All-Source Capacity RFP for 2029–2031
                                                                                               RFP Document
                                                                                   Final Approved – Revision 1


               Device Design Capacity. See the pro forma PPAs for additional details.
            5.2    These two metrics will be averaged to produce the “Monthly Storage Performance Metric.” See
            the pro forma PPAs for additional details.

            PART 6     ROUNDTRIP EFFICIENCY PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENT
            6.1   The Round-Trip Efficiency Performance Metric will be determined by comparing actual Monthly
            RTE to the guaranteed RTE.
            6.2     Each PPA Bidder must include in its Bid a guaranteed RTE of the ESS. Actual installed RTE will
            be confirmed by third party-certified testing before Commercial Operation to confirm actual RTE is greater
            than the guaranteed RTE (e.g., if the guaranteed RTE is 86%, the actual RTE must be 86% or greater).
            6.3    GPC will track actual achieved RTE monthly for all stored energy. This RTE will be calculated by
            dividing stored energy for the month delivered to the POI by the energy input into the ESS.
            6.4   If, for a month, the measured RTE for stored energy that reaches the POI is below the guaranteed
            RTE by more than one percentage point (e.g., the measured RTE of 84% for a Facility with an 86%
            guaranteed RTE would have a measured RTE that is two percentage points below the guaranteed RTE),
            GPC will calculate a “Monthly RTE Adjustment” from: (i) the stored energy; (ii) the percent that actual
            Monthly RTE is below the guaranteed RTE; (iii) and GPC’s Associated Interchange Energy Rate (AIER).
            6.5   The Monthly RTE Adjustment will be subtracted from the Monthly Capacity Payment after the
            Storage Performance Reduction is applied.
            6.6    The Monthly RTE Adjustment will be calculated using GPC system incremental cost (i.e., AIER) for
            the stored energy lost due to the measured RTE being below the guaranteed RTE by more than one
            percentage point.

            PART 7     PPA PAYMENTS FOR ESS CAPACITY AND ENERGY
            7.1    For each PPA Annual Period, GPC will pay to Seller a fixed “Annual Capacity Price,” which will
            be stated in the PPA. The Annual Capacity Price will be: (i) all compensation owed by GPC to Seller under
            the PPA; and (ii) subject to reduction for Seller failure to achieve performance guarantees, as will be
            described in the applicable pro forma PPA. The Annual Capacity Price will be prorated by application of
            Monthly Value Factors and paid monthly (“Monthly Capacity Payment”), as may be reduced in
            accordance with the PPA.
            7.2  As applicable, GPC will reduce the payment to Seller by subtracting from the Monthly Capacity
            Payment: (i) the Storage Performance Reduction; and (ii) the RTE Performance Adjustment.

            PART 8     ANNUAL RENEWABLE ENERGY PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENT (ESS WITH
                       RENEWABLE RESOURCE ONLY)
            8.1    After the conclusion of each Annual Period, GPC will compare the Renewable Energy that was
            available for the Annual Period against the Seller’s binding annual Renewable Energy forecast (“Annual
            Renewable Energy Forecast”) to calculate an annual Renewable Energy performance adjustment. (see
            the pro forma ESS with Renewable Energy PPA for additional information)
            8.2    If the Renewable Energy available for an Annual Period is less than 90% of the Annual Renewable
            Energy Forecast, then a “Renewable Energy Performance True-up” will be calculated by GPC as
            detailed in the PPA to recover from Seller up to 50% of the sum of the Monthly Capacity Payments that
            GPC paid during the Annual Period.

                       EXHIBIT M – ENVIRONMENTAL SITE ASSESSMENT REQUIREMENTS

          PART 1 ALL BIDS.
          From an environmental perspective, and in GPC’s view, the best property for siting generation is property
          that has been comprehensively evaluated and determined to either have no past or present environmental
          concerns, or if concerns are identified, they can be avoided through generation technology or Site
          configuration. Where environmental impacts are possible, it is necessary to fully address impacts through
          avoidance, minimization, regulatory permitting, and compliance, and, possibly, mitigation.

          Each Bid will consider and address, at a minimum, the items outlined below. If Bidder does not believe an
          item is applicable to its Project, Bidder must provide a statement as to why.

                1. Waters of the U.S.
                2. State waters (where applicable)
                3. 100-Year Floodplains
                4. NPDES Construction Stormwater Permitting
                5. Federal and State Protected Species and Species of Special Concern
                6. Cultural Resources (Archaeology and Historical Architecture)
                7. Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasures (SPCC) Compliance
                8. Any contamination or potentially contaminated soil or groundwater (A Phase I Environmental Site
                   Assessment may be required)
                9. Air Quality requirements (including construction and development related considerations, e.g.,
                   permitting of timber/other open burning, as well as air pre-construction and operating permit
                   requirements, etc.)
                10. Local government permitting, ordinances, and restrictions
          With each Bid submittal, Bidder must provide a notarized Environmental Compliance Affidavit found in
          Exhibit N (Environmental Compliance Affidavit).

          PART 2 ENVIRONMENTAL ASSURANCES DUE AFTER BID ADVANCES TO CONFORMING LIST
          GPC requires assurances from each Bidder that due diligence concerning the protection of project-related
          environmental factors has been conducted and will continue to be observed throughout the PPA Term, until
          Closing of an APA, or until completion of Seller’s obligations under a BTA, as applicable. Efforts must be
          made by Bidder to avoid environmental impacts, but where impacts are unavoidable, efforts must be made
          by Bidder to minimize and mitigate environmental impacts accordingly. Therefore, Bidder is required at a
          minimum to address the above factors with its Bid to allow GPC to independently assess what potential
          environmental impacts may result from construction and operation of the Facility. Bidder must submit
          Environmental Assurances after its Bid advances to the Conforming List. Failure to address the items below
          will result in an incomplete Bid and possibility of rejection.

                                   EXHIBIT O – FACILITY TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
          PART 1       WINTERIZATION REQUIREMENTS
          1.1    Each Submission must comply with the following requirements:
             A. The Facility must comply with applicable EOP-012-1 (Extreme Cold Weather Preparedness and
             Operations) requirements, including Requirements R1 (applicable to New Facilities), R2 (applicable to Existing
             Facilities), R3, R4, R5, R6, and R7. EOP-012-1 (Extreme Cold Weather Preparedness and Operations) is
             published by NERC and available at: https://www.nerc.com/pa/Stand/Reliability%20Standards/EOP-012-1.pdf.
             B. Bidder must provide, by no later than Bid Due Date the Facility’s: (i) extreme cold weather temperature; and
             (ii) cold weather preparedness plan.
          PART 2       CYBERSECURITY
          2.1    Each Facility must comply with the requirements for Bulk Electric System generation facilities in North
          America set forth in the NERC reliability standards (Cyber Security Standards) created pursuant to FERC order
          706 (Mandatory Reliability Standards for Critical Infrastructure Protection) and any other cyber security best
          practices consistent with Prudent Industry Practices.
          2.2    For all BESS Submissions, programmable electronic components of the: (i) Battery Management System
          (BMS); (ii) BESS Controller; and (iii) Site Controller (including controls, hardware and software) must not be sourced
          from or manufactured by Foreign Entities of Concern (“FEOC”) as defined in 42 U.S.C. § 18741(5) and
          subsequently interpreted in “Interpretation of Foreign Entity of Concern,” 89 Fed. Reg. 37085 (May 6, 2024) or
          sourced from or manufactured in one of the following countries: China, Russia, North Korea, Saudi Arabia, Serbia,
          Algeria, Venezuela, Iran, Iraq, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Syria, Lebanon, South Sudan,
          Pakistan, or Cuba. For purposes of this provision, the terms Battery Management System, BESS Controller, and
          Site Controller are defined as follows:
             A. Battery Management System (BMS): A control system used to protect the battery and to provide
             key parameters, such as state of charge, battery health, and temperature.
             B. BESS Controller: A controller used to manage multiple stacks or arrays of batteries. This controller
             manages the balancing of the batteries.
             C. Site Controller: A control system used to manage one or more sources (Photovoltaic solar,
             batteries, etc.) to achieve facility level control.
          PART 3       ADDITIONAL MINIMUM FACILITY TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR ESS FACILITIES
          3.1     PPA Bids for Facilities utilizing solar photovoltaic modules as a Renewable Resource must meet the
          following requirements:
             A. Hydrology and Site drainage
                (i)    Site grading must ensure positive drainage of the Site.
                (ii)   Site design must ensure no flooding, no standing water, and no increase in flows offsite.
                (iii) The drainage design must be based on a 100-year, 24-hour rain event.
                (iv) No portion of the Facility may be located in a floodplain without the proper permit(s) from the appropriate
                Governmental Authority.
                (v) The construction contract scope must include responsibility of contractor to close out the National
                Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit.


             B. Site grading and stabilization
                (i)    Measures must be in place to prevent sediment loss.
                (ii)   Permanent site vegetation and site stabilization must be completed before demobilizing.

                 devices of each measurement type must be provided.
                 (iii) For Facilities using bifacial modules, an albedometer must be provided for each GHI pyranometer.
                 (iv) At minimum two soiling stations utilizing full sized modules must be provided.


            L. Testing
                 (i) Operational test, performance ratio test, and capacity test (ASTM Based) must be performed for PV
                 facilities.
                 (ii)   Additional testing, if required under the Interconnection Agreement, must also be performed.
                 (iii) NERC testing must be performed for facilities defined as a Bulk Electric System (BES).


            M. Main Power Transformer
                 (i)    Transformers must be capable of meeting 100% of Facility output using 100% ONAN-cooling.
                 (ii)   Transformer suppliers must be subject to review and approval by GPC.
                 (iii) A design review prior to ordering materials utilizing third-party transformer design consultant must be
                 approved by GPC.
                 (iv) RIS-type bushings are preferred.

                                                                         All-Source Capacity RFP for 2029–2031

                                                                                    Final Approved – Revision 1
              (v)    Transformers must be designed with a 25% temporary emergency overload.
              (vi) Transformer overload capability must be unlimited by components (i.e., bushing ratings, DETC rating,
              etc.)
              (vii) The transformer tank design must be in accordance with IEEE C57.156 Table 1 to mitigate tank rupture
              in the event of a high-energy arcing fault internal to the tank.
            N. Facility Substation
              (i) Facility substations must meet safety requirements of the NESC-2023 and comply with the design
              principles set forth ASCE 7, ASCE 113, IEEE 605, and IEEE 80.
              (ii)   Facility substations must be commissioned to NETA ATS 17 standards.
              (iii) All bus and cable sizes must be designed with a maximum operating temperature of 80 °C with a 40
              °C ambient, with no sun and 2 ft/s wind.
              (iv) Spatial separation from oil-filled electrical equipment must be compliant with IEEE 979-2012.
              (v) All equipment suppliers, protection and control designs and settings, and grounding design/modeling
              must be subject to review.


            O. SCADA
              (i) The design must provide a real-time data link for remote operation (using Ignition) by Southern
              Monitoring and Diagnostic Center and also provide a feed to system-wide historian data collection (Pi).
              These data links can be directly from the site controller or from a separate SCADA controller.
              (ii)   The data link preference is OPC DA, DNP, or Modbus.
              (iii) The real time data must include inverters, solar details, MET station (if applicable), breakers, meters,
              and site controller. Solar details to pass data down to string or the lowest level possible.
              (iv) Site controller, battery management system (if applicable) and inverters time must be synchronized to
              a local time clock. The preference is to time sync with any devices that can take a remote time sync.
              (v)    Local Human Machine Interface platform must be Ignition by Inductive Automation.
            P. Cyber Security
              (i) Equipment providers and site design must comply with NERC CIP policies as well as the Southern
              Company Cyber Security Policy, which will be made available to Bidders upon their submission of an intention
              to Bid a Build Transfer Facility by the date set forth in the Solicitation Schedule.
            Q. End-of Life Disposal
              (i) The Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) testing procedure and results for modules must
              be submitted.
              (ii)   Description of the end-of-life disposal/recycling plan must be provided.

                         SCHEDULE OF DEFINED TERMS AND RULES OF CONSTRUCTION


         This 2023 RFP uses the defined terms identified in this Schedule, or in the body of this 2023 RFP, and
         the rules of construction identified in this Schedule.

         2019 IRP Final Order: The Order from GPC’s 2019 IRP as entered by the Commission in Docket No. 42310.
         2022 IRP: GPC’s 2022 Integrated Resource Plan as approved by the Commission in Docket No. 44160.
         2022 IRP Final Order: The Order from the 2022 IRP as approved by the Commission in Docket No. 44160.
         2023 RFP: This CARES 2023 Utility Scale Request for Proposals for Renewable Generation.
         2025 RFP: GPC’s planned CARES 2025 Utility Scale Request for Proposals for Renewable Generation.
         AC: Alternating current.
         Access Route: The suitable all-weather access route from the nearest public roadway to the Point of
         Interconnection that is acceptable to GPC and that must be always available to GPC (24/7/365(366))
         throughout the IA term to facilitate GPC’s construction, operation, or maintenance of the Interconnection
         Facilities or other related GPC activity.
         Affected System: An Electric System utility other than the Southern Company Transmission System or an
         electric facility owner whose facilities require additions, modifications, or upgrades that are necessary for safe
         and reliable operation of the Electric System during parallel operation of the Facility, other than those required
         due to GPC’s designation of the Facility output to serve GPC’s customers (i.e., to deliver the Energy from the
         Point of Delivery to GPC’s customers).
         Affected System Upgrade: Any addition, modification, or upgrade to an Affected System’s Electric System
         that would be necessary for safe and reliable operation of the Electric System during parallel operation of the
         Facility. Each addition, modification, or upgrade will be constructed and owned by that Affected System.
         Affiliate: For any specific Person, any other Person directly or indirectly controlling, controlled by, or under
         common control with that Person. For purposes of this definition, “control” when used regarding any entity
         means the power to direct the management and policies of the entity, directly or indirectly, whether through
         ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise. A Person directly or indirectly owning 50% or more
         of the outstanding stock or other equity interest of a Person has “control” of that Person; the terms “controlling”
         and “controlled” have meanings correlative to “control.”
         Affiliate Bid Team: As set forth in Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(d), any GPC Affiliate (e.g., Southern
         Power Company) that intends to submit a Bid into this 2023 RFP, as well as any other Persons acting for that
         Affiliate or on its behalf in support of the development and submission of any Bid.
         AGC: See Automatic Generation Control.
         AGC Requirements: The AGC performance and technical requirements for AGC as set forth in the applicable
         pro forma PPA or pro forma BTA, as applicable.
         Alabama Power: Alabama Power Company, a regulated electric utility GPC Affiliate that is also a subsidiary
         of Southern Company.
         Annual Energy Contract Amount: The Annual Energy Contract Amount, as defined in each of the pro forma
         PPAs in MWh for any identified Annual Period reflected in the pro forma PPAs.
         Annual Period: Any one of a succession of consecutive 12-Month periods during the PPA Term or the Facility
         Design Life, the first which will begin on the first Day of the Month following the COD or Closing, as applicable,
         except that if Commercial Operation or Closing is achieved on the first Day of a Month, the first Day of the first
         Annual Period is the COD or Closing, as applicable.
         Asset Purchase Agreement or APA: The Asset Purchase agreement to be entered into by GPC and a
         Winning Bidder (or other Person identified as APA counterparty (i.e., Seller) as allowed by this 2023 RFP)
         proposing an Existing Facility that: (i) utilizes solar photovoltaic (fixed or tracking) as the Renewable Resource;
         (ii) does not include a Storage Device; (iii) interconnects to the STT; and (iv) is located in the state of Georgia,
         in the form of the pro forma APA attached as Exhibit L (Pro Forma APA) to this 2023 RFP.

         ASC: The FASB Accounting Standards Codification.
         Automatic Generation Control or AGC: The automatic control of a facility’s output performed within the
         balancing authority, with the purpose of balancing load and generation or implementing curtailments. This is
         achieved through the electric generation or storage facility’s capability of accepting a set point electronically
         and the automatic adjustment and regulation of the facility’s output to meet that set point.
         Avoided Energy Cost: For each hour of a given month, the amount, in dollars per megawatt-hour ($/MWh)
         that is equal to the avoided cost of generation on the GPC territorial system for each hour of that month.
         Avoided Energy Cost can include the costs associated with avoided fuel costs, avoided variable operations
         and maintenance costs, avoided environmental compliance costs, and avoided transmission energy losses.
         Awarded Contract: An executed PPA, APA, or BTA, as applicable, between GPC and a Seller (i.e., Winning
         Bidder).

         one or more SWAC Reference Benchmarks.
         Best Cost Threshold: The threshold selected through the Best Cost Analysis that GPC will use to determine
         which Bids and Company-Owned Proposals are Economically Competitive Submissions.

         2023 RFP.

         by the Bidder are stored and a record of all communications are recorded.

         with the guidelines of this 2023 RFP and Commission Rules).
         Bid Period: The period from the Bid Period Open Date until the Bid Due Date, as shown in the Solicitation
         Schedule.
         Bid Security: Security provided by Bidder for each Bid advanced to the Competitive Tier, as further described
         in Section 4.4 (Bid Security).
         Bidder: As applicable, each Person contemplating submission of a Bid or submitting a Bid into this 2023 RFP.
         Bidders’ Conference: The conference held with GPC, Staff, and the IE for potential Participants and
         interested Persons to learn about the 2023 RFP Process and the draft RFP Documents.
         Build Transfer Agreement or BTA: The Build Transfer Agreement to be entered into by GPC and a Winning
         Bidder (or other Person identified as BTA counterparty as allowed by this 2023 RFP) regarding a Build Transfer
         Facility, in the form of the pro forma BTA attached as Exhibit M (Pro Forma BTA) to this 2023 RFP.
         Build Transfer Facility: A Facility that is a Utility Scale Renewable Resource that: (i) uses solar photovoltaic
         (fixed or tracking) as the Renewable Resource; (ii) does not include a Storage Device; (iii) is transferred to
         GPC on or after mechanical completion but prior to energization; (iv) interconnects to the STT; and (v) is
         located in the state of Georgia.
         Business Day: Any Day excluding Saturday, Sunday, and any Day on which banking institutions in Atlanta,
         Georgia, are closed because of a federal holiday.
         CARES: The Clean and Renewable Energy Subscription program approved pursuant to the 2022 IRP Final Order.
         CARES ED Program: The Clean and Renewable Energy Subscription economic development program
         approved pursuant to the 2022 IRP Final Order.

         Storage Device: An Energy storage device (e.g., a battery) that connects to the same POI as the Renewable

         Device under normal operation, as identified in Exhibit F (Facility Description and Site) of Exhibit K-2 (Pro
         Forma Energy with Storage Power Purchase Agreement), which is the product of the Storage Device Design
         Capacity and the Storage Device Discharge Duration.

         Capacity continuously over at least two hours; (iv) will maintain its Storage Device Design Capacity and its

                         CARES 2023 Utility Scale Request for Proposals for
                                               Renewable Generation


         Georgia Power Company issues this 2023 RFP to continue the expansion of renewable development for the
         benefit of GPC’s customers. The cornerstone of this 2023 RFP is the Clean and Renewable Energy
         Subscription (“CARES”) program through which GPC will offer subscriptions to renewable energy to
         commercial and industrial customers. Within the CARES program, GPC will also offer a program specifically
         designed for customers seeking around the clock carbon free energy from carbon free resources (“CFE-ATC”)
         that leverage renewable resources with battery storage systems.

         Through the leadership of the Commission, GPC has advanced the development of renewable resources in
         the state of Georgia and has continued to grow one of the largest voluntary renewable procurement programs
         in the country. GPC remains dedicated to adding renewable resources to its generation portfolio in a clean,
         safe, reliable, and cost-effective manner.

         On July 21, 2022, the Commission issued its 2022 IRP Final Order concerning the 2022 IRP. The 2022 IRP
         Final Order amended and approved the Stipulation that included the directive to procure energy from up to
         approximately 2,100 MWs of Utility Scale Renewable Resources, including energy from up to 650 MWs of
         CFE-ATC Resources. GPC also plans to roll forward 1,250 MW left unfilled from previous utility scale
         procurements for a total target of 3,350 MW to be procured. GPC will issue at least two requests for proposals
         to meet these requirements.

         This 2023 RFP seeks to procure Renewable Energy from approximately 2,875 MWs of Utility Scale Renewable
         Resources, with anticipated in-service dates of 2026, 2027, or 2028, including up to 650 MWs of Renewable
         Energy from CFE-ATC Resources. The second request for proposals, the 2025 RFP, is expected to be issued
         in 2025 to procure the balance of the target for Utility Scale Renewable Resources. In addition to the
         Renewable Energy under this 2023 RFP and the 2025 RFP, GPC may procure additional Utility Scale
         Renewable Resources, that are not CFE-ATC Resources, for the CARES ED Program.

                      1.3.1. Standards of Conduct Regarding Affiliate Bids. A GPC Affiliate may submit Bids in

                      segregate the Evaluation Team and any Affiliate Bid Team. The lists identifying the Evaluation
                      Team and, if applicable, Affiliate Bid Team members are found on the Commission’s website under
                      Docket No. 45084, and on the “Documents” page of the IE Website. Each Participant is
                      encouraged to review these lists. Except when communication is facilitated by Staff and monitored
                      by the IE, each Participant is prohibited from discussing this 2023 RFP and any related documents
                      with the Evaluation Team. GPC has implemented specific controls to ensure RFP-related
                      information is confined to the appropriate team. Additionally, before receipt of Bids, GPC, Staff,
                      and the IE will implement procedural steps to ensure that all Bids from Affiliate Bid Teams and from
                      non-Affiliates are evaluated using a common methodology applied in a manner that ensures that
                      any Affiliate Bid Team Bid does not receive any advantage in the evaluation. In all instances, an
                      Affiliate Bid Team will be treated as a third-party Participant.

         PART 2.      RENEWABLE ENERGY PRODUCTS SOUGHT; FACILITY OWNERSHIP STRUCTURES; AND
                      TYPES OF FACILITIES

               2.1.   Renewable Energy Products Sought in this 2023 RFP.
                      2.1.1. Renewable Energy from Utility Scale Renewable Resources (other than CFE-ATC
                      Resources). GPC seeks to procure Renewable Energy from Utility Scale Renewable Resources
                      that are not CFE-ATC Resources. Utility Scale Renewable Resources may include a Storage
                      Device. The procurement of Renewable Energy from Utility Scale Renewable Resources under
                      this Section 2.1.1 (Renewable Energy from Utility Scale Renewable Resources) constitutes a
                      separate and distinct procurement from that set forth in Section 2.1.2 (Renewable Energy from
                      CFE-ATC Resources).

                      2.1.2. Renewable Energy from CFE-ATC Resources. GPC seeks to procure around the clock
                      carbon free Renewable Energy from CFE-ATC Resources. After receiving all Bids for CFE-ATC
                      Resources, GPC will establish a price that it can offer to CFE-ATC Applicants for a subscription in
                      the CFE-ATC Program. If a CFE-ATC Applicant agrees to the established pricing and executes a
                      CFE-ATC Customer Agreement, GPC will proceed with reviewing the Bidder’s Bid as part of the
                      Competitive Tier for advancement to the Short List. If no CFE-ATC Applicant executes a CFE-ATC
                      Customer Agreement, then Bids for CFE-ATC Resources will be placed on the Release List.
                      However, CFE-ATC Bids placed on the Release List will not affect GPC’s evaluation of any
                      Alternative Bid or Additional Bid submitted by Bidder under Section 6.3.2 (CFE-ATC Resource
                      Bids). The procurement of Renewable Energy from CFE-ATC Resources under this Section 2.1.2
                      (Renewable Energy from CFE-ATC Resources) constitutes a separate and distinct procurement
                      from that set forth in Section 2.1.1 (Renewable Energy from Utility Scale Renewable Resources).

               2.2.   Facility Ownership Structures That May Be Bid into This 2023 RFP. As further summarized
                      in Exhibit N (Summary of Ownership, Types of Facilities, and Awarded Contracts), Bidders may
                      submit Bids proposing one of two Facility ownership structures:

                      2.2.1. Seller Owned Facilities. GPC will accept Bids for Facilities comprising Utility Scale
                      Renewable Resources (including CFE-ATC Resources) where Bidder will maintain ownership of
                      the Facility. The Awarded Contract that a Winning Bidder would execute with GPC would be a PPA
                      where GPC would have exclusive rights to all of the Renewable Energy produced by the Facility.
                      A Bid for a PPA may be for: (i) a single, unique Facility comprised of a single Renewable Resource;
                      (ii) a Facility that combines resource options into a single unique Facility (e.g., a wind and solar
                      combination); but each Renewable Resource must individually meet the size requirements set
                      forth in the definition of Generating Capacity of Renewable Resource; (iii) Facilities that are either
                      mutually exclusive or contingent upon one another; (iv) a Facility comprised of a Utility Scale
                      Renewable Resource without a Storage Device; or (v) a Facility comprised of a Utility Scale
                      Renewable Resource with a Storage Device so long as it is capable of meeting the Storage Device
                      (non-CFE-ATC) Requirements, or in the case of a Bid for a Facility comprising a CFE-ATC
                      Resource, capable of meeting the CFE-ATC Requirements; or

                      2.2.2. GPC Owned Facilities. GPC will accept Bids for Facilities comprising Utility Scale
                      Renewable Resources that are not CFE-ATC Resources where Bidder proposes transfer of
                      Facility ownership to GPC. The Awarded Contract that a Winning Bidder would execute with GPC
                      would be an APA or a BTA. Any Bidder desiring to submit a Bid for an APA or a BTA, must inform
                      the IE of this election by no later than the date set forth in the Solicitation Schedule. Bidder will be
                      asked to provide to the IE information regarding its proposed Bid. The IE will research and review
                      the potential Bid and discuss findings with Staff and the Evaluation Team, as applicable.
                      Thereafter, the IE will advise Bidder whether or not it may submit a Bid for an APA or a BTA based
                      on the information submitted to the IE. Additional information regarding APA and BTA Facility Bids,
                      including the form of submission of an indication of interest in submitting an APA or BTA Facility
                      Bid, is available on the IE Website.

                           with Storage PPA), or Exhibit K-3 (Pro Forma CFE-ATC PPA), depending on (a) whether the Facility
                           includes a Storage Device; and (b) whether the Facility being proposed would be a CFE-ATC
                           Resource.

                      Environmental Attributes and Electrical Products associated with the Energy throughout the PPA

                      2.4.1. Inclusion in Environmental Attributes. Environmental Attributes include any
                      environmental attribute that could qualify or does qualify for application toward compliance with
                      any local, state, federal, or international renewable energy portfolio standard, green pricing
                      program, renewable energy program, carbon reduction or greenhouse gas reduction initiative,
                      electricity savings program, licensing requirement, verification or certification procedure, federal
                      contract, or other environmental program, incentive, mandate, or objective, in each case whether
                      voluntary or mandatory, and whether created by applicable law or by any Governmental Authority,
                      partnership, coalition, advisory committee, or independent certification board, group, or scientific
                      panel. Environmental Attributes include the exclusive right to report those Environmental Attribute
                      to any Governmental Authority or other Person.

                      2.4.2. Exclusion from Environmental Attributes. Environmental Attributes do not include:
                      (i) any federal, state, or local tax attribute arising from ownership of the Facility, including
                      investment tax credit, production tax credit, or depreciation deduction; (ii) any grant in lieu of
                      investment tax credit or any similar financial payment or grant with respect to the Facility; or (iii) the
                      metered electric Energy produced by the Facility.

               2.5.   Augmentation for CFE-ATC Resources. Each Bid proposing a Facility as a CFE-ATC Resource
                      must include in the Bid price all augmentation costs of both the Renewable Resource and the
                      Storage Device to ensure the CFE-ATC Requirements are met for the duration of the PPA Term.

               2.6.   Remaining Capacity from CFE-ATC Resources. Any capacity remaining after the capacity from
                      the procurement of Renewable Energy from CFE-ATC Resources has been allocated to GPC’s
                      customers under the CFE-ATC Customer Agreements will be allocated to customers in the
                      Existing Load, New Load, and MUSH (as each of these terms are set forth in the 2022 IRP),
                      portions of the CARES program. Any further capacity remaining but left unallocated will be used
                      to serve all GPC retail customers. For example, if GPC procures only 500 MWs of CFE-ATC
                      Resources, then the remaining 150 MWs would be allocated to customers in other portions of the
                      CARES program.


         PART 3.      KEY PROJECT REQUIREMENTS

               3.1.   PPA Term, Facility Design Life, RCOD, and RCD.
                      3.1.1. PPA Term and Facility Design Life. GPC will consider Bids for: (i) PPAs in the form of
                      Exhibit K-1 (Pro Forma Energy Only PPA) or Exhibit K-3 (Pro Forma CFE-ATC PPA) with a PPA
                      Term of 15, 20, 25, or 30 Annual Periods, at Bidder’s option; (ii) PPAs in the form of Exhibit K-2
                      (Pro Forma Energy with Storage PPA) with a PPA Term of 15, 20, or 25 Annual Periods, at Bidder’s
                      option; (iii) APAs for Existing Facilities with a Facility Design Life of 15, 20, 25, or 30 Annual
                      Periods; or (iv) BTAs for Build Transfer Facilities with a Facility Design Life of no fewer than 30
                      Annual Periods, at Bidder’s option. Once a Bid has been submitted and following the Bid Due
                      Date, Bidder will not be allowed to change the PPA Term length or the Facility Design Life, as
                      applicable. For purposes of evaluation, GPC will evaluate the Bids pursuant to the methodology
                      outlined in Exhibit I (Overview of Bid Evaluation).

                      3.1.2. RCOD and RCD. Pursuant to the 2022 IRP Final Order, GPC is seeking to procure
                      Renewable Energy from Utility Scale Renewable Resources (including CFE-ATC Resources)
                      designed to obtain in-service dates in 2026, 2027, and 2028. Each Bidder must indicate the RCOD

               3.2.   Facility Size and Output
                      3.2.1. Facility Size Parameters. GPC will accept Bids for Facilities where the Generating
                      Capacity of the Renewable Resource is no less than 6 MWs and Bidders may not aggregate
                      Renewable Resources to meet that minimum size requirement. However, a Bidder may combine
                      Renewable Resources into a single unique Bid (e.g., a wind and solar combination) where: (i) the
                      Renewable Resources are located on the same Site; (ii) the Renewable Resources have the same
                      Point of Delivery; and (iii) the Generating Capacity of each Renewable Resource, individually, is
                      at least 6 MW. In consultation with Staff and IE, GPC may request that Bidder resize the Facility
                      so that GPC can obtain the best portfolio for its customers. At the time of Bid submission, Bidder
                      must identify how much it would agree to reduce the size of the Facility without changing the Bid
                      price. If GPC will only award a PPA, APA, or BTA, to a Bidder if the Facility is resized, and Bidder
                      refuses to resize the Facility, the Bid will be placed on the Release List and the Bid Security will
                      be returned to Bidder. For Facilities that do not include a Storage Device, Bidders should also
                      indicate whether the Site is suitable for the addition of one or more energy storage system(s) in
                      the future (with or without increasing the Facility’s Interconnection Limit) and if so, how much space
                      is available. In addition, Bidders should indicate whether they would consider entering into future
                      discussions with GPC should GPC wish to explore the option of adding one or more energy
                      storage system(s) to the Site leveraging the Facility’s Point of Interconnection.

                      3.2.2. No Partial Output Bids. GPC will not accept a Bid that constitutes partial output from a
                      Facility. A Bid must represent the full output of the Facility, which is the full capability of the
                      Renewable Resource, combined with any Storage Device.

               3.3.   Location of Facilities
                      3.3.1.     Facility Location.

                               A.     GPC will accept Bids for Facilities located anywhere in the United States that are
                               seeking PPAs in the form of either Exhibit K-1 (Pro Forma Energy Only Power Purchase
                               Agreement) or Exhibit K-2 (Pro Forma Energy with Storage PPA), provided the Facility can
                               deliver the Energy to GPC pursuant to one of the interconnection options set forth in Exhibit
                               B (Interconnection and Delivery Requirements).
                               B.     GPC will accept Bids for Facilities seeking a PPA in the form of Exhibit K-3 (Pro
                               Forma CFE-ATC Power Purchase Agreement) that interconnect to the STT and are located
                               in the state of Georgia.
                               C.    GPC will accept Bids for Facilities seeking an APA or a BTA that interconnect to the
                               STT and are located in the state of Georgia.
                      3.3.2. List of Substations. Bidders may desire to review the list of substations included in
                      Exhibit B (Interconnection and Delivery Requirements) to obtain additional information regarding
                      certain Georgia ITS substations that may have interconnection capacity within the Southern
                      Transmission Territory.

               3.4.   Transmission Interconnection. Each Bidder is responsible for determining all transmission
                      interconnection and delivery-related rules, practices, and policies with which it must comply, as
                      further detailed in Exhibit B (Interconnection and Delivery Requirements). Each Bid must comply

               3.5.   Station Service. Seller is responsible for all Station Service at Seller’s expense. For a Facility
                      located in Georgia, a Seller must arrange retail electric service for the Facility in accordance with
                      the Georgia Territorial Electric Service Act (O.C.G.A. §§ 46-3-1 through 46-3-15). Seller will

                      and install a separate meter for the service. A Bid must not include energy used for Station Service
                      in its Profile in any hour that reflects negative energy production in the Profile. Any negative MWh
