               3.6.   Automatic Generation Control. Bidders must be familiar with, and all Bids for PPAs and BTAs
                      must comply with the AGC Requirements. For Facilities subject to a PPA, the Facilities must
                      comply with the AGC Requirements throughout the PPA Term.

               3.7.   Energy Storage
                      3.7.1. Storage Device. Any Bidder proposing a Facility that includes a Storage Device must
                      provide in the Bid: (i) a description of the Storage Device; (ii) the Storage Device Design Capacity;
                      (iii) the Storage Device Discharge Duration; (iv) the Storage Device Operating Energy; (v) the
                      Maximum Storage Device ROC Rate (as defined in the pro forma PPA attached as Exhibit K-2
                      (Pro Forma Energy with Storage PPA); (vi) the Cycle Limit of the Storage Device; (vii) the plan to
                      maintain the Storage Device to ensure it performs as evaluated for the PPA Term or Facility Design
                      Life, as applicable; (viii) the Facility’s Profile with the Storage Device; (ix) the total maximum
                      instantaneous Energy output of the Renewable Resource; (x) the total simultaneous maximum
                      Energy output of the Renewable Resource and energy output of the Storage Device combined;
                      and (xi) the corresponding Interconnection Limit.

                      3.7.2.     Storage Requirements for Utility Scale Renewable Resources.

                               A.   CFE-ATC Resource. Any Facility containing a Storage Device that is bid in as a CFE-
                               ATC Resource must meet the CFE-ATC Requirements.
                               B.     Non-CFE-ATC Resources. Any Facility containing a Storage Device that is not being
                               bid in as a CFE-ATC Resource must meet the Storage Device (non-CFE-ATC)
                               Requirements. The maximum output of Energy from such a Facility must be the lesser of: (i)
                               the Interconnection Limit; and (ii) the Generating Capacity of Renewable Resource that
                               Bidder includes in its Bid Form.
                      3.7.3. Storage Guidance. Any Bidder offering a Facility with a Storage Device must thoroughly
                      review all storage guidance provided on the IE Website.

               3.8.   Environmental Compliance. Bidder must cooperate with GPC’s Environmental Affairs

                      Resource without a Storage Device must be capable of providing, and upon GPC’s request Seller
                      will cause the Facility to provide, reactive power support to GPC (i.e., to produce and absorb
                      reactive power) to meet GPC’s voltage schedule requirements specified in The Southern Company
                      Bulk Power Operations Procedure BPO-01 at all real power levels (pushing and pulling), including
                      zero real power. For Facilities consisting of technologies other than inverter-based technology,
                      these requirements will apply only when the Facility is producing real power. For Facilities with
                      inverter-based technology, these requirements will apply at all times, regardless of whether the
                      Facility is producing real power.

         PART 4.      PRICING, FEES, AND SECURITY

               4.1.   PPA and Bid Pricing
                      4.1.1. Levelized or Escalating Pricing. Pricing in the PPA may be a Levelized Price or an
                      Escalating Price. Each Bid must specify Bidder’s pricing election. GPC will consider a Bid
                      proposing two pricing alternatives as one Bid, requiring only one Bid Fee.

                      4.1.2. All-in Price. Bid prices must include all costs that GPC will pay for the Renewable Energy
                      provided under the PPA and must be in dollar figures quoted in nominal terms (i.e., any applicable
                      escalation has already been applied) for the Annual Period in which they occur. Attempts by Bidder
                      to increase its price or impose any other costs to GPC after the Bid is submitted will be grounds
                      for rejection of the Bid. Each proposed Bid price must be in $/MWh and if Bidder is a Winning
                      Bidder, then the proposed price will become the Contract Energy Price (as that term will be set
                      forth in the PPA executed between GPC and a Winning Bidder).

                      4.1.3. Payment for Test Energy. For a new Facility, GPC will pay Seller for test energy delivered
                      prior to the Facility’s Commercial Operation Date. The test energy price is 90% of the Associated
                      Interchange Energy Rate, which, as determined for each hour, is based on the variable dispatch
                      cost of the incremental resources that serve the collective obligations of the Southern Companies.

               4.5.   Winner’s Fee. A portion of the IE cost is covered by the Winner’s Fee assessed upon each
                      winning Bid. The Winner’s Fee will be determined once the final amount of Renewable Energy
                      procured under this 2023 RFP and the total IE costs are known, after winning Bids have been
                      selected. In no event will the total of the Winner’s Fees exceed five hundred thousand dollars
                      ($500,000). The Winner’s Fee is calculated for each winning Bid as the pro rata share for any
                      remaining IE cost not covered by the Bid Fees and is based upon Winning Bidder’s total projected
                      revenue (regardless of whether the revenue is determined on the basis of revenues over the PPA
                      Term for a PPA or based upon the payment of a purchase price pursuant to an APA or BTA)
                      compared to the total projected revenues for all winning Bids. The Winner’s Fee must be paid by
                      a Winning Bidder before GPC will execute the applicable Awarded Contract. If a Company-Owned
                      Proposal advances to the Short List and is submitted to the Commission for certification as
                      described in Section 9.2 (Company-Owned Proposal Certification), GPC will be responsible for
                      its portion of the Winner’s Fee.

                      PPA with a PPA Term of 30 Annual Periods, the total expected revenues during the PPA Term (after
                      COD) will represent the sum of 30 Annual Periods of revenue. This value will be multiplied by 5%
                      to calculate the appropriate amount of Performance Security.

                      of the experience of the principal members of Bidder’s project team; and (iii) information on who
                      will be responsible for design, siting, permitting, financing, constructing, and, in the case of a Bid
                      for a PPA, on-going operation and maintenance of the Facility, if known.

                      agreements imposing requirements to use unionized labor.

               5.6.   Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI). GPC is committed to supporting diversity, equity, and
                      inclusion within GPC’s own decision-making, hiring and promotion, and daily operations, and
                      GPC encourages its counterparties, service providers, consultants, and supply chain vendors to
                      promote similar efforts. GPC encourages projects that use contractors or suppliers that are
                      classified as Certified Diverse Suppliers. To be considered for this non-price factor, Bidders must
                      complete the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Certificate found in Exhibit H (Diversity, Equity, and
                      Inclusion Certificate). More information regarding GPC’s focus on DEI can be found here:
                      https://www.southerncompany.com/sustainability/diversity-equity-inclusion.html.


         PART 6.      BID SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

               6.1.   Bid Form. Each Bid must be submitted via the Bid Form on the IE Website by no later than the
                      date and time specified in the Solicitation Schedule.

               6.2.   Effect of Bid Submission. Bidder’s submission of a Bid to the IE will constitute Bidder’s
                      acknowledgment and acceptance of all terms, conditions, and requirements of this 2023 RFP.
                      Bidders will receive an email acknowledgment of receipt of the Bid Form from the IE Website.

               6.3.   Multiple Bid Submissions.

                      6.3.1. General. Bidder may submit multiple Bids in response to this 2023 RFP. If Bidder submits
                      multiple Bids, each Bid must state clearly whether the Bid is dependent upon another Bid. For
                      example, if Bidder submits multiple Bids for several Sites, but is only willing to develop a limited
                      number of those Facilities or requires a combination of the Bids to be selected together, or some
                      of the Bids are mutually exclusive, these contingencies and limitations must be stated clearly in
                      each affected Bid and made known to GPC as part of the Bid submission and by the Bid Due Date.
                      Bidder may not aggregate multiple Facilities from one or more Sites to meet the minimum MW
                      required to be submitted in this 2023 RFP.

                      6.3.2.     CFE-ATC Resource Bids.

                               A.     Alternative Bids. A Bidder submitting a Bid for a CFE-ATC Resource may also
                               submit, by the Bid Due Date, a separate, mutually exclusive, alternative Bid (“Alternative
                               Bid”). The Alternative Bid must be: (i) a Facility that utilizes the same Site and Point of
                               Delivery as the CFE-ATC Resource; and (ii) a Utility Scale Renewable Resource meeting
                               the Storage Device (non-CFE-ATC) Requirements, or a Utility Scale Renewable Resource
                               without a Storage Device. In that instance Bidder would pay only one Bid Fee. If Bidder’s Bid
                               for a CFE-ATC Resource is placed on the Release List in accordance with Section 2.1.2
                               (Renewable Energy from CFE-ATC Resources), Bidder’s Alternative Bid will be evaluated
                               by GPC for purposes of this 2023 RFP.
                               B.     Additional Bids. If a Bidder who submits a Bid for a CFE-ATC Resource submits an
                               Alternative Bid and submits one or more additional Bids (each an “Additional Bid”) for Utility
                               Scale Renewable Resources that are not CFE-ATC Resources, then Bidder will pay a
                               separate Bid Fee for each Additional Bid. For example, if Bidder submitted a Bid for a CFE-
                               ATC Resource, an Alternative Bid, and an Additional Bid, then Bidder would pay two Bid
                               Fees. The first Bid Fee would be for both the CFE-ATC Resource Bid and the Alternative
                               Bid, and the second Bid Fee would be for the Additional Bid.

               6.4.   Unique Bids. Each Bid must be unique with respect to the PPA Term (for Bids seeking PPAs),
                      Facility location, size, POI, Southern Transmission Interface (if applicable), and any characteristic
                      that would alter the amount or timing of the delivery of Renewable Energy from the Facility (e.g.,
                      tracking capability and panel orientation for solar resources, or inclusion of a Storage Device).
                      For Bid Fee purposes, Bids for PPAs that are identical in all respects, but otherwise offering
                      differing PPA Term lengths, are considered a single Bid.

               6.5.   Bid Release Date. Each Bid submitted for consideration must remain valid until the earlier of:
                      (i) the date it is released by GPC; (ii) the date it is withdrawn by Bidder, subject to Bidder’s loss
                      of its Bid Security, if applicable; or (iii) the date on which GPC files the applicable Awarded
                      Contract with the Commission, which events are projected to occur in accordance with the
                      Solicitation Schedule.

               6.6.   Required Supporting Documents. In addition to providing all information required by the Bid
                      Form, Bidder must complete and submit each of the following documents with its Bid by the Bid
                      Due Date for the Bid to be considered complete. Any Bid that does not satisfy all requirements of
                      this 2023 RFP may be considered nonresponsive. GPC, in consultation with the IE and Staff, may
                      choose to reject nonresponsive Bids from further consideration.

                      6.6.1. Conformance of Pro Forma PPAs, APA, or BTA. After the Commission approves the
                      terms and conditions of the pro forma PPAs, and the pro forma APA and BTA, no substantive or
                      material change will be allowed. GPC will only consider non-material clarifications or Facility- and
                      Site-specific changes to the pro forma PPAs and pro forma APA and BTA. Conforming changes
                      may only be proposed through a mark-up of the pro forma PPA, APA, or BTA, as applicable,
                      submitted by Bidder. The mark-up must include: (i) a “red-lined version” of the Commission-
                      approved pro forma PPA, APA, or BTA, as applicable, reflecting any and all proposed changes by
                      showing the specific additions (bold and underlined) or deletions (strike-through) that Bidder
                      requires in order to enter into the PPA, APA or BTA; (ii) a separate document explaining each
                      change; and (iii) a statement confirming that the substantive terms and conditions of the pro forma
                      PPA, APA, or BTA, as applicable, are acceptable to Bidder. GPC will not consider any material or
                      substantive exception, change, or modification that would affect the value of the Bid, or that would
                      substantively change the risks and benefits as outlined in the pro forma PPA, APA, or BTA, as
                      applicable. If a Bid’s red-lined version suggests material changes, GPC will not consider those
                      changes and the Bid may be disqualified.

                      Bidder has obtained site control of the Site for the PPA Term or the duration of the Facility Design

                    requirements of this 2023 RFP; (ii) avoid, minimize, or, if necessary, permit and mitigate, any Site,
                    ICF Site, or Facility environmental impact; and (iii) comply with all environmental requirements of
                    this 2023 RFP, as outlined in Exhibit C (Environmental Site Assessment Requirements). If a Bid
                    advances to the Competitive Tier, Bidder must submit to GPC its Environmental Assurances by
                    the due date as indicated in the Solicitation Schedule.

                    GPC executes will require that: (i) Seller covenant that GPC will not be subject to VIE treatment
                    and deemed the Primary Beneficiary as contemplated by ASC Topic 810, Consolidation, as issued
                    and modified from time to time by Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) at any point

         PART 7.      COMMUNICATION

               7.1.   Monitored Communications. Before an award for an Awarded Contract, all communications
                      regarding this 2023 RFP must be conducted through the IE Website. Following the close of the
                      Bid Period and until the Winning Bidder executes the Awarded Contract, any communication
                      between any individual Bidder and the Evaluation Team regarding a specific Bid is confidential,
                      except to the extent that Staff or the IE monitor communications. Communications may include
                      face-to-face meetings with a Bidder to discuss the Bid. The Evaluation Team may conduct
                      conference calls with a Bidder to clarify or resolve Bid questions. A Bidder may request a meeting
                      or conference call using the confidential message board on the IE Website, but may not contact
                      any member of the Evaluation Team otherwise. The IE and Staff will monitor any meeting or
                      communication that includes the Evaluation Team and any Bidder or any Company-Owned
                      Proposal Team.

               7.2.   Communication Before Initiation of a Bid.
                      Each Bidder and each interested Person registered on the IE Website may submit questions
                      concerning this 2023 RFP, the RFP Documents, the Bid, or Bid evaluation on the “Q&A” page of
                      the IE Website. The questions and, following consultation with IE and Staff, GPC’s responses will
                      be posted on the IE Website for viewing by all potential Bidders and registered users of the IE
                      Website. In no instance may Bidder or any interested Person contact any member of the
                      Evaluation Team or Staff to discuss any issue related to the RFP Documents, the RFP
                      Process, the evaluation process, or any similar subject. All inquiries must be directed to
                      the IE, through the IE Website, in compliance with Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(e)(2)(ii).
                      Any breach of this requirement may result in Bid disqualification.

               7.3.   Communication Following Initiation of a Bid.
                      7.3.1. Bid Books, Message Board. Once the Bid Period begins and Bidder initiates the Bid
                      process, each Bidder will have a confidential Bid Book on the IE Website, where Bidder posts all
                      RFP deliverables and all messages from IE to Bidder are available to Bidder. Bidder may ask Site-
                      specific and Facility-specific questions using the confidential message board. Questions submitted
                      on the message board are not available to other Bidders and are only viewed by the Evaluation
                      Team, the IE, and Staff. The Evaluation Team will reply to each question posted on the message
                      board, after review and consultation with the IE and Staff. All questions determined by the IE to be
                      generic in nature, and not unique to a specific Site or Facility, may be transferred to the “Q&A”
                      page of the IE Website so that all Bidders and registered users have the benefit of the question
                      and response.

                      7.3.2. Submission Deficiencies. Participants may amend a Submission only up until the
                      submission deadline on the Solicitation Schedule. After the submission deadline, a Deficient
                      Submission may be rejected as nonresponsive to this 2023 RFP unless the Evaluation Team, in
                      consultation with Staff and IE, determines it will allow Participant to cure the deficiency within a
                      specified time frame. After the submission deadline, no Participant will be allowed to change its
                      Submission price, nor will any Participant be allowed to revise its Submission on its own initiative.
                      All Participants that are granted a cure period will be given the same amount of time to cure their
                      Deficient Submission. In the case of Deficient Submissions from Bidders, Bid Fees will not be
                      returned.

                      7.3.3. Bidder Identified Bid Error. If Bidder discovers an error or omission in a Bid after
                      submitting the electronic filing, but before the submission deadline on the Bid Due Date, Bidder
                      should use the “withdraw” feature on the Bid management page on the IE Website, make the
                      desired change, and resubmit the Bid before the submission deadline.

               7.4.   Listing Determination. The status of a Bid (whether included on the Short List, the Reserve List,
                      the Competitive Tier, or Release List) is confidential. GPC will not publicly announce the Short
                      List, Reserve List, Competitive Tier, or Release List. The identity of the winning Bids and Bidders
                      will become public information when GPC requests Certification of the related PPAs, APAs, or
                      BTAs, or Company-Owned Proposals, if any, by the Commission.

               7.5.   Following Execution of an Awarded Contract. A Winning Bidder is prohibited from announcing
                      its status as a winning Bid or execution of an Awarded Contract via a press release or any other
                      method of public communication, without GPC’s prior, express written consent. A Winning Bidder
                      is responsible for ensuring that its winning Bid status remains confidential and is not announced
                      by any Affiliate, Representative, or contractual party. A Winning Bidder must educate its Affiliates,
                      Representatives, contractual parties, and any other participants in the development of the Facility

                      impact of public statements regarding renewable facilities (e.g., REC claims) and how these
                      statements may jeopardize the validity of Environmental Attributes that are sold to GPC under
                      the Awarded Contract, which could result in a breach of the Awarded Contract by Seller. Upon
                      execution of the Awarded Contract, the Winning Bidders and GPC will work together to determine
                      the timing and content of the official announcement of the winning status of the Facility and
                      execution of the Awarded Contract.

                      Bidder’s Bid book on the IE Website. This contact person must be familiar with all aspects of the
                      Bid process and the Bid in order to efficiently communicate with GPC and to reduce any delay in
                      communication. Bidder must notify GPC via the IE Website if there is a change in its point of
                      contact.

               7.7.   Confidentiality. Each Bidder is prohibited from disclosing to others any Bid Information; except
                      that Bidder may disclose Bid Information to its Representatives as reasonably necessary for
                      Bidder to submit a Bid in this 2023 RFP with the following conditions to any disclosure: (i) Bidder
                      must direct its Representative not to disclose Bid Information; and (ii) Bidder’s Representative
                      must be subject to a contractual obligation or professional ethical obligation to maintain the
                      confidentiality of, and not disclose, Bid Information. If the Representative does not have a
                      professional ethical obligation or cannot be made subject to a contractual obligation to maintain
                      confidentiality of Bid Information, Bidder must obtain GPC’s prior written consent before making
                      the disclosure. Furthermore, Bidder and its Representatives are prohibited from making any
                      public statement or other claim regarding the Energy or Environmental Attributes to be generated
                      by the Facility, including any statement that the Energy or Environmental Attributes are generated
                      from any sustainable, perpetual, renewable, or other particular type of fuel, including in any
                      marketing or advertising material, press release, or public statement. Each Bidder will be
                      responsible for any statement, claim, commitment, or disclosure made by itself or its
                      Representatives that has the effect of retiring or claiming the Environmental Attributes from the
                      Facility or otherwise limiting or jeopardizing the Facility’s Environmental Attributes that would be
                      conveyed to GPC under the Awarded Contract.

                      GPC will take reasonable precautions and use reasonable efforts to protect any proprietary or
                      Confidential Information contained in a Bid, so long as Bidder clearly states that the information
                      is confidential on each page on which Confidential Information appears. Such information may,
                      however, be made available under applicable state or federal law to Governmental Authorities
                      having appropriate jurisdiction over this 2023 RFP. GPC reserves the right to release such
                      information to: (i) the IE and Staff as needed to monitor this 2023 RFP; (ii) to regulated retail
                      Affiliates; (iii) to SCS; and (iv) to affected entities who have a need to know in order to assist in
                      the evaluation of Bids, so long as the entities agree to observe the same care with respect to
                      non-disclosure as GPC. Under no circumstance will GPC (including its Affiliates, and the officers,
                      directors, employees, representatives, or agents of any of them) or the IE or Staff be liable for

         PART 8.      BID EVALUATION AND AWARDED CONTRACTS.

               8.1.   Staff and IE Oversight/Evaluation. In accordance with Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(e)(3),
                      Staff and the IE actively and contemporaneously monitor all aspects of GPC’s evaluation process
                      for transparency purposes. Staff and the IE will review all Bid and Company-Owned Proposal
                      submissions and conduct an independent evaluation of the resource options submitted to GPC
                      in the RFP Process pursuant to Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(e)(3). Staff and the IE are
                      permitted access to all of the documents and information utilized by GPC in its evaluation. GPC,
                      Staff, and IE will meet to discuss and finalize the composition of the Competitive Tier identified
                      for further evaluation, as well as the Short List identified for awards of Awarded Contracts and
                      any Company-Owned Proposal which has been identified for inclusion on the Short List.

               8.2.   Criteria. All Bids submitted in response to this 2023 RFP will be evaluated in accordance with
                      the evaluation criteria and structure described in Exhibit I (Overview of Bid Evaluation). GPC
                      reserves the right to contact any Bidder through the IE Website to request additional information
                      on any aspect of the Bid.

               8.3.   Initial Review of Bids. GPC reserves the right to reject any Bid for failure to meet any 2023 RFP
                      requirement. Without qualification and in its sole discretion, GPC may decline to enter into an
                      Awarded Contract with any Person. If GPC discovers that any Bidder violated this 2023 RFP or
                      otherwise violated the spirit and intent of this 2023 RFP, GPC has the right to reject any related
                      Bids, which may also further affect the Bidder’s participation in any future programs offered by
                      GPC. Any Bidder who submits a Bid in response to this 2023 RFP waives any recourse
                      against GPC, its parent, or any of its Affiliates, or the IE, for either rejection of its Bid or
                      for failure to execute a PPA, APA, or BTA for any reason. GPC will not refund any Bid Fee or
                      costs associated with any Interconnection Study paid by Bidder for any reason, including GPC’s
                      rejection of the Bid or failure by Bidder to execute an Awarded Contract.

                      8.3.1. Rejection of Submission for Failure to Respond or Comply with Deadlines. GPC
                      reserves the right to reject any Deficient Submission at any time if Participant fails to submit
                      required information, make a required payment, or otherwise provide to GPC any required
                      deliverable by the deadline set forth in this 2023 RFP (and any date in the Solicitation Schedule
                      as revised, if applicable). A question asked by a Bidder regarding a deadline does not extend the
                      deadline. If a Submission is found to be a Deficient Submission then it may be placed on the
                      Release List and released from this 2023 RFP. GPC is not required to contact any Participant to
                      obtain any omitted information.

                      8.3.2. Rejection of Bid for Environmental Concerns. GPC reserves the right to reject any Bid
                      at any time if the siting or construction of the proposed Facility presents an environmental or
                      archeological impact or risk that: (i) cannot be mitigated or overcome within the timeframe of this
                      2023 RFP; or (ii) potentially undermines GPC’s environmental stewardship efforts. The
                      archeological risks and impacts may include, for example, the presence or discovery of any
                      archaeological, historical, religious, or cultural site, place, artifact, or monument.

                      8.3.3. Rejection of a Bidder’s Request that Conflicts with GPC Policy. If Bidder requests
                      that GPC take any action that conflicts with GPC’s business policies and procedures, GPC will not
                      honor Bidder’s request and will inform Bidder of the conflict, in which case, GPC may reject
                      Bidder’s Bid.

               8.4.   Complete Bids. Bids that are complete and conform to the requirements of this 2023 RFP will
                      be ranked and screened on economic value. Economically Non-Competitive Bids may be placed
                      on the Release List and released from this 2023 RFP. The remaining Bids will be further evaluated

                      Competitive Tier in accordance with the Solicitation Schedule. The Competitive Tier will be further
                      evaluated to determine which Bids are to be included on the Short List or the Reserve List, or
                      whether they are to be subsequently placed on the Release List and released from this 2023
                      RFP.

               8.7.   Bid Security Mechanics.
                      8.7.1. Draft Bid Security. Pursuant to Section 4.4 (Bid Security), for each Bid advanced to the
                      Competitive Tier, Bidder must submit Bid Security. Each Bidder that intends to provide Bid Security
                      in the form of a Surety Bond or a Letter of Credit must upload to its Bid Book a draft (unissued)
                      Surety Bond or Letter of Credit for review and approval by the Evaluation Team, at least five
                      Business Days before the Bid Security due date. Instructions for posting the draft and final Bid
                      Security will be available on the IE Website. The form of Surety Bond will also be available on the
                      IE Website.

                      8.7.2. Delivery of Bid Security. Bid Security in the form of cash must be submitted to GPC
                      through the IE Website according to the instructions posted on the Documents Page. Any Bid
                      Security submitted in the form of Surety Bond or Letter of Credit must be uploaded to the Bid Book
                      and thereafter, mailed via a reputable overnight courier to arrive on or before the Bid Security due
                      date at the following address:

                                           Accion Group, LLC
                                           244 North Main Street
                                           Concord, NH 03301
                                           Tel: (603) 229-1644
                                           Attention: Harold T. Judd

                      8.7.3. Return of Bid Security. The Bid Security is fully refundable to Bidder: (i) if the Bid is
                      placed on the Release List; or (ii) on the date Seller and GPC execute the Awarded Contract for a
                      winning Bid. The Bid Security is non-refundable if Bidder withdraws the Bid or otherwise fails to
                      execute the pro forma PPA, APA, or BTA, as applicable, after being advanced to the Competitive
                      Tier.

                      8.7.4. Conversion of Bid Security to Performance Security. If Bid Security is in the form of
                      cash or a Letter of Credit, Bidder may opt to appropriately amend the Bid Security to convert it to
                      the required Performance Security at the time of execution of the Awarded Contract, or Bidder
                      may replace the Bid Security with another acceptable form of Performance Security pursuant to
                      provisions of the Awarded Contract.

               8.8.   Evaluation Components.
                      8.8.1. Environmental Screening. All Bids in the Competitive Tier will undergo a comprehensive
                      review to ensure environmental compliance with the requirements of this 2023 RFP, which at a
                      minimum considers the Environmental Compliance Assessment/Requirements found in Exhibit C
                      (Environmental Site Assessment Requirements).

                      8.8.2. Improvement Costs Imputed. Based on the information contained in each Bid advanced
                      to the Competitive Tier, GPC will develop a cost estimate for Electric System improvements, if any,

                      as described in the sections entitled “Interconnection Impacts” and “Delivery Impacts” in the
                      applicable interconnection scenario described in Exhibit B (Interconnection and Delivery of
                      Electricity Requirements General). Those costs will be included in evaluating the economics of the

                      8.8.3. Due Diligence Portfolio Analysis. As discussed in more detail in Exhibit I (Overview of
                      Bid Evaluation), if the potential Short List includes Facilities connecting to the Southern Company
                      Transmission System such that their system impact costs are not independent, evaluations of the
                      combined effects of those Bids will be necessary to select the best combination of Bids.

                      8.8.4. Non-Price and Qualitative Considerations. Although GPC’s evaluation will focus on the
                      Bid’s economic net benefits, other qualitative and non-price considerations will be considered.
                      Non-price factors that may be used in evaluating Bids include: (i) reliability associated with Facility
                      location interconnecting to the Southern Company Transmission System; (ii) locating the Facility
                      inside GPC’s service territory; (iii) Bidder’s project development experience; (iv) Bidder’s DEI
                      initiatives; (v) environmental impacts; (vi) the substation into which the Facility proposes
                      interconnection; (vii) cost and schedule of any Electric System improvements that are required as
                      a result of Bidder’s proposed Facility; and (viii) Bidder’s proposed date for the achievement of
                      Commercial Operation or Closing, as applicable. It is Bidder’s responsibility to submit additional
                      information related to its Bid if such information will materially improve the quality of its offer or
                      GPC’s understanding thereof.

               8.9.   Company-Owned Proposal and APA/BTA Evaluation. The IE, Staff, and GPC will agree on a
                      methodology to compare Company-Owned Proposals and Bids for APAs and BTAs to Bids for
                      PPAs. This methodology will include calculating a revenue requirement using GPC’s proprietary
                      revenue requirement model that will be locked down before Bids are received. For Company-
                      Owned Proposals, the revenue requirement will be converted into a price stated in dollars per
                      megawatt-hour ($/MWh) to: (i) provide Company-Owned Proposal information to the Evaluation
                      Team in a manner that will not identify the submission as a Company-Owned Proposal; and (ii)
                      allow the Evaluation Team to evaluate Company-Owned Proposal pricing and Bid pricing on an
                      equivalent basis using the criteria described in Section 8.3 (Initial Review of Bids). For Bids for
                      APAs and BTAs, the purchase price will be converted into a revenue requirement. Staff will
                      oversee these conversions. Bids will not be opened until the IE and Staff have reviewed and
                      validated all Company-Owned Proposals. Following the IE’s and Staff’s review and validation of
                      Submissions, the IE will release Bids and Company-Owned Proposals to the Evaluation Team.
                      The Evaluation Team will then compare all Bids received with any Company-Owned Proposal
                      and will advance the best options to meet the specific needs for GPC’s portfolio.

               8.10. Short List, Reserve List, and Release List
                      8.10.1. Short List Identified. Based on the results of the detailed evaluation, Bids will advance
                      from the Competitive Tier to the Short List. GPC will contact each Short-Listed Bidder to confirm
                      that the PPA, APA, or BTA, as applicable, conforms to the Facility’s specifications and correctly
                      identifies Bidder’s business entity. Each Bidder with a Bid advanced to the Short List for further
                      evaluation must also provide the following information, if requested by GPC: (i) updates to the
                      construction schedule; (ii) a current Site plan; (iii) equipment delivery schedules; and (iv) any and
                      all financial and business data associated with the Seller, the Facility, the PPA, the APA, or BTA
                      that GPC would need to independently make the necessary accounting determinations.
                      Requested Information may include data supporting the economic life, the fair value, investment
                      tax credits associated with the Facility, or other costs associated with the Facility, including debt
                      specific to the asset proposed. Financial data contained in Bidder’s financial statements (e.g.,
                      income statements, balance sheets, etc.) may also be required.

                      8.10.2. Reserve Lists and Release Lists. Any Bid not identified for the Short List may be placed
                      on the Reserve List. GPC will notify each Bidder eligible for the Reserve List that its Bid has been
                      identified for continued evaluation on the Reserve List. Any Bidder whose Bid is not competitive
                      will be notified that its Bid is no longer being considered for the Short List or Reserve List. These

                      8.10.3. Short List, Reserve List, Release List Determination. In accordance with the
                      Solicitation Schedule, and as discussed in Section 8.8.3 (Due Diligence Portfolio Analysis) and
                      Section 8.10.1 (Short List Identified), upon completion of evaluation, Bidder will be notified whether
                      its Bid is on the Short List, Reserve List, or Release List. GPC will contact each Bidder with a Bid
                      advanced to the Short List to finalize and execute the PPA, APA, or BTA, as applicable. A Bid on
                      the Reserve List is a Bid that is essentially on a waiting list that will continue to be under evaluation
                      and may move on to the Short List if a Short List Bidder withdraws or is unable to proceed to
                      execution of an Awarded Contract. A Bid on the Reserve List that is not for a CFE-ATC Resource
                      and that elected to participate in the CARES ED Program may be considered for further evaluation.
                      Additional details regarding how a Bidder whose Bid is placed on the Reserve List may elect to
                      participate in the CARES ED Program will be made in a separate filing by GPC with the
                      Commission. A Bid on the Release List was determined to be non-competitive and will no longer
                      be considered for advancement in this 2023 RFP. Release List determinations are final and will
                      not be reconsidered. As provided in Section 7.7 (Confidentiality), Bidder must not disclose the
                      status of its Bid, including its inclusion on the Short List, Reserve List, or Release List. By the end
                      of the 2023 RFP Process, all Bids not placed on the Release List and not advanced for contracting
                      will be placed on the Reserve List. When GPC executes the winning PPAs, APAs, or BTAs and
                      files the executed Awarded Contracts with the Commission, all unadvanced Bids will be placed on
                      the Release List, unless the Bid has previously elected to be considered for the CARES ED
                      Program.

               8.11. Awarded Contracts. GPC will award and execute Awarded Contracts (subject to payment of the
                     Winner’s Fee) with the Winning Bidders whose Bids are on the Short List. A Winning Bidder will
                     enter into the applicable and conforming pro forma PPA, APA, or BTA with GPC. As stated in
                     Section 6.6.1 (Conformance of Pro Forma PPA, Pro Forma APA, or Pro Forma BTA), GPC will
                     not accept substantive or material changes to the pro forma PPA, pro forma APA, or pro forma
                     BTA, as applicable, at the time of contract execution. GPC and Winning Bidder will coordinate to
                     execute the PPA, APA, or BTA, as applicable (subject to the payment of the Winner’s Fee).

               8.12. GPC Discretion in Contracting. GPC reserves the right, without qualification and in consultation
                     with the IE and Staff, to reject any, all, or portions of Bids received for failure to meet any criteria,
                     and further reserves the right, without qualification and at its sole discretion, and in consultation
                     with the IE and Staff, to decline to enter into an Awarded Contract with any Bidder. Any Bidder
                     who submits a Bid in response to this 2023 RFP waives the right to claim any recourse against
                     GPC or any of its Affiliates or the IE for either rejection of Bidder’s Bid(s) or any other Bid(s) or
                     for failure to execute a PPA, BTA, or APA for any reason.

                      Contract without any further obligation pursuant to the applicable provisions of the Awarded
                      Contract. Performance of an Awarded Contract is also conditioned upon, if required by applicable
                      law, FERC issuing an order accepting the Awarded Contract in a timely manner and without
                      material qualification or condition adversely affecting either party to the Awarded Contract;

         20.    Bids for PPAs for Facilities utilizing solar photovoltaic modules as the sole Renewable Resource must
                meet the following requirements:

                A.       Hydrology and Site Drainage
                                  Site grading must ensure positive drainage of the Site.
                                  Site design must ensure no flooding, no standing water, and no increase in flows
                                   offsite.
                                  The drainage design must be based on a 100-year, 24-hour rain event.
                                  No portion of the Facility may be located in a floodplain without the proper permit(s)
                                   from the appropriate Governmental Authority.
                                  The construction contract scope must include responsibility of contractor to close out
                                   the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit.

                B.           Site Grading and Stabilization
                                  Measures must be in place to prevent sediment loss.
                                  Permanent site vegetation and site stabilization must be completed before
                                   demobilizing.

                C.           Facility Design
                                  Equipment must be sized to deliver rated Facility nameplate power at the POI,
                                   accounting for worst-case local ambient temperature, and interconnection reactive
                                   power requirement.
                                  Site performance at the POI must meet the interconnection requirements as set forth
                                   by the Interconnection Provider.
                                  Reactive power requirement must be solely met by the inverters without the use of
                                   capacitor banks.
                                  All equipment enclosures (e.g., combiner boxes) must be tamperproof and lockable
                                   (e.g., a special tool or key is required to open the equipment enclosure).
                                  Hurricane resistance rating and restoration plan.

                D.           Major Equipment Vendors
                                  Major equipment vendors must demonstrate quality and performance and be
                                   prepared to perform future warranty and maintenance work.
                                  Major equipment must be manufactured in factories certified to both IEC TS 62941
                                   and ISO 9001.
                                  Final major equipment vendors subject to review by GPC.

                E.           PV Module
                                  Solar modules must be sourced from Bloomberg New Energy Finance (BNEF) Tier 1
                                   photovoltaic manufacturers.
                                  Provide detailed Highly Accelerated Life Test (HALT) report (PVEL or equivalent) for
                                   the specific module proposed, preferably from independent third-party testing agency.
                                  Provide module manufacturing location and Bill of Material (BOM).

                F.           Inverter
                                  Inverters must be listed to UL1741 latest version.
                                  Inverters may be reviewed by GPC.
                                  Inverters must be capable of producing their maximum rated reactive power at all
                                   active power levels (from 0% to 100% inclusive), when the primary energy source is
                                   available and not available.

         CARES 2023 US RFP                                                                                  Page 44 of 88
                                                       www.gonitro.com

STF-JKA-1-24 Attachment B.pdf
                                                                                               CARES 2023 US RFP
                                                                                        GEORGIA POWER COMPANY
                                                                                       FINAL APPROVED (12.22.2023)

                                 Inverters must be equipped with DC ground detection means through either insulation
                                  monitoring or differential current monitoring.
                                 Facilities that are transmission interconnected must conform to NERC
                                  recommendations and requirements pertaining to IBR facilities.

                G.           Inverter Step-up Transformer
                                 Transformers must be two-winding and KNAN type cooling; winding must be copper.
                                 All transformers must be IEEE routinely tested including dielectric test, impulse test,
                                  and power factor test. Lightning impulse tests must include one full wave test.
                                 Oil reservoir for spill containment must be provided for each transformer.

                H.           MV Switchgear
                                 MV switchgear protection scheme must, at minimum, include main break protection,
                                  feeder breaker protection, bus differential protection, a dedicated bus lockout, and
                                  breaker failure functionality.
                                 All current transformers (CT) must have an accuracy class of C400 or higher.

                I.           Grounding
                                 Dual grounding, as depicted in IEEE 665, must be provided in all cases with an
                                  equipment grounding conductor (for a reliable ground fault current return path) and an
                                  additional local safety ground (for limiting touch potential).

                J.           PV Monitoring
                                 Meteorological and performance monitoring equipment/system must conform to
                                  IEC61724 and the requirements defined for a Class A (high) accuracy monitoring
                                  system.
                                 Table 4 of IEC61724 will be used to determine the number of devices required. At
                                  minimum two devices of each measurement type must be provided.
                                 At minimum two soiling stations utilizing full sized modules must be provided.

                K.           Testing
                                 Operational Test, Performance Ratio Test, and Capacity Test (ASTM Based) must be
                                  performed for PV facilities.
                                 Additional testing, if required under the Interconnection Agreement, must also be
                                  performed.
                                 NERC testing must be performed for facilities defined as a Bulk Electric System
                                  (BES).

                L.           Main Power Transformer
                                 Transformers must be capable of meeting 100% of Facility output using 100% ONAN-
                                  cooling.
                                 Transformer suppliers may be subject to review.
                                 RIS-type bushings are preferred.
                                 Transformers must be designed with a 25% temporary emergency overload.
                                 Transformer overload capability must be unlimited by components (i.e., bushing
                                  ratings, DETC rating, etc.)
                                 The transformer tank design must be in accordance with IEEE C57.156 Table 1 to
                                  mitigate tank rupture in the event of a high-energy arcing fault internal to the tank.


         CARES 2023 US RFP                                                                                  Page 45 of 88

                                                                                               CARES 2023 US RFP

                M.        Facility Substation
                                 Facility substations must meet safety requirements of the NESC-2023 and comply
                                  with the design principles set forth ASCE 7, ASCE 113, IEEE 605, and IEEE 80.
                                 Facility substations must be commissioned to NETA ATS 17 standards.
                                 All bus and cable sizes must be designed with a maximum operating temperature of
                                  80 °C with a 40 °C ambient, with no sun and 2 ft/s wind.
                                 Spatial separation from oil-filled electrical equipment must be compliant with IEEE
                                  979-2012.
                                 All equipment suppliers, protection and control designs and settings, and grounding
                                  design/modeling will be subject to review by GPC.

                N.           Cyber Security
                                 Facility connectivity must be in compliance with NERC CIP policies.

                                 The Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) testing procedure and results

                                 Description of the end-of-life disposal/recycling plan must be included.

         22.    Bids for BTAs for Build Transfer Facilities must meet the following requirements:

                A.       Hydrology and Site Drainage

                                Site grading must ensure positive drainage of the Site.
                                Site design must ensure no flooding, no standing water, and no increase in flows
                                 offsite, as prescribed by the Georgia Stormwater Management Manual.
                                The drainage design must be based on a 100-year, 24-hour rain event.
                                No portion of the Facility will be located in a floodplain without the proper permit(s)
                                 from the appropriate Governmental Authority. GPC reserves the right to review the
                                 location of any portion of a Facility proposed to be in a floodplain, as well as any such
                                 permit(s).
                                The construction contract scope must include responsibility of contractor to close out
                                 the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit.
                                Contractor will remain responsible for getting the Notice of Termination (NOT) verified
                                 and signed by the agency.

                B.       Site Grading and Stabilization

                                Balanced earthwork is desired. Grades within the array to be used for
                                 vehicular/equipment ingress and egress must be no steeper than 10%. The maximum
                                 slope for areas of elevation transition must not exceed a ratio of 3:1.
                                Measures must be in place to prevent sediment loss.
                                Permanent site vegetation and site stabilization must be completed before Final
                                 Completion.

                C.       Facility Design

                                Equipment must be sized to deliver rated Facility nameplate instantaneous Energy
                                 output at the POI, accounting for worst-case local ambient temperature, plant losses
                                 (including auxiliary power), and interconnection reactive power requirement.

                                  Site performance at the POI must meet the interconnection requirements as set forth
                                   by the Interconnection Provider.
                                  Reactive power requirement must be solely met by the inverters without the use of
                                   capacitor banks.
                                  Input and output of all control and communication devices must be wired out to
                                   marshalling terminal blocks that is easily accessible.
                                  All equipment enclosures (e.g., combiner boxes) must be tamperproof and lockable
                                   (e.g., a special tool or key is required to open the equipment enclosure).

                D.           Major Equipment Vendors

                                  Major equipment vendors must demonstrate quality and performance and be
                                   prepared to perform future warranty and maintenance work.
                                  Major equipment must be manufactured in factories certified to both IEC TS 62941
                                   and ISO 9001.
                                  Final major equipment vendors subject to review and approval by GPC.

                E.           PV Module

                                  Solar modules must be sourced from Bloomberg New Energy Finance (BNEF) Tier 1
                                   photovoltaic manufacturers.
                                  Photovoltaic modules must be framed. All string connectors must use the same
                                   connector manufacturer and model as the PV module lead.
                                  Provide detailed Highly Accelerated Life Test (HALT) report (PVEL or equivalent) for
                                   the specific module proposed, preferably from independent third-party testing agency.
                                  Provide module manufacturing location and Bill of Material (BOM).

                F.           Inverter

                                  Inverters must be listed to UL1741 latest version.
                                  Inverters must be approved by GPC.
                                  Inverters must be capable of producing their maximum rated reactive power at all
                                   active power levels (from 0% to 100% inclusive), when the primary energy source is
                                   available and not available.
                                  Inverters must be equipped with DC ground detection means through either insulation
                                   monitoring or differential current monitoring.
                                  A lockable fused disconnect must be provided at each discrete incoming DC input.
                                  Facilities that are transmission interconnected must conform to NERC
                                   recommendations and requirements pertaining to IBR facilities.

                G.           Inverter Step-up Transformer

                                  Transformers must be two-winding and KNAN type cooling; winding must be copper.
                                  Transformers must be equipped with fully rated no-load tap changers at HV side two
                                   taps at 2.5% above nominal position and two taps at 2.5% below nominal position
                                   must be provided.
                                  All transformers must be IEEE routinely tested including dielectric test, impulse test,
                                   and power factor test. Lightning impulse tests must include one full wave test.
                                  Two IR windows must be provided on both low side and high side terminations.
                                  Oil reservoir for spill containment must be provided for each transformer.

                H.           MV Switchgear

                                 Outdoor rated metal-clad medium-voltage (MV) switchgear (e.g., over a sectionalizer
                                  cabinet) must be provided when required to combine and reduce the number of
                                  circuits to the substation; a main breaker must be provided.
                                 MV switchgear protection scheme must at minimum include main break protection,
                                  feeder breaker protection, bus differential protection, a dedicated bus lockout, and
                                  breaker failure functionality.
                                 All current transformers (CT) must have an accuracy class of C400 or higher.
                                 Bidder must coordinate with GPC on specific relays used and protection philosophy.

                I.           Grounding

                                 Dual grounding, as depicted in IEEE 665, must be provided in all cases with an
                                  equipment grounding conductor (for a reliable ground fault current return path) and an
                                  additional local safety ground (for limiting touch potential).
                                 Safety ground must be bare stranded copper #2/0 AWG or larger and direct buried,
                                  with risers bonded to each row of PV array and all equipment.
                                 Grounding study must be provided for the entire Site to determine the safety
                                  grounding design for limiting hazardous touch and step potentials during a worse case
                                  postulated ground fault event.

                J.           Cable Management

                                 All equipment enclosure within the PV array must be located at the end of PV racking
                                  rows towards the road and facing the same direction whenever possible.
                                 All DC wiring must be below grade unless routed along and below the PV array to
                                  prevent the blocking of aisle space between rows. However, an E-W CAB system will
                                  be acceptable for Facilities with trackers. All DC and LV AC cables below grade must
                                  be routed in conduit.
                                 PV array must use single string harness that routes strings directly to the combiner
                                  box or the string inverter. (i.e., harness that combines multiple strings must not be
                                  used)

                K.           PV Monitoring

                                 Meteorological and performance monitoring equipment/system must conform to
                                  IEC61724 and the requirements defined for a Class A (high) accuracy monitoring
                                  system.
                                 Table 4 of IEC61724 must be used to determine the number of devices required. At
                                  minimum two devices of each measurement type must be provided.
                                 For facilities using bifacial modules, an albedometer must be provided for each GHI
                                  pyranometer.
                                 At minimum two soiling stations utilizing full sized modules must be provided.

                L.           Testing

                                 Operational Test, Performance Ratio Test, and Capacity Test (ASTM Based) must be
                                  performed for PV facilities.
                                 Additional testing, if required under the Interconnection Agreement, must also be
                                  performed.
                                 NERC testing must be performed for facilities defined as a Bulk Electric System
                                  (BES).

                M.       Main Power Transformer

                                  Transformers must be capable of meeting 100% of Facility output using 100% ONAN-

                                  Transformer suppliers must be subject to review and approval by GPC.

                                  Site controller, battery management system (if applicable) and inverters time must be
                                   synchronized to a local time clock. The preference is to time sync with any devices
                                   that can take a remote time sync.
                                  Local Human Machine Interface platform must be Ignition by Inductive Automation.

                                  The Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP) testing procedure and results

                        EXHIBIT B - INTERCONNECTION AND DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS


         Each Bidder is responsible for determining all transmission interconnection and delivery-related rules,
         practices, and policies with which it must comply. Each Bid must comply with the general requirements
         outlined in Section 1 of this Exhibit B and with one of the interconnection options described in Sections
         2 through 4 of this Exhibit B.


         1.    Interconnection and Delivery Requirements – General
              The following interconnection requirements apply to all Bids, regardless of Facility location.
               1.1.      Transmission Projected Commercial Operation Date. GPC may decline to advance a Bid to
               the Short List or to execute an Awarded Contract with any Bidder if, in the opinion of GPC, the
               transmission facilities cannot be constructed in time to achieve Commercial Operation or Closing, as
               applicable, by the date set forth in the Solicitation Schedule. Except for the provision in Section 2.7
               (Facility Interconnecting Directly to GPC) below for a Facility interconnecting to the Southern Company
               Transmission System via GPC, Bidder assumes all interconnection and delivery lead-time risk (if
               applicable) to meet the RCOD or RCD, as applicable.
               1.2.     Bid Price Assumptions. Each Bidder must, if the Facility’s POI is not on the Southern
               Company Transmission System, state in its Bid the assumptions regarding interconnection and delivery
               costs that are included in its Bid price. Specifically, each Bid must include details of these costs and
               refer to any completed or active Interconnection Study results related to the Facility.
               1.3.     Bid Lead-Time Assumptions. Bidder must describe, with respect to the proposed Facility, its
               current status within the applicable interconnection process and its ability to meet the RCOD, or RCD,
               in the case of an APA or a BTA, based upon the applicable interconnection process timeline.
               1.4.      Interconnection Agreement Required. Each Winning Bidder must enter into an
               Interconnection Agreement with the appropriate Interconnection Provider, depending on the geographic
               location and interconnection configuration of the Facility. Each Bidder must contact the appropriate
               Interconnection Provider to obtain all relevant information and interconnection requirements. The
               submission of a Bid in response to this 2023 RFP does not constitute an interconnection request or an
               Interconnection Agreement. Bidder is solely responsible for all fees, deposits, and other charges in
               connection with its interconnection request and the Interconnection Agreement. At any point in time, any
               Facility that is not a CFE-ATC Resource is prohibited from delivering output to the Point of Delivery that
               exceeds the lesser of the Generating Capacity or the Interconnection Limit; a CFE-ATC Resource is
               prohibited from delivering output to the Point of Delivery that exceeds the Interconnection Limit.
               1.5.     Timing and Notification of Initiating Interconnection Process (New Facility). At the time of
               Bid submission, Bidder must indicate if there is an existing interconnection request for the Facility (either
               in active study stage or if there is an IA that is in suspension), and if so, Bidder also must identify the
               Interconnection Provider, request number/identifier, and status. For Facilities not interconnecting to the
               Southern Company Transmission System, Bidders are responsible for understanding the
               interconnection requirements of the applicable Interconnection Provider and initiating the application
               and study process so as to comply with the RCOD requirements of this RFP. For Facilities
               interconnecting to the Georgia ITS, see also Section 3 (Interconnection to the Electric System of an ITS
               Participant (>40 kV)); for Facilities interconnecting to neither the Southern Company Transmission
               System nor the Georgia ITS, see also Section 4 (Interconnection Outside Both the Southern Company
               Transmission System and Georgia ITS).
               If a Facility is interconnecting to the Southern Company Transmission System, Bidder must initiate the
               interconnection process and obtain a queue position by no later than April 4, 2024, to ensure eligibility
               to participate in one of the FERC Order 2023 FERC-mandated transitional studies. This date is based
               on Southern Companies’ intended compliance filing date of March 5, 2024, and assumes FERC will
               approve Southern Companies’ request in their compliance filing to make FERC Order 2023 effective
               April 5, 2024. Unless a Bidder is able to obtain an LGIA under Order 2003, failure to participate in one
               of the FERC Order 2023 transitional studies, either the transitional serial facilities study or the transitional
               cluster study, will delay completion of the interconnection process to 2026 which would make the


         CARES 2023 US RFP                                                                                       Page 52 of 88
                                                        www.gonitro.com

STF-JKA-1-24 Attachment B.pdf
                                                                                                  CARES 2023 US RFP
                                                                                           GEORGIA POWER COMPANY
                                                                                          FINAL APPROVED (12.22.2023)
               Bidder’s ability to meet the Required COD of this RFP highly unlikely. Additional information regarding
               Southern Companies’ implementation of FERC Order 2023, including any changes in the schedule, can
               be found on the Southern Company OASIS website (https://www.oasis.oati.com/SOCO).
               Regardless of the Interconnection Provider, if Bidder has an Interconnection Agreement in suspension,
               by no later than seven Days after notification that the Bid has advanced to the Short List, Bidder must
               initiate the process with the appropriate Interconnection Provider to move out of suspension and into
               active status.
               1.6.    Existing Qualifying Facility Interconnection Agreement (Existing Facility). If the Facility of
               a Winning Bidder has an existing Transmission Qualifying Facility Interconnection Agreement with GPC
               (“QFIA”), and the Facility has already reached COD or will reach COD before PPA execution, the QFIA
               will be converted to an LGIA or SGIA (defined below in Section 2.1 of this Exhibit B (Procedure
               Guidance)), as applicable, without additional studies or study fees.

         2.    Interconnection with the Southern Company Transmission System (>40 kV)
              The following requirements apply to a Bid for a Facility interconnecting to the transmission system of
              GPC or one of its regulated electric utility Affiliates (i.e., Alabama Power or Mississippi Power) with a
              Point of Interconnection at greater than 40 kV.
               2.1.    Procedure Guidance. If the Facility will interconnect to the Southern Company Transmission
               System, the evaluation of the Submission will assume Participant has executed either the small
               generator interconnection agreement (“SGIA”) or a large generator interconnection agreement (“LGIA”)
               and that either the small generator interconnection procedures (“SGIP”) or large generator
               interconnection procedures (“LGIP”) will apply. Generally, the SGIP is utilized for generators 20 MW or
               smaller and the LGIP for generators larger than 20 MW. The Southern Company Transmission System
               includes facilities owned by GPC or one of its regulated electric utility Affiliates (Alabama Power or
               Mississippi Power). The prompt submission of an accurate and complete application and prompt return
               of agreements will reduce the overall timeframe of the interconnection process. Each Bidder must
               determine all rules, practices, policies, and timelines with which its Facility must comply to interconnect
               with the Southern Company Transmission System. Bidder may obtain additional information on
               Southern Company’s OASIS web site at:
                        http://www.oatioasis.com/SOCO/index.html
               2.2.      Bidder Cost Responsibility. If the Facility will interconnect with the Southern Company
               Transmission System, Bidder is responsible for all Interconnection Study-related costs, in addition to
               the interconnection costs and risk up to the POI. These costs generally include equipment such as the
               Facility generator step-up (“GSU”) transformer (for conversion up to the interconnecting voltage level),
               Facility-side generator interrupting device, all Station Service equipment, tie-line (which carries electrical
               power and communications), and any additional equipment (such as a utility-owned interrupting device
               and metering needed to connect to the transmission facilities), as well as any additional real property
               for the interconnection substation and access and any operation and maintenance expenses and
               administrative costs. In addition, if applicable, Bidder is responsible for the costs, risk, and coordination
               of all Affected System Upgrades. It is Bidder’s responsibility to determine and consider all information
               regarding interconnection costs in preparing its Bid.
               2.3.    Interconnection Impacts.
                       A.    Southern Company Transmission System Interconnection Costs. Interconnection
                       impacts to the Electric System are unique to the specific design and location of each Facility
                       and may require new or modified equipment beyond the POI. For a Facility interconnecting to
                       the Southern Company Transmission System, any costs for new or modified equipment on the
                       Southern Company Transmission System beyond the POI will be imputed to the Bid during the
                       Bid evaluation and should not be included in the Bid price. However, as stated above in Section
                       2.2 (Bidder Cost Responsibility) of this Exhibit B any costs associated with Affected System
                       Upgrades are solely Bidder’s responsibility and will not be reimbursed by GPC.
                       B.     SCS LGIA/SGIA Costs. A Winning Bidder (i.e., Seller) may be required under the terms
                       of its SCS LGIA or SGIA, as applicable, to fund or provide security for new or modified
                       equipment beyond the POI. However, if a Seller incurs such interconnection-related costs for

                       C.     Affected System Interconnection Costs. If a winning Bid has associated
