         PART 7.     COMMUNICATION

              7.1.   Monitored Communications. Prior to selection of the Winning Bid(s), any communication
                     between an individual Bidder and GPC regarding a specific Bid will be confidential, except to the
                     extent that Staff and IE monitor communications. Such communications may include face-to-face
                     meetings with Bidder to discuss the Bid. GPC also may conduct a conference call with Bidder to
                     clarify or resolve Bid questions. Staff and IE, at their discretion, may participate in each such
                     discussion.

              7.2.   Prior to Submission of Bids. Each Bidder and each interested party registered on the IE
                     Website may submit questions concerning this 2023 Biomass RFP, the pro forma RFP
                     Documents, the Bids, or Bid evaluation on the “Q&A” page of the IE Website. When a Bidder
                     submits a question via the “Q&A” page, the identity of the Bidder asking the question is known to
                     the IE, Staff, and Evaluation Team members. The questions and GPC’s responses will be posted
                     on the IE Website for viewing by all potential Bidders. Bidder may submit project-specific
                     questions on the confidential message board that will be responded to by the IE, after consultation
                     with the Evaluation Team, as needed. Any question posted to the confidential message board
                     that the IE determines to be generic in nature, and not unique to a specific Site or Project, may
                     be transferred to the “Q&A” page so that all Bidders and registered users have the benefit of the
                     question and response. In no instance may Bidder or any interested party contact any
                     member of the Evaluation Team, Staff, or Commission to discuss any issue related to the
                     RFP Documents, the RFP process, the evaluation process, or any similar subject. All such
                     inquiries must be directed to the IE, through the IE Website, in compliance with Commission Rule
                     515-3-4-.04(3)(e)(2)(ii). Any breach of this requirement may result in Bid disqualification.

              7.3.   Following Submission of Bids
                     7.3.1. Bid Books, Message Board. Once the Bidding period commences and Bidder initiates
                     the Bid process, each Bidder will have a confidential “Bid book” on the IE Website, where Bidder
                     posts all RFP deliverables and all messages sent by the IE Website to Bidder are available to
                     Bidder. Bidder may ask Site-specific and Project-specific questions using the confidential
                     message board. Questions submitted on the message board are not available to other Bidders
                     and are only viewed by the Evaluation Team, the IE, and Staff. The Evaluation Team will reply to
                     each question posted on the message board, after review and consultation with the IE and Staff.
                     However, all questions determined by the IE to be generic in nature, and not unique to a specific
                     Site or Project, may be transferred to the “Q&A” page of the IE Website so that all Bidders and
                     registered users have the benefit of the question and response.

                     7.3.2. Bid Deficiencies. Bidder may amend a Bid only up until the submission deadline on the
                     Bid Due Date. Thereafter, a Deficient Bid will be rejected as nonresponsive to this 2023 Biomass
                     RFP unless GPC, in consultation with Staff and IE, determines it will permit Bidder to cure the
                     deficiency within a specified time frame. After the Bid Due Date, no Bidder will be allowed to
                     change its Bid price, nor will any Bidder be allowed to revise its Bid on its own initiative. Bid Fees
                     submitted with a Deficient Bid will not be returned.

              7.4.   Listing Determination. GPC will not publicly announce the Short List, Reserve List or
                     Competitive Tier. The identity of the winning Bid(s) and Bidder(s) will become public information
                     when GPC requests Certification of the related PPA(s) by the Commission.

              7.5.   Following Execution of the PPA. A Winning Bidder is prohibited from announcing the selection
                     of its winning Bid or execution of a PPA via a press release or any other method of public
                     communication, without the prior, express written consent of GPC. A Winning Bidder is
                     responsible for ensuring that its winning Bid status remains confidential and is not announced by
                     any Affiliate, Representative, or contractual party. A Winning Bidder must educate its Affiliates,
                     Representatives, contractual parties, and any other participants in the development of the Project
                     (e.g., development authorities, county, state, or federal Governmental Authorities) on the potential
                     impact of public statements regarding renewable facilities (e.g., REC claims) and how such
                     statements may jeopardize the validity of Environmental Attributes that are sold to GPC under


         2023 NEW BIOMASS RFP                                                                                 Page 24 of 58
                                                      www.gonitro.com

STF-JKA-1-24 Attachment E.pdf
                                                             2023 BIOMASS RFP FOR NEW BIOMASS GENERATION
                                                                              FINAL APPROVED - JUNE 16, 2023


                     the PPA, which could result in a breach of the PPA by Generator. Upon execution of the PPA(s),
                     the Winning Bidder(s) and GPC will work together to determine the timing and content of the
                     official announcement of the winning status of the project and PPA execution.

              7.6.   Point of Contact. Each Bid must include detailed contact information for the person who will
                     serve as the primary point of contact for Bidder. This person will serve as the contact between
                     GPC and Bidder when questions and answers are exchanged and will receive authority to access
                     Bidder’s Bid book on the IE Website. This contact person must be familiar with all aspects of the
                     Bid process and the Bid in order to efficiently communicate with GPC and to reduce any delay in
                     communication. Bidder must notify GPC via the IE Website if there is a change in its point of
                     contact.

              7.7.   Bidder-Identified Bid Error. If Bidder discovers an error or omission in a Bid after submitting
                     the electronic filing, but before the submission deadline on the Bid Due Date, Bidder should use
                     the “withdraw” feature on the bid management page on the IE Website, make the desired change,
                     and resubmit the Bid before the submission deadline.

              7.8.   Confidentiality. Each Bidder is prohibited from disclosing to others any Bidder Information;
                     except that Bidder may disclose Bidder Information to its Representatives as reasonably
                     necessary for such Bidder to submit a Bid in this 2023 Biomass RFP with the following conditions
                     to any such disclosure: (i) Bidder must direct its Representative not to disclose Bidder Information,
                     and (ii) such Representative must be subject to a contractual or professional ethics obligation to
                     maintain the confidentiality and not disclose Bidder Information. If the Representative does not
                     have a professional ethics obligation or cannot be made subject to a contractual obligation to
                     maintain confidentiality of Bidder Information, Bidder must obtain GPC’s prior written consent
                     before making the disclosure. Furthermore, Bidder and its Representatives are prohibited from
                     making any public statement or other claim regarding the Energy or Environmental Attributes to
                     be generated by the Facility, including any statement that the Energy or Environmental Attributes
                     are generated from any sustainable, perpetual, renewable, or other particular type of fuel,
                     including in any marketing or advertising material, press release, or public statement. Each Bidder
                     will be responsible for any statement, claim, commitment, or disclosure made by itself or its
                     Representatives that has the effect of retiring or claiming the Environmental Attributes from the
                     Facility or otherwise limiting or jeopardizing the Facility’s Environmental Attributes that would be
                     conveyed to GPC under the PPA.

                     GPC will take reasonable precautions and use reasonable efforts to protect any proprietary or
                     Confidential Information contained in a Bid, provided Bidder clearly identifies that such
                     information is confidential on each page on which such Confidential Information appears. Such
                     information may, however, be made available under applicable state or federal law to appropriate
                     Governmental Authorities. GPC reserves the right to release such information to the IE and Staff
                     as needed to monitor this 2023 Biomass RFP, to regulated retail Affiliates, to SCS, and to affected
                     entities who have a need to know in order to assist in the evaluation of Bids, provided that such
                     entities will observe the same care with respect to non-disclosure as GPC. Under no
                     circumstance will GPC (including its Affiliates, and the officers, directors, employees,
                     representatives, or agents of any of them) or the IE or Staff be liable for any damages resulting
                     from any disclosure before, during, or after the solicitation process.


         PART 8.     BID EVALUATION AND PPA AWARD.

              8.1.   Staff and IE Oversight/Evaluation. In accordance with Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(e)(3),
                     Staff and the IE actively and contemporaneously monitor all aspects of GPC’s evaluation process
                     for transparency purposes. Staff and the IE will review all Bid submissions and conduct an
                     independent evaluation of the resource options submitted to GPC in the RFP process pursuant
                     to Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(e)(3). Staff and the IE are permitted access to all of the
                     documents and information utilized by GPC in its evaluation. GPC, Staff, and IE will meet to
                     discuss and finalize the composition of the Competitive Tier identified for further evaluation, as
                     well as the Short List identified for PPA(s) awards.

              8.2.   Criteria. All Bids submitted in response to this 2023 Biomass RFP will be evaluated in
                     accordance with the evaluation criteria and structure described in Exhibit H (Overview of Bid
                     Evaluation). GPC reserves the right to contact any Bidder through the IE Website to request
                     additional information on any aspect of the Bid.

              8.3.   Initial Review of Bids
                     8.3.1. Deficient Bids. If, upon an initial review of the Bids a Bid is found to be a Deficient Bid,
                     then it may be placed on the Release List and released from 2023 Biomass RFP. GPC is not
                     required to contact any Bidder to obtain any omitted information.

                     8.3.2. Complete Bids. Bids that are complete and conform to the requirements of this 2023
                     Biomass RFP will be ranked and screened on economic value. Economically Non-Competitive
                     Bids may be placed on the Release List and released from the RFP. The remaining Bids will be
                     further evaluated for price, performance, and value to GPC’s energy portfolio. Based on such
                     criteria, the best Bids will be selected for inclusion in the Competitive Tier while the other Bids
                     may be placed on the Release List and released from the RFP.

                     8.3.3. Bids Released After Initial Review. Bidders will be notified of the placement of their Bid
                     on the Release List, and release thereof from this 2023 Biomass RFP, in accordance with the
                     Solicitation Schedule.

              8.4.   Competitive Tier Identified. Bidders will be notified of the selection of their Bids into the
                     Competitive Tier in accordance with the Solicitation Schedule. The Competitive Tier will be further
                     evaluated to determine whether such Bids are to be included on the Short List or the Reserve List
                     or whether they are to be subsequently placed on the Release List and released from this 2023
                     Biomass RFP.

              8.5.   Bid Security Mechanics
                     8.5.1. Draft Bid Security. Pursuant to Section 4.3 (Bid Security), for each Bid selected for the
                     Competitive Tier, Bidder must submit Bid Security. Each such Bidder that intends to provide Bid
                     Security in the form of a Surety Bond or a Letter of Credit must upload to its Bid book a draft
                     (unissued) Surety Bond or Letter of Credit for review and approval by the Evaluation Team, at
                     least five (5) Business Days before the Bid Security due date. Instructions for posting the draft
                     and final Bid Security will be available on the IE Website. The form of Surety Bond will also be
                     available on the IE Website.

                     8.5.2. Delivery of Bid Security. Bid Security in the form of cash must be submitted to GPC
                     through the IE Website according to the instructions posted on the Documents Page. Any Bid
                     Security submitted in the form of Surety Bond or Letter of Credit must be uploaded to the Bid
                     book and thereafter, mailed via a reputable overnight courier to arrive on or before the Bid Security
                     due date at the following address:

                         Georgia Power Company
                         c/o Southern Company Services Inc.
                         Attention: Assistant Treasurer
                         Bin No. SC1407
                         30 Ivan Allen Jr. Blvd.
                         Atlanta, GA 30308

                     8.5.3. Return of Bid Security. The Bid Security is fully refundable to the Bidder (i) if such Bid
                     is placed on the Release List, or (ii) on the date Generator and GPC execute the PPA for such
                     winning Bid. The Bid Security is non-refundable if a Bidder withdraws the Bid or otherwise fails to
                     execute the pro forma PPA after being selected for the Competitive Tier.

                     8.5.4. Conversion of Bid Security to Performance Security. If Bid Security is in the form of
                     cash or a Letter of Credit, Bidder may opt to convert and appropriately amend the Bid Security to

                     the required Performance Security at the time of PPA execution, or Bidder may replace the Bid
                     Security with another acceptable form of Performance Security pursuant to provisions of the PPA.

              8.6.   Bid Evaluation Components
                     8.6.1. Environmental Screening. All Bids in the Competitive Tier will undergo a
                     comprehensive review to ensure environmental compliance with the requirements of this 2023
                     Biomass RFP, which at a minimum considers the Environmental Compliance
                     Assessment/Requirements found in Exhibit C (Environmental Site Assessment Requirements).

                     8.6.2. Improvement Costs Imputed. Based on the information contained in each Bid selected
                     for the Competitive Tier, GPC will develop a cost estimate for Electric System improvements, if
                     any, as described in the clauses entitled “Interconnection Impacts” and “Delivery Impacts” in the
                     applicable interconnection scenario described under Section 1 of Exhibit B (Interconnection and
                     Delivery Requirements - General). Those costs will be included in evaluating the economics of
                     the Bid. In addition, this process will assist in identifying the potential Short List.

                     8.6.3. Due Diligence Portfolio Analysis. As discussed in more detail in Exhibit H (Overview
                     of Bid Evaluation), if the potential Short List includes Facilities connecting to the transmission
                     system such that their system impact costs are not independent, evaluations of the combined
                     effects of such Bids will be necessary to select the best combination of Bids.

                     8.6.4. Non-Price and Qualitative Considerations. Qualitative and non-price factors will be
                     considered in the detailed evaluation process. Exhibit H (Overview of Bid Evaluation) provides
                     additional information on these qualitative and non-price considerations. It is a Bidder’s
                     responsibility to submit additional information related to the proposal if such information will
                     materially improve the quality of its offer and GPC’s understanding thereof.

              8.7.   Short List, Reserve List, and Release List
                     8.7.1. Short List Identified. Based on results of the detailed evaluation, the best ranked Bids
                     will be chosen as the Short List. GPC will contact each Short-Listed Bidder to confirm that the
                     PPA conforms to the Facility’s specifications and Bidder’s business entity.

                     8.7.2. Reserve Lists and Release Lists. Any Bid not identified for the Short List may be placed
                     on the Reserve List. GPC will notify each Bidder eligible for the Reserve List that the Bid has
                     been identified for continued evaluation on the Reserve List. Any Bidder whose project is not
                     competitive will be notified that such Bid is no longer being considered for the Short List or
                     Reserve List. These Bids will be placed on the Release List and GPC will notify such Bidders of
                     removal from further consideration in this 2023 Biomass RFP.

                     8.7.3.       Short List, Reserve List, Release List Determination. In accordance with the
                     Solicitation Schedule, and as discussed in Section 8.6.3 (Due Diligence Portfolio Analysis) and
                     Section 8.7.1 (Short List Identified), upon completion of evaluation, Bidder will be notified of
                     whether its Bid is on the Short List, Reserve List, or Release List. GPC will contact each Bidder
                     with a Bid selected for the Short List to finalize and execute the PPA. A Bid on the Reserve List
                     is a project that is essentially on a waiting list that will continue to be under evaluation and may
                     move on to the Short List if a Short List Bidder withdraws or is unable to proceed to PPA
                     execution. A Bid on the Release List was determined to be non-competitive and will no longer be
                     considered for selection in this 2023 Biomass RFP. Release List determinations are final and will
                     not be reconsidered. As provided in Section 7.8 (Confidentiality), Bidder must not disclose the
                     status of its Bid, including its inclusion on the Short List, Reserve List, or Release List. By the end
                     of the 2023 Biomass RFP process, all Bids not placed on the Release List and not selected for
                     PPA contracting will be placed on the Reserve List. When GPC executes the winning PPAs and
                     files the executed winning PPAs with the Commission, all unselected Bids will be placed on the
                     Release List.

              8.8.   PPA Award and Execution. GPC will award and execute PPAs (subject to payment of the
                     Winner’s Fee) with the Winning Bidders whose Bids are on the Short List. A Winning Bidder will

                     PPAs)). As stated in Section 6.6.1 (Conformance of Pro Forma PPA), GPC will not accept

              8.9.   Facility Specifications. A Winning Bidder must obtain GPC’s written consent prior to making

              8.10. GPC Discretion in Contracting. GPC reserves the right, without qualification and in consultation
                    with the IE and Staff, to reject any, all, or portions of Bids received for failure to meet any criteria,

                    any of its Affiliates or IE for either rejection of Bidder’s Bid(s) or any other Bid(s) or for failure to
                    execute a PPA for any reason.


         PART 9.     CERTIFICATION

              9.1.   Commission Certification. Following completion of the 2023 Biomass RFP evaluation and
                     award process, GPC will seek Commission Certification, pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 46-3A-4, of each
                     of the PPAs executed in connection with this 2023 Biomass RFP. The Certification process will
                     take place under a separate Commission Docket and may take up to six months to complete,
                     unless otherwise expedited pursuant to the Procedural and Schedule Order to be issued by the
                     Commission. GPC’s performance of an executed PPA is conditioned on the Commission issuing
                     a Certification approving the executed PPA in a timely manner without material qualifications or
                     conditions adversely affecting GPC; otherwise, PPA Section 2.3.2 (Commission Certification)
                     provides that GPC may terminate the PPA without any further obligation.

                     Performance of an executed PPA is also conditioned upon, if required by applicable law, FERC
                     issuing an order accepting the PPA in a timely manner and without material qualification or
                     condition adversely affecting either Party to the PPA; otherwise, PPA Section 2.3.1 (FERC
                     Acceptance) provides that either Party may terminate the PPA without any further legal obligation.

                        Interconnection Study processes and the construction of Interconnection Facilities.

         19.    A description of the number and nature of new jobs, if any, the Project will provide, the amount of new
                capital investment that will be put into the Project, and other information relevant to economic
                development stemming from the Project.

                            EXHIBIT B - INTERCONNECTION AND DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS


         Each Bidder is responsible for determining all transmission interconnection and delivery-related rules,
         practices, and policies with which it must comply. Each Bid must comply with the general
         requirements outlined in Section 1 of this Exhibit B and with one of the interconnection options
         described in Sections 2 through 4 of this Exhibit B. This Exhibit B applies to a Facility associated with
         a New Greenfield Project, as well as to a Project associated with a Biomass Addition Project. In the
         Biomass Addition Project scenario, replace each reference to “Facility” in this Exhibit B (or, as
         applicable, in a defined term used in this Exhibit B) with “Project.”


         1.    Interconnection and Delivery Requirements – General
              The following interconnection requirements apply to all Bids, regardless of the Facility location.
               1.1.   Transmission Projected Commercial Operation Date. GPC may decline to select a Bid for the
                      Short List or to execute a PPA with any Bidder if, in the opinion of GPC, the transmission facilities
                      cannot be constructed in time to achieve Commercial Operation by the RCOD submitted by
                      Bidder. Except for the provision in Section 2.7 (Facility Interconnecting Directly to GPC) below for
                      a Facility interconnecting to the Southern Company Transmission System via GPC, Bidder
                      assumes all interconnection and delivery lead-time risk (if applicable) to meet the RCOD.
               1.2.   Bid Price Assumptions. This Exhibit B provides guidance for clarifying which interconnection
                      costs will be the responsibility of Bidder. Each Bid must state the assumptions regarding
                      interconnection and, if applicable, delivery costs included in its Bid price. Specifically, each Bid
                      must include details of these costs and refer to any completed or active Interconnection Study
                      results related to the Facility.
               1.3.   Bid Lead-Time Assumptions. Bidder must describe, with respect to the proposed Facility, its
                      current status within the applicable interconnection process and its ability to meet the proposed
                      RCOD based upon the applicable interconnection process timeline.
               1.4.   Interconnection Agreement Required. Each Winning Bidder must enter into an Interconnection
                      Agreement with the appropriate Interconnection Provider, depending on the geographic location
                      and interconnection configuration of the Facility. Each Bidder must contact the appropriate
                      Interconnection Provider to obtain all relevant information and interconnection requirements. The
                      submission of a Bid in response to this 2023 Biomass RFP does not constitute an interconnection
                      request or an Interconnection Agreement. Bidder is solely responsible for all fees, deposits, and
                      other charges in connection with its interconnection request and the Interconnection Agreement.
                      At any point in time, the Facility is prohibited from delivering output to the Point of Delivery that
                      exceeds the lesser of the Generating Capacity and the Interconnection Limit.
               1.5.   Timing and Notification of Initiating Interconnection Process. At the time of Bid submission,
                      Bidder must indicate if there is an existing interconnection request for the Facility, and if so, Bidder
                      also must identify the Interconnection Provider and request number/identifier. If an
                      interconnection request has not been submitted at the time of Bid submission, Bidder must initiate
                      the interconnection process with the appropriate Interconnection Provider no later than seven
                      Days after notification that such Bid is on the Short List (as discussed in RFP Section 8.7.1 (Short
                      List Identified).

         2.    Interconnection with the Southern Company Transmission System
              The following requirements apply to a Bid for a Facility interconnecting to the transmission system of
              GPC or one of its regulated electric utility Affiliates (i.e., Alabama Power Company or Mississippi Power
              Company).
               2.1.   Procedure Guidance. If the Facility will interconnect to the Southern Company Transmission
                      System, the evaluation of the Bid will assume Bidder has executed either the small generator
                      interconnection agreement (“SGIA”) or a large generator interconnection agreement (“LGIA”) and
                      that either the small generator interconnection procedure (“SGIP”) or large generator


         2023 NEW BIOMASS RFP                                                                                    Page 32 of 58
                                                       www.gonitro.com

STF-JKA-1-24 Attachment E.pdf
                                                            2023 BIOMASS RFP FOR NEW BIOMASS GENERATION
                                                                             FINAL APPROVED - JUNE 16, 2023


                     interconnection procedure (“LGIP”) will apply. Generally, the SGIP is utilized for generators 20
                     MW or smaller and the LGIP for generators larger than 20 MW. The Southern Company
                     Transmission System includes facilities owned by GPC or one of its regulated electric utility
                     Affiliates (Alabama Power Company or Mississippi Power Company). The prompt submission of
                     an accurate and complete application and prompt return of agreements will reduce the overall
                     timeframe of the interconnection process. Each Bidder must determine all rules, practices,
                     policies, and timelines with which its Facility must comply to interconnect with the Southern
                     Company Transmission System. Bidder may obtain additional information on Southern
                     Company’s OASIS web site found at: http://www.oasis.oati.com/SOCO/index.html.
              2.2.   Bidder Cost Responsibility. If the Facility will interconnect with the Southern Company
                     Transmission System, Bidder is responsible for all Interconnection Study-related costs, in addition
                     to the interconnection costs and risk up to the POI. These costs generally include equipment such
                     as the Facility generator step-up (“GSU”) transformer (for conversion up to the interconnecting
                     voltage level), Facility-side generator interrupting device, all Station Service equipment, and any
                     additional equipment (such as a utility-owned interrupting device and metering needed to connect
                     to the transmission facilities), as well as any additional real property for the interconnection
                     substation and access. In addition, if applicable, Bidder is responsible for the costs, risk, and
                     coordination of all Affected System Upgrades. It is Bidder’s responsibility to determine and
                     consider all information regarding interconnection costs in preparing its Bid.
              2.3.   Interconnection Impacts. Interconnection impacts to the Electric System are unique to the
                     specific design and location of each Facility and may require new or modified equipment beyond
                     the POI. For a Facility interconnecting to the Southern Company Transmission System, any costs
                     for new or modified equipment on the Southern Company Transmission System beyond the POI
                     will be imputed to the Bid during the Bid evaluation and should not be included in the Bid price.
                     However, as stated above in Section 2.2 (Bidder Cost Responsibility) of this Exhibit B any costs
                     associated with Affected System Upgrades are solely the Bidder’s responsibility and should be
                     included in the Bid price.
                     A Winning Bidder may be required to fund or provide security for new or modified equipment
                     beyond the POI. However, if a Winning Bidder incurs interconnection-related costs for new or
                     modified equipment on the Southern Company Transmission System beyond the POI, the costs
                     will be refunded to Bidder, or security will be released, after the Facility achieves Commercial
                     Operation.

                     If a winning Bid has associated interconnection impacts to any Affected System, such that the
                     Affected System must add, modify, or upgrade its Electric System, Bidder must coordinate with
                     the Affected System with respect to identification, planning, and construction of, and payment of
                     costs for, such additions, modifications, or upgrades. Bidders must contemplate such schedule
                     and cost impacts in each Bid. Such Bidder may be required to execute an Affected System
                     Agreement. Any costs related to such Affected System Agreement are the sole responsibility of
                     Bidder and will not be reimbursed by GPC through this 2023 Biomass RFP.

              2.4.   Delivery Impacts. From the Bids selected in the Competitive Tier, pursuant to RFP Section 8.4
                     (Competitive Tier Identified), GPC will develop a cost estimate for Electric System improvements,
                     if any, to the Southern Company Transmission System, the Georgia ITS, or both, necessary to
                     deliver the Energy from the POI to GPC’s customers. These costs will be imputed to the Bid. If
                     Electric System improvement costs are anticipated to be incurred by GPC beyond the POI to
                     deliver the full output of the Facility, Bidder will be required, before GPC commences construction
                     of such facilities or incurs costs on behalf of Bidder, to provide Additional Security that GPC may
                     draw upon in the event of early termination of the PPA prior to Commercial Operation. After the
                     Facility achieves Commercial Operation, GPC will return such Additional Security to Bidder.
              2.5.   Construction of Southern Company Transmission System Facilities. Any Electric System
                     improvement, modification, or new facility that will become part of the Southern Company
                     Transmission System must be owned by, and will be designed, procured, and constructed by, as
                     applicable, GPC, Alabama Power Company, or Mississippi Power Company.

                     with an access route to the ICF Site acceptable to GPC, as well as any necessary encroachment
                     agreement, consent, or similar document. All necessary property right documents must be
                     acceptable to GPC and on its standard terms and conditions; all property rights documentation
                     must be timely obtained, negotiated, and executed. During the Interconnection Study process,
                     interconnection facility and access route sitting will be discussed and agreed upon by GPC and
                     Bidder. Bidder also must coordinate with GPC to prepare to GPC’s satisfaction the property (e.g.,
                     grading and preparation of the ICF Site and suitable access route) and turn access to the property
                     over to GPC by no later than one year prior to the projected transmission in-service date. After
                     initial preparation of the access route, a Winning Bidder also must maintain, at its own expense,
                     the access route in accordance with GPC’s standards and to GPC’s satisfaction throughout the
                     PPA Term.
                     2.7.2. Notice to Proceed. A Winning Bidder whose Facility will interconnect with GPC must
                     submit a notice to proceed to initiate the construction of Interconnection Facilities by 14 Days
                     after the Commission issues the Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity, if the
                     Interconnection Agreement has already been executed. Otherwise, depending upon when Bidder
                     initiates the interconnection process and so long as the System Impact Study has been completed
                     and the Facility Study stage is in process, Bidder may be required to enter into an Engineering
                     and Procurement Agreement with GPC to assume cost responsibility and allow pre-construction
                     activities, such as engineering work and procurement of long lead-time materials, to commence
                     prior to execution of the Interconnection Agreement.
                     2.7.3. Failure to Achieve Commercial Operation by the PPA RCOD. PPA Section 9.3.1
                     (RCOD Extension) provides relief from payment of liquidated delay damages if Commercial
                     Operation will not be achieved prior to the PPA RCOD for reasons wholly and solely caused by
                     the inability of GPC to construct the Interconnection Facilities (and not caused by Generator’s
                     (i.e., Winning Bidder’s) failure to comply with the provisions of PPA Section 9.1 (Interconnection).
              2.8.   Additional Guidance for Facilities Interconnecting to the Southern Company Transmission

         3.   Interconnection to the Electric System of an ITS Participant
              The following requirements apply to a Bid for a Facility interconnecting with the transmission system of
              an ITS Participant (Georgia Transmission Corporation, MEAG Power, or Dalton).
              3.1.   Procedure Guidance. If the Facility will interconnect to a transmission facility owned by an ITS
                     Participant, such Bidder’s interconnection application and Interconnection Agreement will be with
                     the applicable ITS Participant. While ITS Participants utilize Interconnection Study processes
                     comparable to GPC’s process, Bidder is responsible for determining all rules, practices, policies,
                     and timelines with which it must comply.
              3.2.   Bidder Cost Responsibility. If Bidder’s Facility will interconnect with an ITS Participant, such
                     Bidder is responsible for all Interconnection Study-related costs, in addition to any interconnection
                     costs and risks up to and beyond the POI associated with any ITS Participant (non-GPC) owned
                     transmission facilities. These costs generally include equipment such as the ITS Participant-
                     owned interconnection substation, the GSU transformer (for conversion up to the interconnecting
                     voltage level), Facility-side generator interrupting device, all Station Service equipment, and any
                     additional equipment (such as a utility-owned interrupting device and metering needed to connect
                     to the Interconnection Facilities), as well as any additional real property for the interconnection
                     substation and access. In addition, if applicable, a Winning Bidder is responsible for the costs,
                     risks, and coordination of Affected System Upgrades. It is Bidder’s responsibility to determine and
                     review all information regarding interconnection costs.
              3.3.   Interconnection Impacts. Interconnection impacts to the Electric System are unique to the
                     specific design and location of each Facility and may require new or modified equipment beyond
                     the POI. If a Facility is interconnecting with an ITS Participant, GPC will not impute to the Bid any
                     costs for any new or modified ITS Participant-owned transmission Interconnection Facilities
                     beyond the POI. Such costs must be determined by Bidder and included in the Bid price.
                     However, any costs beyond the POI on the Southern Company Transmission System will be
                     imputed to the Bid during the Bid evaluation and should not be included in the Bid price. If a
                     Winning Bidder incurs interconnection-related costs for new or modified equipment beyond the
                     POI on the Southern Company Transmission System, such Bidder must provide Additional
                     Security for design, procurement, and installation of that equipment. However, the Additional
                     Security will be returned to Bidder after the Facility achieves Commercial Operation. Any costs
                     associated with ITS Participant-owned Interconnection Facilities or other Affected System
                     Upgrades are solely Bidder’s responsibility and should be included in the Bid price.
              3.4.   Delivery Impacts. From the Bids selected in the Competitive Tier, GPC will develop a cost
                     estimate for Electric System improvements, if any, to the Southern Company Transmission
                     System, the Georgia ITS, or both necessary to deliver the Energy from the POI to GPC’s
                     customers. These costs will be included in evaluating the economics of the Bid. If Electric System
                     improvement costs are anticipated to be incurred by GPC to deliver the full output of the Facility,
                     Bidder must provide Additional Security before GPC commences design, procurement, and
                     construction of such facilities or incurs costs on the Bidder’s behalf. GPC will return the Additional
                     Security to Bidder once the Facility achieves Commercial Operation.
              3.5.   Facility Specifications. Each Bid must include the Facility data and specifications requested in
                     the Bid form in order to allow the Evaluation Team, during the Bid evaluation, to identify any
                     required modifications to the Southern Company Transmission System, Georgia ITS, or both that
                     would be necessary to interconnect and deliver Energy from the Facility to GPC’s customers.

                             EXHIBIT C - ENVIRONMENTAL SITE ASSESSMENT REQUIREMENTS


         All Bid Submittals

         From an environmental perspective, and in GPC’s view, the best property for siting generation is property that
         has been comprehensively evaluated and determined to either have no past or present environmental
         concerns, or if concerns are identified, they can be avoided through generation technology or Site
         configuration. Where environmental impacts are possible, it is necessary to fully address impacts through
         avoidance, minimization, regulatory permitting and compliance, and possibly mitigation.

         Each Bid will consider and address, at a minimum, the items outlined below. If a Bidder does not believe an
         item is applicable to its Project, Bidder must provide a statement as to why.

             1. Waters of the U.S.
             2. State Waters (where applicable)
             3. 100-Year Floodplains
             4. NPDES Construction Stormwater Permitting
             5. Federal and State Protected Species and Species of Concern
             6. Cultural Resources (Archaeology and Historical Architecture)
             7. Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasures (SPCC) Compliance
             8. Any contamination or potentially contaminated soil or groundwater (A Phase I Environmental Site
                Assessment may be required)
             9. Air Quality (e.g., permitting of timber/other open burning, proximity to non-attainment areas, etc.)
             10. Local government permitting, ordinances, and restrictions
         With each Bid submittal, Bidder must provide a notarized Environmental Compliance Affidavit found in Exhibit
         D (Environmental Compliance Affidavit).

         Environmental Assurances Due at Competitive Tier Selection

         GPC requires assurances from each Bidder that due diligence concerning the protection of Project-related
         environmental factors has been conducted and will continue to be observed. Efforts should be made by Bidder
         to avoid environmental impacts, but where impacts are unavoidable, efforts should be made by Bidder to
         minimize and mitigate environmental impacts accordingly. Therefore, Bidder is required at a minimum to
         address the above factors with its Bid to allow GPC to independently assess what potential environmental
         impacts may result from construction and operation of the Project. Environmental assurances should be
         submitted once Bidder is selected to the Competitive Tier. Failure to address the items below will result in an
         incomplete Bid.

         If a Bid is selected to the Competitive Tier, Bidder must submit to GPC the Environmental Assurances
         outlined below by the due date noted in the Solicitation Schedule.

         Bidder should provide a preliminary Site plan that includes all environmental sensitivities overlayed with areas
         of proposed panels or land disturbance actions.

             A. Waters of the United States
                 1.    Documentation indicating that the final Site design accommodates final U.S. Army Corps of
                       Engineers wetland delineation determination, protective buffers, and mitigation actions needed
                       to satisfy the Section 404 permitting authority, as appropriate. Bidder must provide to GPC a
                       copy of any final permit issued by the U.S. Army Corp of Engineers for the Project upon receipt.
                       (a)     A completed Waters of the U.S. (WOTUS) survey and findings report. The WOTUS
                               survey must be no older than 5-years from date of Environmental Assurances submittal.


         2023 NEW BIOMASS RFP                                                                               Page 40 of 58

                                                                              FINAL APPROVED - JUNE 16, 2023


                            The WOTUS evaluation should be up to date with current regulations in place at the time
                            of Competitive Tier selection.
                     (b)    A preliminary Site plan/figure with WOTUS delineation shown.
                     (c)    If WOTUS impacts will be required, provide an intended permitting strategy.
                     (d)    Any Agency coordination associated with WOTUS, including jurisdictional verifications,
                            permitting, or mitigation efforts.
            B. State Waters and Protected Buffers
                1.   If the Project is subject to regulations that require waters to have protective buffers, those buffers

                2.   If impacts to buffers are required, provide a statement acknowledging and outlining any

            C. Cultural Resources
                1.   Desktop review for archaeological and architectural resources. This will include, minimally:
                     A review of the Georgia Natural, Archaeological, and Historic Resources Geographic Information
                     System (GNAHRGIS) database for recorded archaeological sites and historic buildings, as well
                     as previous surveys conducted in the area.
                     The National Register of Historic Places (NRHP) database maintained by the National Park

                     Other online resources include:

                                        EXHIBIT H - OVERVIEW OF BID EVALUATION
         I.      Overview

         Each Bid submitted into this 2023 Biomass RFP will be evaluated and ranked based on the net present value
         benefits to GPC’s customers on a dollar per MW hour ($/MWh) basis. The net benefit of a Bid is calculated by
         subtracting the costs customers will pay if the Bid is selected from the projected costs customers would
         otherwise incur if the Bid were not selected. GPC will consider the Bid costs, the Projected Avoided Costs, any
         transmission and distribution costs, and will perform a portfolio analysis to consider the impact of such costs.
         These evaluation components are described in further detail below.

         II.     Bid Costs

         Bid costs are the costs GPC customers will pay for implementing the Bid.

         The primary component of these costs are the costs paid by GPC to the Generator for the Renewable Energy.
         These costs are dependent upon the Bid price of the Renewable Energy and the anticipated quantity of
         Renewable Energy to be delivered throughout the PPA Term. GPC’s evaluation assumes 100% of the Project’s
         Profile is delivered.

         III.    Projected Avoided Costs

         Projected Avoided Costs represent the costs GPC would incur to provide the same service as would be
         provided by the proposed Project. Discussed more fully in Docket No. 44160, components of this cost include
         Deferred Generation Capacity, and Avoided Energy Costs. Because Projected Avoided Costs are calculated
         on an hourly basis, the total evaluated projected avoided cost benefit will vary depending on the Project’s
         Profile reflected in the Bid.

                 A.      Generation Costs – Determining the Deferred Generation Capacity Costs:

         The Deferred Generation Capacity cost is a measure of the effective load carrying capability (“ELCC”)
         consistent with the technology included in the Bid.

                 B.      Generation Costs – determining the Avoided Energy Costs:

         Each Bid’s contribution to reducing the aggregate annual system generation fleet fuel and variable cost will be
         calculated by multiplying the projected hourly avoided energy rates in $/MWh by the Project’s Profile in MWh
         for each Annual Period based on Bidders’ provided Profile. The Profile submitted by Bidder will be adjusted to
         account for transmission losses.

         IV.     Evaluation of Transmission/Distribution System Impacts of Bids

         An assessment of the transmission/distribution impact of each Bid is an integral part of the total cost analysis.
         Each Bid is evaluated from a transmission/distribution perspective in order to assess the additional investment
         to the existing transmission/distribution system required to interconnect and deliver the proposed generation
         to GPC’s customers from the COD through the PPA Term.

         For Bid evaluation purposes, the cost that would be borne by GPC of such transmission/distribution
         improvements over the PPA Term is imputed to the Bid.

         As part of the evaluation of transmission/distribution impacts of each Bid, GPC will further assess any project
         scheduling risk posed by the transmission/distribution system evaluation, including the ability of the proposed
         Project to meet the RCOD.

         V.      Due Diligence Portfolio Analysis

         Portfolio analysis will be necessary if the potential Short List includes Projects connecting to the Electric
         System such that the transmission/distribution cost of one Bid impacts the transmission/distribution cost of

         2023 NEW BIOMASS RFP                                                                                Page 51 of 58
                                                      www.gonitro.com

STF-JKA-1-24 Attachment E.pdf
                                                                2023 BIOMASS RFP FOR NEW BIOMASS GENERATION
                                                                                 FINAL APPROVED - JUNE 16, 2023


         another Bid. In such case, evaluations of the combined effects of such Bids would be necessary to select the
         best combination of Bids.

         VI.     Evaluation of Proposals with Unequal Contract Term Lengths

         GPC will consider Bids offering a Term of 10, 15, 20, 25 or 30 Annual Periods at Bidder’s option. For evaluation
         of Bids with unequal contract Term lengths, GPC will utilize its Projected Avoided Costs to enable evaluation
         of Bids on an equivalent basis given the unequal Term lengths, which is consistent with how GPC has
         evaluated Bids with different length terms in prior RFPs.

         VII.    Non-Price and Qualitative Considerations

         Although GPC’s evaluation will primarily focus on a Bid’s economic net benefits, other qualitative and non-
         price attributes will be considered, especially where one or more Bids offer a substantially similar economic
         benefit. It is a Bidder’s responsibility to submit additional information related to its Bid if such information will
         materially improve the quality of its offer or GPC’s understanding thereof. The non-price factors listed below
         may be used by GPC to select the winning bids:

                 •    Reliability associated with the Facility location interconnecting to the Southern Company
                      Transmission System;
                 •    Locating the Facility in Georgia;
                 •    Bidder development experience;
                 •    Environmental Site Assessment;
                 •    Permit status; and
                 •    Bidder’s compliance history.

                                          EXHIBIT I – BID ASSIGNMENT GUIDELINES


                1.1 Overview.

                      1.1.1        A Bid may only be assigned, including any assignment of a previously assigned Bid
                      to the original Bidder, with the prior written notice to and consent of GPC in accordance with the
                      requirements of this Exhibit I (Bid Assignment Guidelines).

                      1.1.2        For each proposed Bid Assignment, Bidder and the proposed Bid assignee named in
                      and executing the consent request (“Bid Assignee”) must review the requirements of this Exhibit
                      I (Bid Assignment Guidelines) and agree to the Request for Georgia Power Company’s Consent
                      to Bid Assignment included as Attachment 1 to this Exhibit I (Bid Assignment Guidelines)
                      (“Consent Request”).

                      1.1.3         These guidelines are limited to Bid assignments during the 2023 Biomass RFP Bid
                      solicitation phase (each such attempted or completed assignment, a “Bid Assignment”). For
                      assignments, transfers, or other changes after execution of the PPA and IA, the contracting party
                      must comply with requirements in such agreements. For purposes of this Exhibit I (Bid
                      Assignment Guidelines) a Change of Control of a Bidder will be deemed an assignment, subject
                      to the provisions hereof. For purposes of this Exhibit I (Bid Assignment Guidelines), a “Change of
                      Control” is any transaction or series of related transactions which, if consummated, would result
                      in Bidder being an Affiliate of another ultimate parent entity immediately after the transaction or
                      series of transactions. For purposes of this definition, the ultimate parent entity is the Person who
                      directly or indirectly controls 50% or more of Bidder’s outstanding capital stock or other equity
                      interests having ordinary voting power and who does not itself have an ultimate parent entity.

                1.2       Notice and Consent Requirements.
                      1.2.1        Notice Requirements.
                          A.       Assignment Before Competitive Tier List Notification. If Bidder intends to assign
                          its Bid, Bidder must provide GPC with prior written notice through the IE in the form of the
                          Consent Request of (i) Bidder’s intent to assign the Bid, (ii) the name of the proposed Bid
                          Assignee, (iii) the Required Information required under Section 1.3 below with respect to such
                          Bid Assignee, and (iv) Bidder’s request for GPC to consent to the Bid Assignment. The
                          Consent Request and all required information must be submitted to GPC through the IE at
                          least 15 days before the proposed effective date of the Bid Assignment, but in no event less
                          than 15 days before the Competitive Tier Selection Date as noted in the Solicitation Schedule.
                          A Bid may not be assigned after it has been included on the Competitive Tier List.

                         SCHEDULE OF DEFINED TERMS AND RULES OF CONSTRUCTION

         This Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP uses the defined terms identified in this Schedule, or in the body of
         this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP, and the rules of construction identified in this Schedule.
         2023 IRP Update: GPC’s 2023 Integrated Resource Plan Update as approved by the Commission in Docket
         No. 55378.
         2023 IRP Update Final Order: The Order from the 2023 IRP Update as approved by the Commission in
         Docket No. 55378.
         AC: Alternating current.
         Access Route: The suitable all-weather access route from the nearest public roadway to the Point of
         Interconnection that is acceptable to GPC and that must be always available to GPC (24/7/365(366))
         throughout the IA term to facilitate GPC’s construction, operation, or maintenance of the Interconnection
         Facilities or other related GPC activity.
         Affected System: An Electric System utility other than the GPC Electric System or an electric facility owner
         whose facilities require additions, modifications, or upgrades that are necessary for safe and reliable operation
         of the Electric System during parallel operation of the Facility, other than those required due to GPC’s
         designation of the Facility output to serve GPC’s customers (i.e., to deliver the energy from the Point of Delivery
         to GPC’s customers).
         Affected System Upgrade(s): Any addition, modification, or upgrade to an Affected System’s Electric System
         that would be necessary for safe and reliable operation of the Electric System during parallel operation of the
         Facility. Each addition, modification, or upgrade will be constructed and owned by that Affected System.
         Affiliate: For any specific Person, any other Person directly or indirectly controlling, controlled by, or under
         common control with that Person. For purposes of this definition, “control” when used regarding any entity
         means the power to direct the management and policies of the entity, directly or indirectly, whether through
         the ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise. A Person directly or indirectly owning 50% or
         more of the outstanding stock or other equity interest of another Person has “control” of that Person. The terms
         “controlling” and “controlled” have meanings correlative to “control.”
         Affiliate Bid Team: As defined in Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(d), any GPC Affiliate that intends to submit
         a Bid into this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP, as well as any other Persons acting for that Affiliate or on its
         behalf in support of the development and submission of any Bid.
         AGC: See Automatic Generation Control.
         AIER: See Associated Interchange Energy Rate.
         Alternative Bid: Defined in Section 7.3.1 (Alternative Bid).
         Ancillary Services: All commercial products other than electrical output that are produced by or related to the
         Facility, including Electrical Products, Environmental Attributes, any other environmental or regulatory credits,
         or allowances resulting from operation of the Facility, and any other benefit GPC otherwise would have realized
         from or related to the Facility if GPC rather than Seller had constructed, owned, or operated the Facility, it
         being the Parties’ intent that all the benefits and entitlements in addition to electrical output that flow to the
         owner or operator of the Facility, whether existing as of the Effective Date or at any time during the PPA Term
         or Facility Design Life, belong to GPC at no additional cost to GPC. However, if a commercial product is not
         produced by the Facility, Seller will not be required to acquire the commercial product in the market to comply
         with the Awarded Contract. Ancillary Services do not include: (i) any federal, state, or local tax attributes arising
         from the ownership of the Facility, including investment tax credits (ITC), production tax credits (PTC), or
         depreciation deductions; (ii) grants instead of ITC or any similar financial payment or grant regarding the
         Facility or the metered electric energy output from the Facility; or (iii) the metered electric energy produced by
         the Facility.
         Annual Period(s): Any one of a succession of consecutive 12-month periods during the PPA Term beginning
         on December 1st and ending on the following November 30th, except that the first Annual Period will begin on
         the Delivery Commencement Date and end the immediately following November 30th.
         ASC: The FASB Accounting Standards Codification.

         Associated Interchange Energy Rate (AIER): The rate determined for each hour, based on the variable
         dispatch cost of the incremental resources that serve the collective obligations of the Southern Companies.
         Automatic Generation Control (AGC): The equipment and capability of a Facility to automatically adjust
         energy output within the applicable balancing authority for purposes of interchange balancing, and specifically,
         the Facility’s capability to accept a set point electronically and the automatic adjustment and regulation of the
         Facility’s energy output to meet that set point.
         Awarded Contract: An executed PPA or BTA, as applicable, between GPC and a Seller (i.e., Winning Bidder).
         Battery Energy Storage System (BESS): An on-Site battery energy storage system that is interconnected to
         the GPC Electric System at the POI.
         BESS: See Battery Energy Storage System.
         BESS with Renewable Resource: A BESS paired with an existing or previously certified Renewable
         Resource.
         Bid: As more fully delineated in Part 7 (Submission Requirements), each separate bid submitted into this
         Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP.
         Bid Assignment: Defined in Exhibit F (Bid Assignment Guidelines).
         Bid Book: Each Participant’s private electronic file on the IE Website in which all Submission-specific
         documents submitted by the Participants are stored and a record of all IE Website communications are
         recorded.
         Bid Due Date: The date and time specified for complete submission of Bids into this Winter 2027_2028 BESS
         RFP, as shown in the Solicitation Schedule (Section 1.1.1 (Solicitation Schedule)) or, if applicable, as modified
         in accordance with Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP terms and conditions.
         Bid Fee: The non-refundable $20,000 fee Bidder must submit with each Bid to defray costs of the RFP
         Process.
         Bid Form: The electronic form found on the IE Website through which a Participant offers its Submission.
         Bid Information: The ongoing status of any Bid or potential Bid, and any information submitted, exchanged,
         or discussed between the Bidder, Staff, the IE, and GPC (any exchange or discussion to occur in accordance
         with the guidelines of this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP and Commission Rules).
         Bid Period: The period from the Bid Period open date until the Bid Due Date, as shown in the Solicitation
         Schedule (Section 1.1.1 (Solicitation Schedule)).
         Bid Security: Security provided by Bidder for each Bid that advances to the Competitive Tier in the form of:
         (i) cash; (ii) Surety Bond; or (iii) a Letter of Credit, in the amount required by Section 4.6 (Bid Security).
         Bidder: As applicable, each Person contemplating submission of a Bid or submitting a Bid into this Winter
         2027_2028 BESS RFP.
         Build Transfer Agreement (BTA): Build Transfer Agreement to be entered into by GPC and a Winning Bidder
         (or other Person identified as BTA counterparty (i.e., Seller) as allowed by this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP).
         Business Day: Any Day except: (i) Saturday; (ii) Sunday; and (iii) any Day on which banking institutions in
         Atlanta, Georgia are closed because of a federal holiday.
         Certification: The Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity GPC will seek from the Commission under
         O.C.G.A. § 46-3A-4 for each Awarded Contract and any winning Company-Owned Proposal.
         Certified Diverse Supplier: Any contractor or supplier that falls into at least one of the following business
         groups: (i) Small Disadvantaged Business; (ii) Woman-Owned Business; (iii) HUBZone Business; (iv) Veteran-
         Owned Business; (v) Minority-Owned Business; (vi) LGBT-Owned Business; or (vii) Disability-Owned
         Business, as those groups are defined by United States Small Business Administration.
         Closing: The closing of the BTA transaction, as will be further described in the BTA.
         COD: See Commercial Operation Date.
         Commercial Operation: The Facility’s ability to charge and discharge energy on a reliable basis according to
         Awarded Contract requirements.

                              Winter 2027_2028 BESS Request for Proposals

         Georgia Power Company’s 2023 IRP Update identified a need for additional BESS capacity resources. On
         April 26, 2024, the Commission issued the 2023 IRP Update Final Order concerning the 2023 IRP Update.
         The 2023 IRP Final Order amended and approved the Stipulation that requires GPC to conduct a Winter
         2027_2028 BESS solicitation to address approximately 500MW of BESS capacity needs identified by GPC.

         GPC issues this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP to procure BESS resources that meet GPC’s identified capacity
         needs, including: (i) Standalone BESS with grid charging capability that has a transmission interconnection
         study completed or is in-progress and requires minimal transmission improvements (those that can be
         completed on or before November 30, 2027); and (ii) BESS with Renewable Resource and grid charging
         capability located at an existing or previously certified solar site that has a POI that allows winter discharging
         of the BESS.

         In consultation with Staff and the IE, GPC may revise its capacity need forecast to reduce, eliminate, or
         increase the amount of capacity sought change the Solicitation Schedule at any point during the RFP process.
         Further, the RFP Documents are subject to modification or withdrawal at any time in the sole discretion of GPC.


         PART 1.        RFP SOLICITATION SCHEDULE AND FRAMEWORK

                1.1.   RFP Solicitation Schedule.

                     1.1.2. Affiliate Bid and Company-Owned Proposal Submission Deadline. Any Company-
                     Owned Proposal or Affiliate Bid must be submitted through the IE Website by 12:00 p.m. (Noon)
                     ET on the date shown in the Solicitation Schedule. Participant must initiate Company-Owned
                     Proposal submission before 10:00 a.m. ET on the Company-Owned Proposal due date. Any
                     Company-Owned Proposal submitted after the deadline will not be accepted.

                     1.1.3. Bid Due Date/Time. Each Bid must be submitted through the IE Website by 12:00 PM
                     (Noon) ET on the date shown in the Solicitation Schedule. Late Bid submissions will not be
                     accepted. To ensure timely Bid submittal and fair treatment of all Bidders, Bidders must initiate
                     submission of each Bid no later than the Bid Due Date and by the time identified on the IE
                     Website. Each Bidder will receive an email acknowledgment for each Bid submitted.

              1.2.   Independent Evaluator.
                     1.2.1. Purpose and Role of IE. GPC is utilizing the IE to oversee this Winter 2027_2028 BESS
                     RFP and to serve as the point of contact for all Participants. As provided in the RFP Rule, the IE
                     serves to maintain fairness, transparency, and consistency in the RFP Process, which helps to
                     prevent claims of favoritism in the evaluation and advancement of Submissions. Commission
                     Rules require GPC to retain an IE, who is selected by and reports to the Commission in carrying
                     out its duties and assisting with development of this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP and evaluation
                     of Submissions.

                     1.2.2. The IE Website. The IE Website serves as the required forum for all RFP communication
                     among the Evaluation Team, Participants, and all interested Persons. Any Participant or
                     interested Person may only communicate with GPC, the IE, or Staff regarding this Winter
                     2027_2028 BESS RFP through the IE Website. If any Participant or interested Person directs
                     questions regarding any RFP information to Staff or GPC, as applicable, will direct the Participant
                     or interested Person to the IE Website to ensure all communications are documented and treated
                     consistently, fairly, and transparently. If a Participant attempts to make contact outside the process
                     described in this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP, Participant will be directed to the IE Website for
                     all information and communication and will be reported to the IE for a violation of this Winter
                     2027_2028 BESS RFP requirement. Repeated violation of this requirement may result in the
                     Bidder being prohibited from participating and all Bids from the Bidder being disqualified.

              1.3.   Standards of Conduct.
                     1.3.1. Standards of Conduct Regarding Affiliate Bids. GPC Affiliates may submit Bids in
                     response to this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP. Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(d) incorporates
                     measures to segregate the Evaluation Team and any Affiliate Bid Team. The lists identifying the
                     Evaluation Team and, if applicable, Affiliate Bid Team members are found on the Commission’s
                     website under Docket No. 55763 and on the “Documents” page of the IE Website. Each
                     Participant is encouraged to review these lists. Except when communication is facilitated by Staff
                     and monitored by the IE, each Bidder is prohibited from discussing this Winter 2027_2028 BESS
                     RFP and any related documents with the Evaluation Team. GPC implemented specific controls
                     to ensure RFP-related information is confined to the appropriate team. Additionally, before receipt

                     1.3.2. Standards of Conduct for Company-Owned Proposals Submitted by the Company-
                     Owned Proposal Team. To meet its identified capacity needs, GPC may develop and submit one
                     or more Company-Owned Proposals in response to this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP for
                     Facilities that would be owned and operated by GPC. GPC must submit any Company-Owned
                     Proposal directly to the IE by the date shown in the Solicitation Schedule. Company-Owned
                     Proposals may include partnership arrangements or agreements between GPC and third parties
                     or contractors that may collaborate to submit a joint proposal.

                          A.       GPC Contractors. To ensure fairness to all Participants, the COP Team will not
                          share with a GPC Contractor, or potential GPC Contractor, any non-public information about
                          the RFP Process. No GPC Contractor or GPC Contractor Affiliate is allowed to submit a Bid
                          in this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP for the same Facility submitted in any Company-Owned
                          Proposal.
                          B.      GPC Internal Communications. While not required under Commission Rules, GPC
                          voluntarily imposes the Affiliate communications restrictions set out in Commission Rule 515-
                          3-4-.04(3) to restrict communications between the Evaluation Team and the COP Team,
                          except as noted regarding Specialized Technical Support Personnel in Section 1.3.2.C
                          (Company-Owned Proposal Team and Specialized Technical Support Personnel). No COP
                          Team member may share with any Primary Evaluation Team member any Company-Owned
                          Proposal information related to the costs or specific characteristics of any aspect of any
                          Company-Owned Proposal or its proposed Facility, except for communications facilitated by
                          the IE and Staff and necessary for evaluation of a Company-Owned Proposal. In addition to
                          the requirements of Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(d) establishing standards of conduct
                          regarding any Evaluation Team member and any Affiliate Bid Team member, no COP Team
                          member will be a member of any Affiliate Bid Team nor communicate with any Affiliate Bid
                          Team member in violation of Commission Rule 515-3-4-.04(3)(d). GPC will not tolerate
                          conduct or communication regarding the development of any Company-Owned Proposal by
                          the COP Team that would unfairly influence the design or evaluation processes for this
                          Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP.
                          C.       Company-Owned Proposal Team and Specialized Technical Support
                          Personnel. The COP Team will develop any Company-Owned Proposal in a manner that
                          preserves the integrity and fairness of the RFP Process for all Participants. Due to their
                          functional expertise and breadth of job responsibilities, two Specialized Technical Support
                          Personnel in the SCS Treasury Department will be involved both with development of a
                          Company-Owned Proposal and with certain aspects of this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP.
                          The RFP information provided to Specialized Technical Support Personnel is limited to the
                          scope of their job responsibilities. Specialized Technical Support Personnel serving as
                          members of both the Evaluation Team and the COP Team will not be allowed to determine
                          the total economic benefit of Submissions. GPC voluntarily posted a list of the COP Team
                          members on the IE Website, and the Evaluation Team and the COP Team lists will
                          separately identify any Specialized Technical Support Personnel who serve on both teams.
                          GPC will not substitute any Specialized Technical Support Personnel without first consulting
                          Staff and the IE.

                     changes (as described in Section 7.4.8.A (Material Conformance)) will be considered.


         PART 2.     PRODUCTS AND RESOURCES SOUGHT IN THIS WINTER 2027_2028 BESS RFP

              2.1.   Products Sought. GPC seeks offers to sell capacity from Facilities that can commence delivery
                     in the 2025 - 2027 timeframe. A Submission may offer any reliable Facility that can meet the
                     requirements of this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP, including but not limited to: (i) Standalone
                     BESS with grid charge capability and a duration of four hours; and (ii) BESS with Renewable
                     Resource, with grid charge capability and a duration of four hours.

              2.2.   Facility Ownership Structures. Under this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP, Bidders may submit
                     Bids proposing one of two ownership structures for Facilities:
                     2.2.1. Seller-Owned Facilities. GPC will accept Bids for Facilities where Seller will retain
                     Facility ownership. The Awarded Contract that a Winning Bidder would execute would be a PPA,
                     where GPC would have exclusive rights to the Facility’s capacity.

                     2.2.2. GPC-Owned Facilities. GPC will accept Bids for Facilities where Bidder proposes to
                     transfer to GPC Facility ownership. The Awarded Contract that a Winning Bidder would execute
                     with GPC would be a BTA.

                          A.      Consideration of BTA Bids. GPC will consider BTA Bids for Facilities that can
                          interconnect to the GPC Electric System and are located in the State of Georgia. A BTA Bid
                          must offer 100% ownership of the Facility. GPC will not consider a BTA Bid offering to pair
