                          a Facility with a Renewable Resource constructed pursuant to a BTA awarded under a prior
                          GPC competitive solicitation.
                          B.      BTA Bid Requirements. A Bidder offering a BTA Bid must submit the same forms
                          as a PPA Bidder, but a BTA Bidder must also complete additional questions, including the
                          questions on the questionnaire found in Exhibit C (Additional Bid Information and
                          Questionnaire), which indicates the information GPC must receive to perform necessary due
                          diligence.
                          C.      BTA Bid Evaluation. BTA Bids will be evaluated alongside PPA Bids and
                          Company-Owned Proposal(s). If a BTA Bid advances to the Competitive Tier, the evaluation
                          of the BTA Bid requires additional due diligence.
                          D.      Winning Bid BTA Execution. If a BTA Bid advances as a winning Bid, BTA
                          execution will occur in accordance with the Solicitation Schedule. The Bidder and GPC must
                          agree on a transaction closing date as soon as practicable once the parties obtain the
                          required regulatory approvals.

              2.3.   BESS Submissions. GPC will consider a Facility structured as: (i) Standalone BESS with grid
                     charging capability; or (ii) BESS with an existing Renewable Resource, with grid charging
                     capability. In addition to the subsections that immediately follow, the pro forma BESS PPA and
                     the additional guidance for Submissions in Exhibit L (Additional Guidance for BESS Submissions)
                     provide the parameters for the acceptable and applicable use of a BESS in this Winter 2027_2028
                     BESS RFP. GPC’s evaluation of a Submission in this RFP will be appropriately focused upon the
                     capacity use of the BESS, which is to ensure system reliability.

                     2.3.1. Degradation. GPC is not responsible for any degradation of any Facility over the Term,
                     whether because of GPC scheduling, charging, or discharging of energy. As set forth in the pro
                     forma BESS PPA, the BESS is subject to monthly performance metrics and must maintain the
                     guaranteed Storage Device Design Capacity and guaranteed Storage Device Discharge Duration
                     for the PPA Term.

                     2.3.2. Operating Policy. Any Participant offering an Submission must be familiar with, and will
                     be expected to comply with, Southern Company Transmission’s Operating Policy for Inverter-
                     Based Electric Storage Resources Interconnecting to the Southern Companies’ Transmission
                     System, as appropriate, which may be found at: https://www.oasis.oati.com/woa/docs/SOCO/SOCOdocs/Inverter-
                     Based_Electric_Storage_Operating_Policy.pdf.

                     2.3.3. Standalone BESS. A Participant offering a Standalone BESS must provide: (i) a
                     description of the BESS; (ii) if offering a PPA, the plan to maintain the BESS to ensure the BESS
                     performs as evaluated for the PPA Term; (iii) the guaranteed Storage Device Design Capacity
                     (AC); (iv) an annual schedule of the guaranteed Round-Trip Efficiency for the PPA Term or Facility
                     Design Life, as applicable; and (v) any other information required by the Bid form. GPC must have
                     the exclusive right, without penalty, to discharge and charge the BESS by dispatching it in
                     accordance with Section 3.6 (AGC). To ensure GPC can toll the energy, a Standalone BESS must
                     be interconnected to, and solely charged from, the GPC Electric System. GPC will provide (toll)
                     all energy required to charge a Standalone BESS, but Seller will be solely responsible for Station
                     Service.
                     2.3.4. BESS with Renewable Resource. A Participant may offer to pair a Facility with an
                     existing Renewable Resource, but the Renewable Resource must: (i) be under a power purchase
                     agreement procured by GPC through a prior competitive procurement; (ii) be sized at least 50
                     MW; and (iii) have a POI that allows for winter discharge of the BESS. In addition to the
                     information required by Section 2.3.3 (Standalone BESS), a BESS with Renewable Resource
                     Submission must also include: (i) description of the Renewable Resource (including facility name
                     and location); (ii) the total expected capacity (AC) from the Renewable Resource; and (iii) a Profile
                     reflecting the Renewable Resource, to demonstrate the charging contribution of the Renewable
                     Resource for the BESS. The BESS must operate independently from the Renewable Resource
                     and have grid-charging capability. Participant is responsible for any design, upgrade, or

                     configuration, the existing PPA may be amended if a BESS resource is paired with a Renewable

                     2.3.5. Additional BESS Guidance. Critical guidance concerning the required parameters for

         PART 3.     KEY PROJECT REQUIREMENTS

              3.1.   PPA Term, Facility Design Life, RCOD, and RCD.
                     3.1.1. PPA Term and Facility Design Life. GPC will consider Bids for: (i) PPAs with a PPA
                     Term of 5, 10, 15, or 20 Annual Periods, at Bidder’s option; and (ii) BTAs with a Facility Design
                     Life appropriate with the technology type and consistent with Prudent Industry Practices. GPC
                     will evaluate Bids under the methodology outlined in Exhibit H (Overview of Evaluation
                     Methodology).

                     3.1.2. RCOD and RCD. Under the 2023 IRP Update Final Order, GPC seeks BESS resources
                     with in-service dates on or before November 30, 2027. Each Bidder must indicate the RCOD or
                     RCD, as applicable, in its Bid, and the date must be in accordance with the Solicitation Schedule.
                     GPC may decline to enter into a PPA or BTA with any Bidder if, in the opinion of GPC, in
                     consultation with the IE and Staff, the transmission facilities cannot be constructed in time to
                     achieve Commercial Operation or Closing by the date set forth in the Solicitation Schedule. BESS
                     with Renewable Resource Bidders must provide a Profile(s) for each Bid that begins on the RCOD
                     or the RCD, as applicable. Bidders may consult the Southern Companies’ Seller Interconnection
                     Business Practices document posted on OASIS for information related to interconnection activity
                     timeframes and limitations. If Seller fails to achieve Commercial Operation or Closing by the
                     RCOD or RCD, as applicable, Seller must pay Delay Damages to GPC under the Awarded
                     Contract. Delay Damages will be calculated in accordance with the applicable Delay Damages
                     table in Exhibit E (Summary of Fees, Costs, Security, and Deadlines), Attachment 2 (Delay
                     Liquidated Damages Summary).

              3.2.   Facility Size and Output.
                     3.2.1. Facility Size Requirements. Each BESS must have a minimum Storage Device Design
                     Capacity of 50 MW at the POI and a Storage Device Discharge Duration of four hours. The
                     Storage Device Design Capacity must be no more than 500 MW at the POI. An evaluated capacity
                     contribution will be assigned to each configuration. Each BESS must have grid charging
                     capability.
                         A.      BESS with a Renewable Resource. A proposed BESS paired with a Renewable
                         Resource must also have a minimum design capacity of 50 MW and must be 50% to 100%
                         of the Renewable Resource capacity. An evaluated capacity contribution will be assigned
                         to each configuration. The BESS must initially charge from the renewable resource but
                         must have grid charging capability.

                     3.2.3. No Partial Input or Output Bids. Each PPA and BTA Bid must offer 100% entitlement
                     to the full input and output capability of the BESS resource in this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP.

                     3.2.4. GPC Consent Required for Facility Changes. A Winning Bidder must obtain GPC’s
                     written consent before making any material change to Facility design, performance, or output (as
                     specified in the Bid and considered by GPC in Bid evaluation).

              3.3.   Location of Facilities.
                     3.3.1. Facility Location. GPC will only accept Submissions for a Facility that is, or will be,
                     interconnected to the GPC Electric System and located in the State of Georgia. A Bidder may not
                     submit a Bid that locates the Facility on GPC property. Only a Company-Owned Proposal may
                     propose a Facility on GPC property.

                          A.     BESS with Renewable Resource Location. Any BESS paired with a Renewable
                          Resource as part of a BESS Submission must interconnect to the same POI as the
                          Renewable Resource.

              3.4.   Transmission Interconnection. Each Bidder is responsible for determining all transmission
                     interconnection and delivery-related rules, practices, and policies with which it must comply, as
                     further detailed in Exhibit B (Interconnection and Delivery Requirements).
                     3.4.1. Point of Interconnection. Each Participant proposing a stand-alone Facility must
                     propose a discrete POI for its Facility. The proposed POI must be consistent with the expected
                     point of electrical interconnection that would be established if Participant were currently applying
                     for interconnection. GPC (through the IE) may suggest a different POI (regarding location or
                     voltage) if it would result in more favorable economic consideration of the Submission. Participant
                     will be responsible for all equipment necessary to interconnect the Facility to the Interconnection
                     Facilities at the POI. All transmission facilities beyond the proposed POI (into the network
                     transmission grid) will be owned by the Transmission Service Provider.
                     3.4.2. Transmission Improvements. GPC will only consider Submissions that require minimal
                     transmission improvements, which are Interconnection Facilities or Network Upgrades (as
                     defined in the LGIA/LGIP) that (i) are necessary for the safe and reliable operation of the Facility;
                     and (ii) feasibly can be completed in time to allow Commercial Operation or Closing, as applicable,
                     by no later than November 30, 2027.

              3.5.   Dispatchability. Facilities offered in this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP must be fully dispatchable
                     and available to meet GPC’s AGC signals for the PPA Term or Facility Design Life, as applicable,
                     which means the Facility can flexibly adjust its output in response to GPC’s AGC signals, subject
                     to any technical limit or other requirement stated in the Awarded Contract.

              3.6.   AGC. Because of their expected use and cost-effectiveness, each Facility must be capable of
                     operating on AGC. Seller will be responsible for conforming to GPC’s requirements to integrate
                     AGC functionality and for all costs to make the Facility respond to GPC’s AGC signals. GPC will
                     have the right, but not the obligation, to dispatch the Facility in the AGC mode. Each Bid must
                     include the cost of the operation in its pricing.

              3.7.   Availability. GPC will rely, in part, on the contracted capacity supplied under a PPA to provide
                     dependable and reliable electric service to meet the needs of its customers. Accordingly, GPC
                     will require stringent protection for GPC and its customers against failures by the Seller to deliver
                     Contracted Capacity in accordance with the PPA.
                     3.7.1. Guaranteed Availability. Any PPA will contain provisions that require Seller to forfeit a
                     portion of the capacity payment for Facility availability below 96% (calculated on a seasonal or
                     monthly basis, as the case may be). After taking scheduled maintenance outages into account,
                     availability during any monthly period that is below 75% will result in a 100% forfeiture of the
                     monthly capacity payment. Bidder may review the pro forma PPA for more information regarding
                     the availability calculation and adjustments to the capacity payment (which may be determined
                     by replacement costs). In addition, a PPA Event of Default will occur if the availability remains
                     below 75% for a certain extended period as specified in the PPA.

              3.8.   Firmness of Proposed Resources. To be considered responsive, a Submission must
                     demonstrate an appropriate level of firmness, which means the Facility must deliver capacity for
         WINTER 27_28 BESS RFP                                                                               Page 20 of 89

                                                                                                    RFP Document

                     the Storage Device Discharge Duration (up to 4 hours) in accordance with GPC’s AGC signals,
                     even under adverse conditions. GPC’s evaluation will assess the reliability and economic value
                     of limits indicated in the Submission. Each Submission must propose to provide the proposed
                     capacity to GPC from specific, dedicated resource(s) on an unencumbered, first-call basis and
                     priority.

                     3.8.1. Charging Plan for BESS Bids. GPC requires each BESS to connect to the GPC Electric
                     System and for each BESS PPA to contain provisions allowing GPC to charge the BESS from
                     the GPC Electric System and to dispatch all energy stored in the BESS. Additional charging
                     details are listed in Exhibit L (Additional Guidance for BESS Submissions).

              3.9.   Technical Requirements. All Facilities must comply with NERC EOP-012-1 (Extreme Cold
                     Weather Preparedness and Operations). Exhibit O (Facility Technical Requirements) contains a
                     general overview of the technical requirements with which each Facility must comply, as applicable.
                     3.9.1. BTA Bids and COPs. All BTA Bids and COPs must conform to GPC’s minimum technical
                     requirements. GPC will make its minimum technical requirements available to any BTA Bidder or
                     COP Team through the IE. To receive the minimum technical requirements, Bidder must execute
                     a nondisclosure agreement.

              3.10. Station Service; Retail Electric Service. Seller is responsible for all Station Service at Seller’s
                    expense. Seller must arrange retail electric service for the Facility in accordance with the Georgia
                    Territorial Electric Service Act. Seller will purchase Station Service (separately-metered energy
                    delivered from the Electric System that is used to serve the Facility’s electrical requirements,
                    including transformer losses and line losses between the Facility and the POI) provided by the
                    local electric service provider (which may or may not be GPC).

              3.11. Environmental Compliance. All Submissions that advance to the Competitive Tier will undergo
                    a comprehensive environmental review to ensure compliance with the requirements of this Winter
                    2027_2028 BESS RFP, including the requirements found in Exhibit M (Environmental Site
                    Assessment Requirements). Bidder must cooperate with GPC’s Environmental Affairs
                    Department, at Bidder’s cost, regarding the environmental and cultural resources assessments,
                    surveys, and studies performed for the Site, and for the property on which the Interconnection
                    Facilities will be located, as well as any related Access Route.
                     3.11.1. Site Assessment. Each Bidder must conduct an Environmental Site Assessment that, at
                     a minimum, considers the factors described in Exhibit M (Environmental Site Assessment
                     Requirements) and must include the affidavit found in Exhibit N (Environmental Compliance
                     Affidavit) with its Bid.

                     3.11.2. Environmental Assurances. Each Bidder must submit a notarized Environmental
                     Compliance Affidavit, found in Exhibit N (Environmental Compliance Affidavit) that affirms Bidder
                     understands all environmental impacts and factors related to the Project and, at a minimum,
                     agrees to fully consider the environmental requirements of this RFP to avoid, minimize, and if
                     necessary, permit and mitigate the Project’s environmental impacts. If a Submission is advanced
                     to the Competitive Tier, it will undergo a comprehensive review to ensure Bidder complied with

         PART 4.     PRICING, FEES, AND SECURITY

              4.1.   PPA Pricing. PPA Bid prices must include all costs GPC will pay for the capacity to be delivered
                     under the PPA in accordance with GPC’s AGC signals. GPC will not be responsible for any other
                     cost associated with the Facility, including Station Service, transmission system interconnection,
                     and all costs incurred to accomplish synchronization.

                     4.1.1. Escalating Pricing. A PPA Bidder may submit a Bid with the capacity payment escalated
                     at a fixed percentage not to exceed 2.5% in any Annual Period. The minimum escalation during
                     any Annual Period for the capacity payment will be limited to 0%.

              4.2.   BTA Pricing. Each BTA Bid must provide an “all-in” price that includes all customary and
                     reasonable facilities necessary for reliable operation of the Facility, including transmission
                     interconnection, any other facilities, and the Site. A BTA Facility must include the Facility’s major
                     equipment and all auxiliary equipment and facilities necessary or used for the storage, control,
                     delivery, or monitoring of electricity on the property. All equipment and other facilities installed on
                     the Facility’s side of the POI must be considered part of the Facility. All data provided in Exhibit C
                     (Additional Bid Information and Questionnaire), including capacity, Variable O&M, and Facility
                     availability must be based on: (i) testing and past performance; or (ii) design criteria for a BTA
                     Facility.

                     4.2.1. Option to Purchase Land. If a BTA Bidder owns property adjacent to the Site, the Bidder
                     may include within its Bid an offer to sell to GPC the adjacent property for an optional price stated
                     in the Bid.

                     4.2.2. Due Diligence. Concurrent with GPC’s initial economic screening of all conforming
                     Submissions, GPC will begin BTA due diligence assessments as generally described in Exhibit A
                     (Due Diligence Phases and Fees Overview (BTA Bids Only)) to determine GPC’s best estimate
                     of the cost to own and operate the Facility.

              4.3.   Bid Fee. To help defray the cost of performing an evaluation of each Bid and the cost of retaining
                     the IE pursuant to the RFP Rule, each Bidder must pay the Bid Fee ($20,000) for each Bid. A
                     portion of each Bid Fee in the amount of $10,000 will be earmarked to offset IE costs. Bidder
                     must pay the Bid Fee by 12:00 p.m. ET on the Bid Due Date.

              4.4.   Due Diligence Fees. To partially offset the cost of screening and assessments of an asset
                     purchase, BTA Bidders will be required to submit Due Diligence Fees as described in Exhibit A
                     (Due Diligence Phases and Fees Overview (BTA Bids Only)). A portion of Due Diligence Fees will
                     be used to offset IE costs.

              4.5.   Winner’s Fee. As stated in Section 4.3 (Bid Fee) and Section 4.4 (Due Diligence Fees), portions
                     of Bid Fees and Due Diligence Fees will be used to offset IE costs. The remainder of the IE cost
                     will be covered by the Winner’s Fee. The Winner’s Fee will be determined once the final amount
                     of Bid Fees, Due Diligence Fees, and IE cost is known, except in no event will the Winner’s Fee
                     exceed one million dollars ($1,000,000.00). The Winner’s Fee is calculated for each winning
                     Submission, including any Company-Owned Proposal,, as the pro rata share for any remaining
                     IE cost not covered by Bid Fees and Due Diligence Fees. In the event of multiple winning
                     Submissions, the Winner’s Fee will be allocated to winning Participant(s) on: (i) a MW-PPA Term

         PART 7.     SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

              7.1.   Bid Process. Each Submission must be submitted via the Bid Form on the IE Website by no later
                     than the date and time specified in the Solicitation Schedule. If a Bidder discovers an error or
                     omission in the Bid after submitting its Bids but before the Bid Due Date, Bidder must note any
                     change in the electronic filing and the changes must be posted to the Bid Form by no later than
                     12:00 p.m. ET on the Bid Due Date.

              7.2.   Effect of Bid Submission. Bidder’s Bid submission will constitute Bidder’s acknowledgment and
                     acceptance of all terms, conditions, and requirements of this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP,
                     including pro forma PPA terms and conditions. Failure to provide all requested Submission
                     information may invalidate a Submission. GPC is not required to contact any Participant to obtain
                     any omitted information.

              7.3.   Alternative Bids; Multiple Submissions; Bid Fees.

                     7.3.1. Alternative Bid. Bidder may submit a separate, mutually exclusive Bid that offers a
                     Facility located on the same Site and using the same Point of Interconnection as another Bid, but
                     the Alternative Bid: (i) offers the same technology under a different form of contract; or (ii) offers
                     varying PPA Term lengths. The placement of a Bid on the Release List will not affect GPC’s
                     evaluation of the Alternative Bid.

                     7.3.2. Multiple Submissions. Participants may submit multiple Submissions into this Winter
                     2027_2028 BESS RFP. Except for an Alternative Bid, GPC will not accept contingent Submissions
                     (i.e., a Submission that is dependent upon another Submission’s outcome). For example, GPC
                     will not accept Submissions where Participant submitted multiple Submissions for several Sites
                     but is only willing to develop a limited number of those Facilities or requires a combination of the
                     Submissions to be advanced together. Additionally, Bidder may not aggregate multiple Facilities
                     from one or more Sites to meet the minimum MW required to be submitted in this Winter
                     2027_2028 BESS RFP.

                     7.3.3. Bid Fees. If Bidder submits separate Bids that vary regarding certain critical parameters,
                     including contract type, the Site, output, or electrical characteristics, Bidder will be required to pay
                     the Bid Fee ($20,000.00) for each Bid. However, PPA Bids submitted by one Bidder for the same
                     Site, same generation technology, and same size that offer options in the fixed cost components

                     of three options will be accepted as a single Bid covered under one Bid Fee.

              7.4.   Submission Information. Submissions must include all applicable information requested on the
                     IE Website and any other information that is necessary for a thorough understanding and
                     evaluation of the Submission. Any Submission that does not contain all the required information
                     on the applicable due date will be subject to rejection by GPC as non-responsive. It is each
                     Participant’s responsibility to submit additional information about its Submission that could further
                     inform GPC’s understanding of the Submission or could materially affect its value. Required
                     Submission information includes the information outlined below.

                     7.4.1. Facility Name. Due to the need to manage a multitude of projects, and GPC’s experience
                     with counterparties selecting similar or confusing names for projects, GPC may reject a Facility
                     name offered by a Winning Bidder and propose an alternative name. To give Bidder sufficient
                     time to perform due diligence on the Facility name and any proposed special purpose entity name
                     it intends to use as the Awarded Contract counterparty, GPC will request Bidder confirmation of
                     the Facility and counterparty names at the time a Bid advances to the Competitive Tier.

                     7.4.2. Site Control Affidavit. Each Bidder must submit a notarized Site Control Affidavit that
                     affirms Bidder has obtained Site Control during the PPA Term or Facility Design Life, as
                     applicable. The form Site Control Affidavit is attached as Exhibit D (Form of Site Control Affidavit
                     and Landowner Confirmation). Bidder may be required to submit further evidence of Site Control,
                     as and when deemed necessary by GPC.

                     7.4.3. Bidder Variable Interest Entity Certification. Depending on the PPA Term and the
                     business structure, a PPA Bidder may choose to adopt accounting and tax rules that may require:
                     (i) that a PPA, or components of the PPA, be accounted for by GPC as a lease; or (ii) Seller under
                     the PPA be consolidated as a VIE onto GPC’s books. Because GPC is unwilling to be subject to
                     accounting or tax treatment that results from VIE treatment, each Bidder is required to certify,
                     using the form found in Exhibit J (VIE Certification), its independent belief that the Bidder’s Bid
                     will most likely not require the Seller at any time over the proposed PPA term to deconsolidate on
                     its books and records any assets, liabilities, cash flow, profits, or losses where GPC is determined
                     to be the Primary Beneficiary. At PPA execution, annually through the Term, and at any time the
                     PPA is amended by the Parties, the Seller’s chief financial officer or an officer having responsibility
                     for financial accounting matters associated with the PPA, must again provide this certification.
                     Further, any PPA that GPC executes will require that: (a) Seller covenant that GPC will not be
                     subject to VIE treatment at any point during the Term; and (b) if the PPA causes GPC to be subject
                     to VIE treatment at any point during the Term, unless cured, such treatment will constitute a PPA
                     Event of Default. As provided for in the pro forma PPA, GPC would have the right to terminate the
                     PPA, and unless Seller can clearly demonstrate that the consolidation event was not due to the
                     direct or indirect actions of Seller, Seller will be liable for termination damages as outlined in the
                     PPA.

                     7.4.4. Finance Lease Certification. If applicable, Bidder must certify certain factual statements
                     for each Bid based on Bidder’s personal consideration of the factual matters and Bidder’s
                     understanding of accounting standards regarding a Finance and Operating Lease, using the form
                     provided in Exhibit K (Finance Lease Certification Checklist). If Bidder responds in the affirmative
                     on one or more of the factual statements, Bidder must also provide the amounts that GPC would

                     for which Bidder responds in the negative to all the factual statements set forth in Exhibit K, Bidder
                     is required to certify such declaration, with supporting information sufficient to enable GPC to
                     independently verify that Finance Lease treatment will not occur. At the time of Bid submission,
                     at PPA execution, and at any time the PPA is amended by the Parties, Seller’s chief financial
                     officer or an officer having responsibility for financial accounting matters associated with the PPA
                     must again provide this certification. For Bids declared as Finance or Operating Lease, the Bid

                     Proposal will be reviewed by Staff and the IE before being addressed with the respective
                     Participant.

                     interest of GPC’s customers and will not harm the RFP Process, as determined by GPC in
                     consultation with the IE and Staff. All modification requests must be made through the IE Website.

                     consideration.

              8.1.   Staff and IE Oversight/Evaluation. In accordance with the RFP Rule, Staff and the IE actively
                     and contemporaneously monitor all aspects of GPC’s evaluation process for transparency
                     purposes. Staff and the IE will review all Submissions and conduct an independent evaluation of
                     the BESS resources offered to GPC in this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP. Staff and the IE are
                     permitted access to all documents and information utilized by GPC in its evaluation. GPC, Staff,
                     and IE will meet to discuss and finalize the Competitive Tier and, after further evaluation of the
                     Competitive Tier, the Short List, including Bids identified for Awarded Contract award and any
                     Company-Owned Proposal identified for inclusion on the Short List. Staff will be given access to
                     all Bid data after the evaluation model has been locked down, Bid Period has closed, and all Bids
                     have been cured.

              8.2.   Criteria. All Submissions in this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP will be evaluated in accordance
                     with the evaluation criteria and structure described in Exhibit H (Overview of Evaluation
                     Methodology). GPC reserves the right to contact any Participant through the IE Website to
                     request additional information on any aspect of a Submission. GPC also reserves the right to
                     request that the IE contact any Participant for additional information or to cure a deficiency
                     identified in a Submission.

              8.3.   Initial Review. Submissions that are complete and conform to RFP requirements will be ranked
                     and screened on price to eliminate Submissions that are clearly not competitive before detailed
                     economic modeling is performed.

              8.4.   Competitive Tier Identified. Under the oversight of the IE and Staff, GPC will evaluate all
                     Submissions and determine a Competitive Tier that consists of the most competitive
                     Submissions. An appropriate selection of Submissions meeting GPC’s requirements will advance
                     as the Competitive Tier for additional evaluation. GPC will further evaluate Submissions included
                     in the Competitive Tier using appropriate production costing methods and models to ensure that
                     all material cost impacts are quantified. All Submissions (including Company-Owned Proposals,
                     BTA Bids, and Affiliate Bids) will be considered and evaluated together. As part of its Competitive
                     Tier evaluation, GPC will review generation and transmission costs and Ancillary Service
                     requirements, as appropriate, to determine the Submission’s total cost impact. After the detailed
                     transmission and portfolio analysis concludes, the most competitive Submissions will advance to
                     the Short List, which may include one or more Company-Owned Proposals, for final evaluation
                     and advancement. A Participant whose Submission(s) advanced to the Competitive Tier or Short

                EXHIBIT A – DUE DILIGENCE PHASES AND FEES OVERVIEW (BTA BIDS ONLY)

         PART 1     BID INFORMATION.
         1.1    Identification of Critical Due Diligence Topics for First Due Diligence Phase. At the time of Bid submission,
         a BTA Bidder must: (i) provide the BTA Due Diligence Checklist available on the IE Website and required
         accompanying documents; and (ii) recommend additional critical due diligence topics that the Evaluation Team should
         include in the first due diligence phase (“Phase One Due Diligence”) described in this Exhibit A.

         PART 2     INITIAL ECONOMIC SCREEN ($20,000 FEE).
         2.1    Bid Fee. Each Bidder must submit a non-refundable Bid Fee ($20,000) with each Bid in accordance with RFP
         Section 7.3.3 (Bid Fees) before the Evaluation Team will begin evaluating the Bid.
         2.2    Screening Overview. If a Bid advances past the initial economic screening, the Bid will proceed through the
         additional due diligence steps outlined in the following sections of this Exhibit A.

         PART 3     PHASE ONE DUE DILIGENCE ($50,000 FEE).
         3.1    Fee Requirement. Bidder must submit a Phase One Due Diligence Fee of $50,000 in addition to the required
         Bid Fee ($20,000) by no later than the Bid Due Date shown in the Solicitation Schedule. The total initial payment
         required for BTA Bids is $70,000, which is the sum of: (i) the $20,000 Bid Fee; plus (ii) the $50,000 Phase One Due
         Diligence Fee.
         3.2   Phase One Due Diligence Overview. Phase One Due Diligence will consist of “fatal flaw assessment” to
         determine if there are significant issues with the BTA Bid that would call into question the value of the asset. The Phase
         One Due Diligence review will be preliminary and will include the following:
            A. BTA Phase One Due Diligence
              (i) Technical and engineering review of BTA Due Diligence Checklist and accompanying documents, including
              review of major equipment and balance of plant components.
                    (a) For items requested in the BTA Due Diligence Checklist and required accompanying documents that
                    Bidder does not provide with the Bid submission, Bidder must explain in writing why Bidder did not submit
                    the information. Bidder must provide to the Evaluation Team for review, any applicable information or
                    supporting documentation that Bidder obtains during due diligence.
              (ii) Proposed Site design and initial engineering review.
              (iii) Review of Bidder-identified due diligence topics.
         3.3   Refund or Credit of Unused Fee. If GPC does not expend the entire $50,000 Phase One Due Diligence Fee,
         GPC will refund the unused portion to Bidder or credit the balance as payment toward the Phase Two Due Diligence
         Fee, as applicable.

         PART 4     PHASE TWO DUE DILIGENCE (UP TO $400,000 FEE).
         4.1     Fee Requirements. If the Bid satisfies the Phase One Due Diligence review and advances to the Competitive

                         EXHIBIT B – INTERCONNECTION AND DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS
         Each Bidder is responsible for determining all transmission interconnection and delivery-related rules,
         practices, and policies with which Bidder must comply. Each Bid must comply with this Exhibit B.

         PART 1     INTERCONNECTION AND DELIVERY REQUIREMENTS – GENERAL
         1.1     Transmission Projected Commercial Operation Date. GPC may decline to advance a Bid to the Short
         List or to execute an Awarded Contract with any Bidder if, in GPC’s opinion, the transmission facilities cannot
         be constructed in time to achieve Commercial Operation or Closing, as applicable, by the date set forth in the
         Solicitation Schedule.
            A. Bid Lead-Time Assumptions. Each Bid must describe the Facility’s current status within the applicable
            interconnection process and Bidder’s ability to meet the RCOD, or RCD in the case of a BTA, based upon the
            applicable interconnection process timeline.
            B. Interconnection Agreement Required. Each Winning Bidder must have or enter into an IA for interconnection to
            the GPC Electric System. Each Bidder must contact the Interconnection Provider (Southern Company Services,
            Inc.) to obtain all relevant information and interconnection requirements. The submission of a Bid in response
            to this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP does not constitute an interconnection request or an IA. Bidder is solely
            responsible for all fees, deposits, and other charges regarding Bidder’s interconnection request and the IA. At any
            point in time, the Facility is prohibited from delivering output to the POI that exceeds the lesser of the
            generating/discharge capacity or the Interconnection Limit.
            C. Interconnection Process. At the time of Bid submission, Bidder must:
               (i) have an Interconnection Agreement and be designated;
               (ii) be in the transitional serial/cluster study process; or
               (iii) qualify for Surplus Interconnection Service as defined in the applicable Large Generator Interconnection
               Procedures (“LGIP”).
         1.2     Evaluation Assumptions. Bid evaluation will assume that the LGIP applies and that Bidder has executed or
         will execute a large generator interconnection agreement (“LGIA”). Each Bidder must determine all rules, practices,
         policies, and timelines with which its Facility must interconnect with the GPC Electric System. A request to interconnect
         to the GPC Electric System is treated the same as a request to interconnect to the Southern Company Transmission
         System, and Bidder may obtain additional information on Southern Company’s OASIS website at:
         http://www.oatioasis.com/SOCO/index.html.
         1.3     Bidder Cost Responsibility. Bidder is responsible for all Interconnection Study-related costs, in addition to the
         interconnection costs and risk up to the POI. Interconnection costs generally include equipment such as the Facility
         generator step-up (GSU) transformer (for conversion up to the interconnecting voltage level), Facility-side generator
         interrupting device, all Station Service equipment, tie-line (which carries electrical power and communications), and
         any additional equipment (such as a utility-owned interrupting device and metering needed to connect to the
         transmission facilities), as well as any additional real property for the interconnection substation and access, and any
         operation and maintenance expenses and administrative costs. In addition, if applicable, Bidder is responsible for the
         cost, risk, and coordination of all Affected System Upgrades. It is Bidder’s responsibility to determine and consider all
         information regarding interconnection costs in preparing its Bid.
         1.4    Interconnection Impacts.
            A. GPC Electric System Interconnection Costs. Interconnection impacts to the Electric System are unique to
            the specific design and location of each Facility and may require new or modified equipment beyond the POI. For
            a Facility interconnecting to the GPC Electric System, any interconnection cost for new or modified equipment on
            the GPC Electric System beyond the POI (refundable “Network Upgrades” under the LGIP/LGIA) will be imputed
            to the Bid during the Bid evaluation and should not be included in the Bid price. However, as stated above in Section
            1.3 (Bidder Cost Responsibility) of this Exhibit B any costs associated with Affected System Upgrades are solely
            Bidder’s responsibility and will not be reimbursed by GPC.
            B. SCS LGIA Costs. A Winning Bidder (i.e., Seller) may be required under the terms of its SCS LGIA to fund or
            provide security for new or modified equipment beyond the POI (interconnection costs beyond the POI that are
            refundable “Network Upgrades” per the LGIP/LGIA). However, if Seller incurs such interconnection-related costs
            for new or modified equipment on the Southern Company Transmission System beyond the POI, after the Facility

         WINTER 27_28 BESS RFP                                                                                      Page 38 of 89

STF-JKA-1-24 Attachment F.pdf

            achieves Commercial Operation or Closing is achieved, as applicable, the costs will be refunded to Seller or security
            will be released in accordance with LGIA terms and Southern OATT.
            C. Affected System Interconnection Costs. If a winning Bid has interconnection impacts to any Affected
            System, such that the Affected System must add, modify, or upgrade its Electric System, Bidder must coordinate
            with the Affected System with respect to identifying, planning, and construction of, and payment of costs for, the
            additions, modifications, or upgrades. Bidders must contemplate the schedule and cost impacts in each Bid. Any
            interconnection costs related to the Affected System are Bidder’s sole responsibility and will not be reimbursed by
            GPC. Any reimbursement for these costs is a matter strictly between the Affected System and Bidder.
         1.5             Delivery Impacts. For Bids advanced to the Competitive Tier, GPC will develop a cost estimate for
         Electric System improvements, if any, to the Southern Company Transmission System, the Georgia ITS, or both,
         necessary to deliver the stored energy from the POI to GPC’s customers. These costs will be imputed to the Bid. If
         Electric System improvement costs are anticipated to be incurred by GPC beyond the POI (including any GPC
         obligation for payment to ITS Participants or other Electric System owners) to deliver the full output of the Facility, Seller
         must deliver to GPC Upgrade Security in the amount of the cost to make the improvements as determined by GPC as
         of the Awarded Contract Effective Date. To the extent an ITS Participant or other Electric System owner has not notified
         GPC of such costs before the Awarded Contract Effective Date, GPC may refine the cost estimate and will notify Seller
         of any change required to the amount of Upgrade Security. Seller must update the amount of the Upgrade Security
         (either by amending the Upgrade Security or by providing replacement Upgrade Security) within 10 Business Days
         after receiving the updated cost information. After the Facility achieves Commercial Operation or Closing, as
         applicable, GPC will return the Upgrade Security to Seller. Alternatively, in the event of early termination of the PPA
         prior to Commercial Operation or early termination of a BTA prior to Closing, as applicable, GPC may draw upon the
         Upgrade Security, subject to repayment in accordance with any applicable OATT.
         1.6    Construction of Southern Company Transmission System Facilities. Any Electric System improvement,
         modification, or new facility that will become part of the Southern Company Transmission System must be owned by,
         and will be designed, procured, and constructed by, as applicable, Georgia Power or, if applicable, Alabama Power.
         1.7    Facility Not Yet Interconnected to GPC. The following provisions apply only to a Facility that is not
         interconnected to GPC at the time of Bid submission.
            A. Land and Property Rights. A Winning Bidder must timely coordinate with GPC’s land acquisition department
            to obtain and provide to GPC, at Bidder’s cost, suitable real property (fee simple or easement, as will be designated
            during the Interconnection Study process) in an acceptable location for the Interconnection Facilities, along with an
            Access Route to the ICF Site acceptable to GPC, as well as any necessary encroachment agreement, consent, or
            similar document. All necessary property right documents must be acceptable to GPC and on its standard terms
            and conditions, and all property rights documentation must be timely obtained, negotiated, and executed. During
            the Interconnection Study process, GPC and Bidder will discuss and agree upon Interconnection Facilities and
            Access Route siting. Bidder also must coordinate with GPC to prepare to GPC’s satisfaction the property (e.g.,
            grading and preparation of the ICF Site and suitable Access Route) and turn access to the property over to GPC
            by no later than one year before the projected transmission in-service date. After initial preparation of the Access
            Route, a Winning Bidder who enters into an Awarded Contract must also: (i) regarding an Awarded Contract that is
            a PPA, maintain, at its own expense, the Access Route in accordance with GPC’s standards and to GPC’s
            satisfaction throughout the PPA Term; and (ii) regarding an Awarded Contract that is a BTA, validly transfer all real
            property rights required by GPC for access to and maintenance of the ICF Site and the Interconnection Facilities.
            B. Notice to Proceed. Notice to proceed requirements for a Winning Bidder whose Facility will interconnect with
            GPC depend on the interconnection request/IA status when the Commission issues the Certificate of Public
            Convenience and Necessity:
              (i) A Winning Bidder with an active IA must submit a notice to proceed to initiate construction of Interconnection
              Facilities by no later than 14 Days after the Commission Certification; or
              (ii) If the interconnection request is still in study phase but the IA has not been finalized, then by no later than
              45 Days after the IA is provided to Bidder for execution, Bidder must submit a notice to proceed to initiate
              construction of Interconnection Facilities. Depending upon when Bidder initiates the interconnection process,
              Bidder may be required to enter into an engineering and procurement agreement with GPC to assume cost
              responsibility and allow pre-construction activities, such as engineering work and procurement of long lead-time
              materials, to commence prior to execution of the IA.
         1.8    Additional Guidance.

                                      EXHIBIT F – BID ASSIGNMENT GUIDELINES

          PART 1    BID ASSIGNMENT
          1.1   Overview.
            A. A Bid may only be assigned, including any assignment of a previously assigned Bid to the original Bidder,
            with the prior written notice to and consent of GPC in accordance with the requirements of this Exhibit F (Bid
            Assignment Guidelines).
            B. For each proposed Bid Assignment, Bidder and the proposed Bid assignee named in and executing the
            Consent Request (“Bid Assignee”) must review the requirements of this Exhibit F (Bid Assignment Guidelines)
            and agree to the GPC Bid Assignment Consent Form included as Attachment 1 to this Exhibit F (“Consent
            Request”).
            C. These guidelines are limited to Bid assignments during the Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP Bid solicitation
            phase (each attempted or completed assignment, a “Bid Assignment”). For assignments, transfers, or other
            changes after Awarded Contract execution, the contracting party must comply with requirements in those
            agreements. For purposes of this Exhibit F (Bid Assignment Guidelines) a Change of Control of a Bidder will be
            deemed an assignment, subject to the provisions of this Exhibit F (Bid Assignment Guidelines). For purposes
            of this Exhibit F, a “Change of Control” is any transaction or series of related transactions which, if
            consummated, would result in Bidder being an Affiliate of another ultimate parent entity immediately after the
            transaction or series of transactions. For purposes of this definition, the ultimate parent entity is the Person who
            directly or indirectly controls 50% or more of Bidder’s outstanding capital stock or other equity interests having
            ordinary voting power and who does not itself have an ultimate parent entity.
          1.2   Notice and Consent Requirements.
            A. Notice Requirements.
              (i) Assignment Before Awarded Contract Execution. If Bidder intends to assign its Bid, Bidder must
              provide GPC with prior written notice through the IE Website in the form of the Consent Request of: (i)
              Bidder’s intent to assign the Bid; (ii) the name of the proposed Bid Assignee; (iii) the information required
              under Section 1.3 (Required Information) of this Exhibit F (Bid Assignment Guidelines) regarding the Bid
              Assignee; and (iv) Bidder’s request for GPC to consent to the Bid Assignment. The Consent Request and all
              required information must be submitted to GPC through the IE Website at least 15 Days before the proposed
              effective date of the Bid Assignment, but in no event less than 15 Days before the Awarded Contract Effective
              Date.
              (ii) Failure to Comply with Notice Requirements. If a Bidder does not comply with the notice and consent
              requirements of this Exhibit F (Bid Assignment Guidelines), GPC may include the Bid in the Release List for
              that reason alone. A consent granted by GPC for a Bid Assignment does not mean that the Bid will be
              advanced as a winning Bid or advanced to the Competitive Tier or Short List.
            B. Consent by GPC. Bidder must not assign any Bid without GPC’s prior written consent. Any attempted Bid
            assignment without GPC’s prior written consent will be void and the original Bidder will remain responsible for
            all its obligations relating to the Bid. GPC's consent to a proposed Bid Assignment will not create any obligation
            for GPC to the original Bidder or Bid Assignee beyond GPC's evaluation of the Bid according to the Winter

                            EXHIBIT H – OVERVIEW OF EVALUATION METHODOLOGY
          The following is a general overview of GPC’s methodology for Submission evaluation. PPA Bids, BTA Bids,
          and any Company-Owned Proposal(s) will receive comparable evaluation that ensures a net total cost is
          calculated while accounting for the net present value of generation and transmission aspects over the life
          of the asset. As part of the evaluation, GPC may also consider the non-price factors described in Exhibit I
          (Non-Price Considerations).

          All graphics and tables included in this Exhibit H are for illustrative purposes only.

          I. Net Total Cost Evaluation. Each Submission advanced to the Competitive Tier will be evaluated and
             ranked using a net total cost analysis approach. The net total cost is the net present value of the
             generation and transmission aspects of the Submission in dollars per kilowatt ($/kW) of capacity
             contribution. The generation cost is comprised of both the fixed cost associated with the Submission
             and the variable cost associated with the operational parameters of the Submission, which will be used
             in production cost modeling simulations. The capacity contribution of each Submission will be based
             on the effective load carrying capability (“ELCC”), which will be determined by the process approved
             by the Commission in GPC’s 2022 Integrated Resource Plan filed in Docket No. 44160. ELCC may
             vary based on technology type and operational characteristics within the same technology.

              A. Generation Costs – Determining Fixed Costs.

              Fixed generation cost will include the following (as applicable to the Submission):

              1. The Bidder-specified capacity cost payment (typically quoted in dollars per kilowatt ($/kW) for each
                 year) for PPA Bids;
              2. The costs associated with PPA treatment as either an Operating Lease or a Finance Lease, as
                 applicable, if it is determined that the PPA constitutes a lease in accordance with RFP Section 7.4.4
                 (Finance Lease Certification); and
              3. GPC’s revenue requirements for the purchase price for BTA Bids and in-service costs for
                 Company-Owned Proposals. These revenue requirements account for depreciation, cost of
                 capital, and taxes.

              The evaluation will consider differences in the seasonal capability of each Submission.

              B. Equity Cost of PPA – Determining the Balance Sheet Consequence for Operating Lease or
                 Finance Lease Treatment.

              If a Bid is determined to be a lease, there is an equity cost to GPC when the PPA is placed on GPC’s
              balance sheet caused by the rating agency treatment of a lease in accordance with FASB ASC Topic
              842.

              For a Finance Lease, GPC must capitalize the PPA as an asset on its balance sheet and must offset it
              by a debt obligation on the liability side of the balance sheet. The addition of the debt obligation on the
              balance sheet requires GPC to recapitalize to maintain the appropriate debt and equity ratio. As a
              result, there are direct equity costs incurred by GPC when a PPA is capitalized and reflected on the
              balance sheet as a Finance Lease. The equity cost of a Bid determined to result in a Finance Lease, if
              selected, will be evaluated by determining the net cost (lease cost less depreciation and tax implication)
              of capitalizing the PPA.

              For an Operating Lease, the PPA is also added to the balance sheet but without directly affecting the
              debt and equity ratio on GPC’s books. However, rating agencies impute debt onto GPC’s balance sheet
              in their evaluation of the credit rating for GPC. Therefore, GPC must still recapitalize to maintain the


          WINTER 27_28 BESS RFP                                                                             Page 67 of 89


                                                       www.gonitro.com

STF-JKA-1-24 Attachment F.pdf

                                                                                          Winter 27_28 BESS RFP
                                                                                                    RFP Document
                                                                                                    Final Approved
             target debt and equity ratio needed to ensure its credit rating is not impacted by the PPA. There is a
             direct equity cost premium associated with this treatment.

             The additional annual revenue requirement cost to GPC is calculated for the Operating Lease or
             Finance Lease. The result is the equity cost applied to the Bid.

             C. Generation Costs – Determining the Production Cost Savings.

             The variable generation cost includes:
             1.   Charging costs for any BESS Submission
             2.   Variable O&M
             3.   Facility dispatch characteristics
             4.   Integration costs for BESS with Renewable Resource Submissions.
             Production cost computer simulations are required to estimate the operational savings associated with
             operating each proposed Facility with the system dispatch. Each Submission’s contribution to reducing
             the aggregate annual system generation fleet fuel and variable cost can be calculated by comparing a
             cost simulation that includes the Submission against a reference simulation (without the Submission).
             The variable cost components of each Submission are modeled within the production cost simulation.
             In addition to Facility operating characteristics, including efficiency (e.g., Round-Trip Efficiency),
             charge and discharge duration, cycle limits, charging source (grid or paired resource), scheduled
             maintenance requirements, any applicable Ancillary Services, and projected availability will contribute
             to the total production cost.

             Evaluation of BESS with Renewable Resource Submissions requires the renewable generation profile
             to be submitted for inclusion in the production cost simulation. Depending on the renewable generation
             technology and configuration of a paired BESS, a $/MWh integration cost reduction will be applied to
             any Renewable Energy to account for mitigation of costs arising from actions taken by system operators
             to respond to the additional volatility on the system from the intermittent nature of Renewable
             Resources. Integration costs will be evaluated in accordance with the RCB Framework, as approved
             by the Commission in Docket 44160.

             In general, GPC conducts the production cost simulation to calculate the projected annual production
             cost savings on a per kilowatt capacity basis for the Submission.

             An illustrative example of the net generation cost calculation (total fixed generation costs net
             production cost savings) is provided below.

                                                     Evaluation Task:
                                          Determine the Production Cost Savings


             D. Net Generation Cost: Calculating the Net Generation Cost of a Proposal.

             The production cost simulation is conducted to achieve the annual production cost savings. The
             calculation of the net generation cost for each proposal is a three-step process: (i) the Submission’s
             fixed costs are calculated annually on a dollar per kilowatt basis; (ii) on an annual basis, the per kilowatt


          WINTER 27_28 BESS RFP                                                                              Page 68 of 89

                                                      www.gonitro.com

STF-JKA-1-24 Attachment F.pdf

                                                                                             Winter 27_28 BESS RFP
                                                                                                       RFP Document
                                                                                                       Final Approved
             production cost savings are subtracted from the fixed costs resulting in the annual net generation per
             kilowatt costs; and (iii) the final net generation cost is the accumulated net present value of the annual
             net generation costs.

             An illustrative example of the net present value of the net generation cost calculation is provided in the
             following table.

                                Determine the Present Value of the Net Generation Costs


             E. Transmission Costs: Evaluation of Transmission Impacts of Bids.

             After determination of the Competitive Tier, an assessment of the transmission impact of each
             Submission will be an integral part of the net total cost analysis. Each Submission on the Competitive
             Tier is evaluated from a transmission network perspective to assess:

             1. The additional network transmission investment required to deliver Facility output to native load on
                a firm basis;
             2. The additional network transmission investment required to provide grid charging service from the
                network, if applicable; and
             3. The increase (or decrease) in transmission system energy losses due to the operation of the
                proposed Facility.

             Each Submission is analyzed using transmission system computer simulation models to determine if
             additional transmission network improvements are required to accommodate the proposed Facility. For
             evaluation purposes, the Submission is assessed the yearly amortized cost of the transmission
             improvements.
             The transmission simulation models include future projections of transmission facilities and planned
             GPC-owned generation to maintain grid reliability in areas of major load (net of generation).
             In addition, each Submission is analyzed to determine whether operation of the proposed Facility
             increases or decreases the transmission system energy losses. Each Submission is assessed an
             annual cost (or credit) associated with its projected impact on the transmission system energy losses.
             As part of the evaluation of transmission impacts of each Submission, GPC will further assess any
             project scheduling risk posed by the transmission system evaluation, including the ability of the
             proposed project to meet the RCOD or RCD, as applicable.
             Illustrative examples of how the net transmission cost and net total cost are determined are provided
             below.

        II.   Due Diligence Portfolio Analysis

          The Competitive Tier will be evaluated and ranked using a consistent methodology that identifies the best
          Submissions based on the net present value of net total cost per kW. To satisfy the capacity need targeted
          in this Winter 2027_2028 BESS RFP, more than one Submission may be selected. A portfolio analysis will
          be required to determine the best portfolio (combination of two or more) of Submissions that satisfy the
          identified capacity need.

          In the due diligence portfolio analysis, the best Submissions will be packaged together into several
          combinations or “portfolios.” Each of the resulting portfolios will be evaluated using a net total cost approach
          that is consistent with the methodology used to evaluate each individual Submission. In the portfolio phase,
          a production cost simulation and a transmission cost analysis are required to evaluate the cost impacts
          resulting from any interaction that may result from packaging several Submissions into a portfolio.

                           EXHIBIT L – ADDITIONAL GUIDANCE FOR BESS SUBMISSIONS
          This Exhibit L provides additional guidance, including operational requirements, for Participants developing
          Submissions. This Exhibit L also summarizes PPA pricing structure and performance metrics, but PPA
          Bidders must also reference the pro forma BESS PPA to gain full understanding of BESS-related
          requirements. BTA Bidders must also reference the pro forma BTA and conform to GPC’s Minimum
          Technical Requirements.
          PART 1       DEFINITIONS
          For purposes of this Exhibit L, each of the following terms has the corresponding assigned meaning:
          Cycle: The equivalent charge of Storage Device Operating Energy (in MWhs) from 0% to 100% and
          subsequent discharge from 100% to 0%, regardless of whether the complete charge or complete discharge
          occurs during one or more charges or discharges. For daily Cycle determinations, the Day in which the
          relevant discharging occurs will include the discharging in the Cycle determination for that day, regardless
          of when the charging occurred.
          Round-Trip Efficiency (RTE): The amount of energy received from the BESS at the POI divided by the
          original amount of energy that was used to charge the BESS at the POI.
          Storage Device Design Capacity: The guaranteed amount of BESS storage capacity allocated to GPC
          under the PPA, as will be designated in the PPA.
          Storage Device Discharge Duration: The guaranteed number of hours that the BESS must be capable
          of continuously discharging to the POI at the Storage Device Design Capacity.
          Storage Device Operating Energy (SDOE): The guaranteed number of MWh that the BESS must be
          capable of discharging to the POI and is equal to the product of the Storage Device Design Capacity
          multiplied by the Storage Device Discharge Duration.
          Storage Performance Reduction (SPR): As defined in the pro forma BESS PPA or.
          PART 2       OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR FACILITIES
          2.1    In addition to the requirements of RFP Section 2.3 (BESS Submissions), a Facility must meet the following
          requirements:
             A. Facility control system must be capable of communicating bidirectionally with GPC’s AGC system, including:
                (i)    Charging and discharging in response to GPC’s 6-second AGC signals;
                (ii)   Operating continuously on AGC for both charging and discharging of the BESS;
                (iii) Operating manually in response to scheduling communications if AGC signals are interrupted for any
                reason; and
                (iv) Sending and receiving all AGC-related signal data (see RFP Section 3.6 (AGC) for details) and
                responding as required by GPC.
             B. The Facility must include control system updates, logic upgrades, connections, and other alterations, as
             requested by GPC, and must be capable of monitoring and controlling the energy flows from and to each Facility
             component.
             C. The BESS must: (i) be capable of Grid charging from the GPC Electric System; and (ii) meet all
             specifications     listed    for   inverter-based generator   interconnections    on      OASIS
             (http://www.oasis.oati.com/SOCO/).


          PART 3       ADDITIONAL OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR A BESS WITH RENEWABLE RESOURCE
                       FACILITY
          3.1  In addition to meeting the requirements of Part 2 (Operational Requirements for Facilities) of this Exhibit L,
          a BESS with Renewable Resource Facility must be capable of:


          WINTER 27_28 BESS RFP                                                                                 Page 76 of 89


                                                        www.gonitro.com

STF-JKA-1-24 Attachment F.pdf

                                                                                         Winter 27_28 BESS RFP
                                                                                                  RFP Document
                                                                                                  Final Approved
             A. Charging and discharging using Renewable Energy in response to GPC’s 6-second AGC signals; and
             B. Charging from the GPC Electric System or the Renewable Resource in response to GPC’s AGC signals.
          3.2     For a Facility that includes a Renewable Resource, GPC prefers that the Renewable Resource be AC
          coupled to the BESS. GPC reserves the right to modify the performance metrics for the proposed Facility if Bidder
          proposes a Facility that is DC coupled. Seller’s Annual Capacity Payment represents all compensation owed to
          Seller for all Facility capacity delivered during the Annual Period.

          PART 4     CAPACITY AND DISPATCH REQUIREMENTS FOR PPA BIDS
          4.1    Over the PPA Term, the BESS must:
             A. Discharge at the guaranteed Storage Device Design Capacity (SDDC) at the guaranteed Storage Device
             Discharge Duration, which must be at least four hours;
             B. Be on AGC and available for charging or dispatch on a 24-hour daily basis except during pre-approved
             scheduled maintenance outages; and
             C. Be capable of at least 365 Cycles per Annual Period, and Cycles will be limited to a maximum of two Cycles
             in any Day.
          4.2     GPC will evaluate the guaranteed Storage Device Design Capacity (SDDC) based on the BESS’s charging
          ability and ability to continuously discharge to the POI for the Storage Device Discharge Duration each Day over
          the PPA Term. GPC is not responsible for any degradation of the BESS over the PPA Term, and either Party may
          request a performance test to demonstrate the performance capability of the BESS.
          4.3   The maximum delivered energy from the BESS or the Renewable Resource, separately or combined, to
          the POI, at one time, may not exceed the Interconnection Limit.
          4.4    There will be a tolling arrangement for grid charging. GPC will provide all grid energy, excluding Station
          Service, required for grid charging a Standalone BESS or a BESS with Renewable Resource in accordance with
          the applicable pro forma PPA. There will be no cost to GPC for tolled grid energy. Seller must separately procure
          any energy needed for Station Service, including, if required, a metered retail service connection to GPC or another
          provider.

          PART 5     STORAGE PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS
          5.1    GPC will evaluate BESS performance monthly based on two components:
             A. Energy Storage Performance Metric. This metric will compare the actual daily availability of the BESS to
             store energy, including both grid energy and Renewable Energy, in an amount equivalent to the guaranteed
             Storage Device Operating Energy. See the pro forma PPA for details.
             B. Charge/Discharge Rate Performance Metric. This metric will compare the daily composite charge or
             discharge rate of the BESS to the guaranteed BESS charge rate or the guaranteed Storage Device Design
             Capacity. See the pro forma PPA for additional details.
          5.2   These two metrics will be averaged to produce the “Monthly Storage Performance Metric.” See the pro
          forma PPA for additional details.

          PART 6     ROUNDTRIP EFFICIENCY PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENT
          6.1   The Round-Trip Efficiency Performance Metric will be determined by comparing actual Monthly RTE to the
          guaranteed RTE.
          6.2    Each PPA Bidder must include in its Bid a guaranteed RTE of the BESS. Actual installed RTE will be
          confirmed by third party-certified testing before Commercial Operation to confirm actual RTE is greater than the
          guaranteed RTE (e.g., if the guaranteed RTE is 86%, the actual RTE must be 86% or greater).
          6.3    GPC will track actual achieved RTE monthly for all stored energy. This RTE will be calculated by dividing
          stored energy for the month delivered to the POI by the energy input into the BESS.
          6.4    If, for a month, the measured RTE for stored energy that reaches the POI is below the guaranteed RTE by


          WINTER 27_28 BESS RFP                                                                                 Page 77 of 89

                                                        www.gonitro.com

STF-JKA-1-24 Attachment F.pdf

                                                                                               Winter 27_28 BESS RFP
                                                                                                        RFP Document
                                                                                                        Final Approved
          more than one percentage point (e.g., the measured RTE of 84% for a Facility with an 86% guaranteed RTE would
          have a measured RTE that is two percentage points below the guaranteed RTE), GPC will calculate a “Monthly
          RTE Adjustment” from: (i) the stored energy; (ii) the percent that actual Monthly RTE is below the guaranteed
          RTE; (iii) and GPC’s Associated Interchange Energy Rate (AIER).
          6.5   The Monthly RTE Adjustment will be subtracted from the Monthly Capacity Payment after the Storage
          Performance Reduction is applied.
          6.6    The Monthly RTE Adjustment will be calculated using GPC system incremental cost (i.e., AIER) for the
          stored energy lost due to the measured RTE being below the guaranteed RTE by more than one percentage point.

          PART 7     PPA PAYMENTS FOR BESS CAPACITY
          7.1     For each PPA Annual Period, GPC will pay to Seller a fixed “Annual Capacity Price,” which will be stated
          in the PPA. The Annual Capacity Price will be: (i) all compensation owed by GPC to Seller under the PPA; and (ii)
          subject to reduction for Seller failure to achieve performance guarantees, as will be described in the applicable pro
          forma PPA. The Annual Capacity Price will be prorated by application of Monthly Value Factors and paid monthly
          (“Monthly Capacity Payment”), as may be reduced in accordance with the PPA.
          7.2     As applicable, GPC will reduce the payment to Seller by subtracting from the Monthly Capacity Payment:
          (i) the Storage Performance Reduction; and (ii) the RTE Performance Adjustment.

                       EXHIBIT M – ENVIRONMENTAL SITE ASSESSMENT REQUIREMENTS

          PART 1 ALL BIDS.
          From an environmental perspective, and in GPC’s view, the best property for siting generation is property
          that has been comprehensively evaluated and determined to either have no past or present environmental
          concerns, or if concerns are identified, they can be avoided through generation technology or Site
          configuration. Where environmental impacts are possible, it is necessary to fully address impacts through
          avoidance, minimization, regulatory permitting, and compliance, and, possibly, mitigation.

          Each Bid will consider and address, at a minimum, the items outlined below. If Bidder does not believe an
          item is applicable to its Project, Bidder must provide a statement as to why.

                1. Waters of the U.S.
                2. State waters (where applicable)
                3. 100-Year Floodplains
                4. NPDES Construction Stormwater Permitting
                5. Federal and State Protected Species and Species of Special Concern
                6. Cultural Resources (Archaeology and Historical Architecture)
                7. Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasures (SPCC) Compliance
                8. Any contamination or potentially contaminated soil or groundwater (A Phase I Environmental Site
                   Assessment may be required)
                9. Air Quality requirements (including construction and development related considerations, e.g.,
                   permitting of timber/other open burning, as well as air pre-construction and operating permit
                   requirements, etc.)
                10. Local government permitting, ordinances, and restrictions
          With each Bid submittal, Bidder must provide a notarized Environmental Compliance Affidavit found in
          Exhibit N (Environmental Compliance Affidavit).

          PART 2 ENVIRONMENTAL ASSURANCES DUE AFTER BID ADVANCES TO COMPETITIVE TIER
          GPC requires assurances from each Bidder that due diligence concerning the protection of project-related
          environmental factors has been conducted and will continue to be observed throughout the PPA Term or
          until completion of Seller’s obligations under a BTA, as applicable. Efforts must be made by Bidder to avoid
          environmental impacts, but where impacts are unavoidable, efforts must be made by Bidder to minimize
          and mitigate environmental impacts accordingly. Therefore, Bidder is required at a minimum to address the
          above factors with its Bid to allow GPC to independently assess what potential environmental impacts may
          result from construction and operation of the Facility. Bidder must submit Environmental Assurances after
          its Bid advances to the Competitive Tier. Failure to address the items below will result in an incomplete Bid
          and possibility of rejection.
